Nuclear Theory.title: Short-range correlated pair formation and nuclear shell structure
Nuclear Theory.summary: Short-range correlated (SRC) nucleon pairs, caused by brief, high-momentum interactions between two nucleons, are dominated by neutron-proton pairs with large relative and smaller center-of-mass momenta. However, which nucleons form pairs is not fully understood. Measurements of 40,48Ca and 54Fe showed that intra-shell pairing was much stronger than inter-shell pairing. We measured high- missing-momentum protons knocked out in electron scattering from selected nuclei with a range of shell configurations, A, and N/Z, including 9Be, 10,11B, 12C, 40,48Ca, 54Fe, and 197Au, focusing on the four light nuclei. Unexpectedly, we found that adding one proton to 9Be (to make 10B) increased the number of correlated protons far more than adding one neutron to 10B or adding one proton to 11B, perhaps due to the large spin (J = 3) of 10B or the unusual structure of 9Be. In addition, the increase in pairing probability from 9Be to 12C and from 40Ca to 54Fe was much steeper than the increase from 9Be to 197Au. This shows the importance of low-momentum nuclear structure on the probability of high-momentum nucleon pairing.

Nuclear Theory.title: The Effect of Mass Loss and Convective Overshooting on the Pre-Collapse Structure, Composition, and Neutrino Emission of Red Supergiants
Nuclear Theory.summary: Prior to core collapse, the neutrino emission from red supergiants (RSGs) is so large that a nearby ($\lesssim1\:$kpc) RSG will become visible in current and near-future neutrino detectors. The rate of emission and the spectra of the pre-supernova (pre-SN) neutrinos from RSGs are sensitive to the temperature, density, and detailed isotopic composition of the core. During the last year of the star's life, these properties change considerably as the nuclear burning accelerates and deleptonization begins. Uncertainties in stellar evolution modeling - including the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting - alter the thermal conditions and composition of the RSG core as it approaches collapse, and thus one expects a consequent effect upon the pre-SN emission. In this paper we present the first study of how varying the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting together affects the pre-collapse core properties and neutrino emission of RSGs. We use the stellar evolution instrument MESA and construct a grid of 32 RSG models with zero-age main sequence masses of $\{ 12, 15, 18, 20\}$ M$_\odot$, apply the so-called "Dutch" mass-loss scheme with wind efficiencies of $\{0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0\}$, and consider two convective overshooting schemes. Our models use a large 206-isotope nuclear network in order to accurately compute the structure and composition of the star. We find that varying the treatment of mass loss and overshooting results in significant differences in core properties and the strength and timing of shell burning episodes, and that the onset of silicon shell burning leads to a localized peak in the pre-SN neutrino event rate observed by a JUNO-like detector $\sim 10$ hours to $\sim 1$ hour prior to collapse.

Nuclear Theory.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
Nuclear Theory.summary: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. We point out a distinct coherent channel when the baryonic component that stores the condensate is superfluid: an effective beta-conversion event between a neutron condensate and normal protons can proceed as an Andreev process, converting a particle-like excitation into a hole-like excitation while adding or removing a Cooper pair from the condensate. The resulting Andreev contribution to beta equilibration is fourth order in the effective conversion vertex, is enhanced by anomalous neutron Green's functions, and is not captured by standard Urca process. We identify the density, temperature, and oscillation-frequency regimes where this channel can dominate viscous damping of neutron-star oscillations and mergers.

Nuclear Theory.title: Charged-current neutrino opacity within the relativistic Hartree-Fock framework for astrophysical simulations of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers
Nuclear Theory.summary: Neutrinos and their weak interactions play a vital role in the physics of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers. Their description within astrophysical simulations, including the weak rates, is of pivotal importance not only for the prediction of accurate neutrino fluxes and spectra, including the associated conditions relevant to nucleosynthesis, neutrinos are also responsible for heating and cooling of the stellar plasma as well as the transport of lepton number and entropy. In the present article, we develop an essential improvement of the description of the underlying nuclear medium, necessary for the calculations of charged-current weak rates, with the inclusion of explicitly momentum-dependent nuclear interactions. To this end, we introduce the relativistic Hartree-Fock (RHF) approach and the associated momentum-dependent nucleon self-energies. We discuss the resulting neutrino and antineutrino opacities and find large discrepancies comparing the weak rates at the RHF level with those of commonly used relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. In particular, we observe a substantial shift of previously reported large medium-dependent modifications associated with the RMF approach.

Nuclear Theory.title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
Nuclear Theory.summary: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.

Nuclear Theory.title: Effects of kinematic cuts on $v_0(p_T)$
Nuclear Theory.summary: We show that the analysis of $v_0(p_T)$ is biased when low-$p_T$ particles are not detected. The low-$p_T$ threshold shifts $v_0(p_T)$ by a constant negative value, which depends on the threshold. We evaluate the shift using hydrodynamic simulations. Correcting for this bias significantly improves agreement between ALICE and ATLAS results for $v_0(p_T)$ in Pb+Pb collisions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
Nuclear Theory.summary: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.

Nuclear Theory.title: Constraints from big bang nucleosynthesis and cosmological observations on varying Higgs vacuum expectation value
Nuclear Theory.summary: The Higgs vacuum expectation value (VEV) alters both the electroweak and strong interaction rates. We study both effects on big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) and seek concordance between observed primordial abundances of light elements and cosmological constraints from CMB fluctuations and anisotropies. We find a strong negative correlation between primordial 4He abundance and the Higgs VEV. Consequently, using a 1.58% uplift of the Higgs VEV during BBN from the current value, an agreement can be achieved among the new primordial 4He abundance, observed by the EMPRESS group, Deuterium abundance determined from absorption lines in the Lyman-alpha forest along the line-of-sight of high-redshift quasars, and the lithium abundance on the Spite plateau. This agreement requires a baryon-to-photon ratio different from the CMB determination, indicating the need for nonstandard cosmological evolution between BBN and recombination epochs. We also demonstrate that a 0.2% uplift in the Higgs VEV can partially alleviate the "cosmic Li problem," keeping consistency with the CMB with remaining discrepancy potentially accounted for by stellar depletion mechanisms.

Nuclear Theory.title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_π\approx 200$ MeV and $M_π\approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1σ$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

Nuclear Theory.title: A general decay form and absolute nuclear stability
Nuclear Theory.summary: A nucleus is conventionally called stable when no decay has been observed. We replace this phenomenological definition with a criterion based on conservation laws. For this purpose, we formulate a general decay form (GDF) for finite charge-neutral nuclear systems that includes all possible final configurations. A nucleus is absolutely stable if no allowed configuration has lower mass. A global search over all nuclei with measured atomic masses yields 84 absolutely stable nuclei.Besides the criterion of absolute stability, we introduce a dimensionless decay-accessibility entropy SGDF as a coarse-grained measure of the relative accessibility of GDF-allowed decay channels. We rank all naturally occurring isotopes according to their maximum SGDF values, identify their favored decay modes, and estimate the corresponding partial half-lives. We further identify promising candidates for natural alpha and two-neutrino double-beta decays. The resulting framework also provides a nuclear-scale perspective on the far-future evolution of matter, in which nuclear decay drives matter toward combinations of these 84 absolutely stable nuclei before still slower processes of matter evolution. These findings extend the conventional phenomenological stable-radioactive classification to a conservation-law-based framework for nuclear stability and provide a systematic guide for future rare-decay searches.

Nuclear Theory.title: Isovector Monopole Resonance
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present a theoretical study of the three isospin channels of the isovector giant monopole resonance (IVGMR) within self-consistent Skyrme Hartree-Fock plus Random-Phase Approximation. A modified charge-exchange monopole operator is introduced to remove the dominant isobaric-analog-state contribution, thereby isolating the genuine radial isovector response. We derive the associated non-energy- and energy-weighted sum rules and establish approximate relations between the charge-exchange and non-charge-exchange strengths. The relative locations of the three IVGMR centroids are interpreted in terms of Coulomb displacement energies, the neutron-proton mass difference, and the finite-nucleus symmetry potential. Calculations for \(^{48}\)Ca, \(^{90}\)Zr, and \(^{208}\)Pb show that the non-charge-exchange centroid is accurately approximated by the average of the two charge-exchange centroids in medium-heavy and heavy nuclei. Using a broad set of Skyrme energy-density functionals, we find that the centroid energies of the three channels display a weak model dependence for a fixed nucleus, whereas the non-charge-exchange monopole polarizability exhibits a clear sensitivity to the density dependence of the symmetry energy. These results clarify the isospin structure of the IVGMR and support its use as a complementary probe of isovector nuclear properties.

Nuclear Theory.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
Nuclear Theory.summary: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=κ_Qσ_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $κ_Q$ and $σ_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.

Nuclear Theory.title: $NΛ$ interaction from a quark model: $pΛ$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton
Nuclear Theory.summary: Understanding the low-energy nucleon--$Λ$ interaction is essential for describing hypernuclear structures, while its spin dependence remains insufficiently constrained by experimental data. In this work, we investigate the $NΛ$ interaction using the quark delocalization color screening model and explore its implications for $pΛ$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton. The energy and scattering phase shifts of the $NΛ$ system are calculated, revealing weak attraction in both the $J^P=0^+$ and $1^+$ channels, but no bound states. The corresponding scattering lengths and effective ranges are found to be $-2.36$ fm and $1.61$ fm for $J^P=0^+$, and $-0.95$ fm and $1.46$ fm for $J^P=1^+$, respectively. Using the Gel'fand--Levitan--Marchenko inverse-scattering method, effective $NΛ$ potentials are reconstructed from the coupled-channel scattering phase shifts and applied to calculate the $pΛ$ femtoscopic correlation function. Comparison with experimental data suggests that the spin-triplet attraction may be underestimated in the present model. Furthermore, employing the Gaussian Expansion Method, we investigate the $NNΛ$ three-body system and obtain a weakly bound hypertriton with a $Λ$ separation energy of $1.06$--$1.16$ MeV. These results demonstrate that $pΛ$ femtoscopic correlations and hypertriton binding provide complementary probes of the spin-dependent $NΛ$ interaction, offering valuable constraints on its low-energy behavior.

Nuclear Theory.title: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
Nuclear Theory.summary: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $μ_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $μ=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.

Nuclear Theory.title: Longitudinal $Λ$ polarization as a competition between freeze-out geometry and elliptic flow in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36\,\mathrm{TeV}$
Nuclear Theory.summary: The second sine harmonic $\Pz$ of longitudinal $Λ$ polarization is sensitive to the balance between the kinematic-vorticity contribution $\Pz^ω$ and the kinematic-shear contribution $\Pz^Ξ$ at decoupling. We quantify this competition in a scan of 48 Pb-Pb initial states evolved with the (3+1)-dimensional Particle-In-Cell Relativistic (PICR) ideal-hydrodynamic code. With the isothermal local-equilibrium (ILE) prescription, the total harmonic follows $\Pz\simeq a\,\efo-b\,v_2$, with $a\simeq0.010$ and $b\simeq0.014$, where $\efo$ is the freeze-out eccentricity and $v_2$ the elliptic flow of $Λ$ hyperons. With coefficients fixed on these 48 states, the relation describes 86\% of the variation of $\Pz$ in 12 states outside the fit. To identify the origin of the two terms, we decompose the ILE integrand exactly into an emission-gradient term and a curl term. On the PICR decoupling surfaces, the tangential emission gradient is positive on average, correlates most strongly with $\efo$, and admits a surface-curvature representation, whereas the normal emission gradient and the curl term are negative on average and correlate most strongly with $v_2$. A blast-wave calculation with the same integrand gives coefficients of comparable magnitude and shows how the cancellation point $\efo/v_2=b/a$ changes with the flow and the surface geometry; both PICR and blast-wave calculations predict that $b/a$ rises with hadron mass from the proton to the $Ω$ when the decoupling surface is held fixed. Although the geometry inferred from ALICE data depends on the background, the measured polarization constrains the displacement of $\efo$ from the cancellation boundary $\efo=(b/a)v_2$. For the central ALICE measurement values at $5.36\,\mathrm{TeV}$, the backgrounds examined give $\efo\simeq0.2$--$0.4$ in 30--50\% Pb-Pb collisions.

Nuclear Theory.title: Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present the first calculation of single inclusive hadron and jet production at large transverse momentum in lepton-hadron scattering in a joint QCD+QED factorization approach. The scattering cross section is factorized into a convolution of infrared-safe hard coefficient functions with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs) and parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the colliding lepton and hadron, respectively, together with fragmentation functions (FFs) of the observed hadron (or jet). With joint QCD+QED factorization, the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) type evolution equations for LDFs, PDFs, and FFs necessarily have evolution kernels calculated in both QCD and QED. We derive a default set of LDFs for our calculations and discuss a strategy to extract universal, non-perturbative LDFs from future data. We present our calculations for single inclusive hadron and/or jet production at the energies of Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider.

Nuclear Theory.title: A New Bayesian Framework with Mass-Radius-Space Priors to Constrain the Neutron Star Equation of State
Nuclear Theory.summary: We propose a new Bayesian framework to infer the neutron star equation of state (EOS) from mass and radius observations and neutron matter theory by defining priors that directly parameterize mass-radius space instead of pressure-energy density space. We use direct and accurate inversion approximations to map mass-radius relations to the underlying EOS. We systematically compare its EOS inferences with those inferred from traditional EOS parameterizations, taking care to quantify the systematic prior uncertainties of both. Our results show that prior uncertainties should be included in all Bayesian approaches. The alternative framework provides broader and more uniform coverage of the physically allowed mass-radius space, especially small radius configurations, with enhanced computational efficiency. Substantially reduced dependence on prior choices seems to result from having both prior and posterior distributions in the same observational mass-radius space. Results indicate that direct parameterization in observed space offers a robust and efficient alternative to traditional methods.

Nuclear Theory.title: Electric Flux as a Criterion for String Breaking and Schwinger Pair Production
Nuclear Theory.summary: We define string breaking by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit. In the massive Schwinger model, an energy balance between intact string and screened configuration predicts this separation using only vacuum observables and meson masses as input. We observe numerically that this half flux point corresponds to equal weights of the two configurations thus explaining the observed peak of the entanglement entropy as maximal uncertainty of the binary flux. The same binary uncertainty explains the entanglement peak at the vacuum transition. Near breaking, screening organizes part of the spatial entanglement between the string interior and exterior into a nearly maximally entangled bit. Within the selected flux sectors, this approximate encoded Bell pair records whether the flux is screened and nearly separates from the remaining correlations. The vacuum transition exhibits the same structure. The string and the $θ$-vacuum reveal a matching structure of the capacity of entanglement minimum at their transition point, linking their entanglement spectra. The transition rearranges degrees of freedom coherently as revealed by the entanglement asymmetry and Robustness of Magic of disjoint subregions. Finally, we construct the $θ$-vacuum and string wavefunctions with high fidelity using a restricted Boltzmann machine ansatz.

Nuclear Theory.title: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei
Nuclear Theory.summary: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei is investigated. In our analysis the central atomic nucleus is assumed to be an infinitely heavy, positively charged and point `particle' with the electric charge $Q e$. The explicit formulas for the both annihilation cross section and one-photon annihilation rate $Γ^{(b)}_{1 γ}$ are derived and discussed. We also derive and discuss the closed formula which describes the angular distribution of the emitted photons. All our formulas can directly be used to evaluate probabilities of the actual one-photon annihilation in various atoms, ions and light molecular ions which also contain one (or two) positron(s).

Nuclear Theory.title: Trapped-ion quantum simulation of (1+1)D SU(2) lattice gauge theory via loop-string-hadron formulation
Nuclear Theory.summary: We present a quantum simulation of the SU(2) lattice gauge theory in 1+1 dimensions with one flavor of fermions, performed using the trapped-ion Quantinuum System Model H2. This work is based on the loop-string-hadron (LSH) formulation of the gauge theory, and is distinguished by using qubits to represent both bosonic-gauge and fermionic-matter degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we access the $j=1$ electric-flux sector beyond the $j_{\max}=1/2$ truncation commonly used in SU(2) quantum simulations. To that end, we digitize an electric-field degree of freedom using a multiqubit register for representing the bosonic quantum number. Our simulation therefore synthesizes several key ingredients relevant to quantum simulations in higher spatial dimensions, in particular explicit local gauge-field degrees of freedom represented here by a multiqubit bosonic register, while relying solely on circuit-construction optimizations that are expected to scale polynomially with lattice size. This work demonstrates that modern quantum hardware is increasingly able to accommodate the features of complicated but physically important lattice gauge theories while successfully reproducing the expected Trotterized dynamics.

Nuclear Experiment.title: Unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry in nucleus-nucleus collisions at CERN SPS energies
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The NA61/SHINE experiment at the CERN SPS reports an unexpectedly large excess in the inclusive production of charged over neutral kaons in 0-10% central Ar+Sc collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=8.8$ and 11.9 GeV. This effect corresponds to an unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry, that cannot be explained by known mechanisms contained in the present theoretical models. The comparison of the NA61/SHINE results to data from other experiments reveals, within sizeable uncertainties, a consistent isospin symmetry-violating excess of charged kaon production in the energy regime $2.6<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<200$ GeV. At LHC energies ($0.9<\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}<13$ TeV) the charged-over-neutral kaon ratio appears consistent with unity, but the uncertainties remain sizeable. A similar excess of charged over neutral kaon yields is observed by NA61/SHINE in minimum bias $π^-$+C reactions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}}=17.3$ and 25.7 GeV, also in disagreement with model predictions. No clear theoretical explanation of these phenomena has been provided so far. An unexpectedly large violation of isospin symmetry brings potential heavy consequences for our understanding of particle production, and calls for a concentrated experimental and theoretical effort.
authors: Andrzej Rybicki for the NA61/SHINE Collaboration

Nuclear Experiment.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.

Nuclear Experiment.title: A New High-Intensity Source for Ultracold Neutrons
Nuclear Experiment.summary: The TRIUMF UltraCold Advanced Neutron (TUCAN) collaboration has completed a new superthermal source for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) at TRIUMF. Neutrons produced in a spallation target are moderated in heavy water and liquid deuterium, and are converted to ultracold neutrons by inelastic scattering inside superfluid $^4$He at around 1.1 K. During commissioning of the completed moderation and conversion system, including the liquid-deuterium moderator, up to $1.47(2)\times 10^7$ UCNs were detected outside the source in the experimental area following a 60 s accumulation period. At the same location, continuous operation produced detector rates of up to $6.75(3)\times 10^7$ UCN/s, and a density of 165.6(1) UCN/cm$^3$ was achieved in a 25.4 L external vessel. These measurements demonstrate high-intensity operation of a spallation-driven He-II UCN source, including extraction and transport to an external experimental area.

Nuclear Experiment.title: Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering
Nuclear Experiment.summary: We present the first calculation of single inclusive hadron and jet production at large transverse momentum in lepton-hadron scattering in a joint QCD+QED factorization approach. The scattering cross section is factorized into a convolution of infrared-safe hard coefficient functions with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs) and parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the colliding lepton and hadron, respectively, together with fragmentation functions (FFs) of the observed hadron (or jet). With joint QCD+QED factorization, the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) type evolution equations for LDFs, PDFs, and FFs necessarily have evolution kernels calculated in both QCD and QED. We derive a default set of LDFs for our calculations and discuss a strategy to extract universal, non-perturbative LDFs from future data. We present our calculations for single inclusive hadron and/or jet production at the energies of Jefferson Lab and the future Electron-Ion Collider.
Nuclear Experiment.comment: 41 pages, 26 figures. v2: version accepted for publication in PTEP. v3: fixed Eqs (21) and (A5), replaced Fig 3

Nuclear Experiment.title: Rossi-alpha Benchmark Validation of a Static Alpha Eigenvalue Capability in OpenMC
Nuclear Experiment.summary: A static alpha eigenvalue capability was implemented in a modified version of the open-source Monte Carlo radiation transport code OpenMC and validated against Rossi-alpha measurements from 21 delayed-critical benchmark experiments and 33 subcritical configurations spanning fast, intermediate, and thermal systems with U-233, HEU, IEU, LEU, and plutonium fuels. The effective delayed neutron fraction was calculated using the k-prompt method, and the prompt neutron lifetime was calculated using the iterated fission probability method, both evaluated within the standard k-eigenvalue power iteration. The delayed-critical alpha eigenvalue was calculated from these quantities using the point kinetics equation alpha_dc = -beta_eff / ell_p. Agreement was generally within 10% for fast metal systems and within 5% for thermal solution systems. Subcritical extrapolation studies derived from the SHE-8 and STACY benchmark families show that alpha_dc remains stable as the system is driven subcritical.

Nuclear Experiment.title: BeAGLE++: A modern modular framework for eA physics at the EIC
Nuclear Experiment.summary: We present the Benchmark eA Generator for LEptoproduction (BeAGLE++), a next-generation, general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator for high-energy lepton-nucleus collisions and the successor to BeAGLE. The framework incorporates a formation-zone intranuclear cascade to describe hadronic final-state interactions (FSIs), followed by statistical de-excitation of the residual nucleus. Compared with the legacy implementation, the BeAGLE++ cascade introduces a discrete time-ordered treatment of hadronic interactions and light-cluster production during intranuclear transport. Comparisons with E665 measurements and legacy BeAGLE calculations show broad agreement for selected observables, while revealing differences in final states sensitive to FSIs. These differences provide opportunities to assess the model dependence of nuclear-breakup predictions and constrain the underlying cascade dynamics. With its modular architecture, BeAGLE++ provides a flexible simulation framework for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) and a platform for developing and testing new physics models against existing data and future EIC measurements.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. A component correlated with a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) annihilation template remains with finer spatial binning and the instrumental response included. Outside the Fermi bubbles footprint, it is detected at nominal significances of about 4-16$σ$ over 5.6-130 GeV, falling to 1-7$σ$ when the enlarged boundaries of a recent substructured bubbles model are also excluded. With the substructured model, which improves the fit substantially, the component remains at 7-18$σ$ in four of six representative foreground configurations. However, its amplitude and spectrum depend strongly on the foreground model, and no tested foreground yields a single NFW normalization across the sky, including with additional spatial freedom in the eROSITA bubbles. Simulations show that foreground mismodeling can produce spurious NFW-correlated emission of the observed amplitude, and that residual-derived bubbles templates can bias the recovered spectrum. The 420 GeV $W^+W^-$ spectrum motivated by the LZ connection describes the data for some foreground models but is disfavored by others. These results disfavor interpreting the full excess as annihilation in a smooth NFW halo and weaken the case for a common origin with the LZ event, but they do not exclude a dark matter contribution to the persistent halo-like residual. [abridged]
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 14 tables. Code: https://github.com/kabazajian/totani (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23420779); data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23420896

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Graded transcendental functions: an application to four-point amplitudes with one off-shell leg
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Several recent works have demonstrated the powerful algebraic simplifications that can be achieved for scattering amplitudes through a systematic grading of transcendental quantities. We develop these concepts to construct a minimal basis of functions tailored to a scattering amplitude in a general way. Starting with formal solutions for all master integral topologies, we organise the appearing functions by properties such as their symbol alphabet or letter adjacency. We rotate the basis such that functions with spurious features appear in the least possible number of basis elements. Since their coefficients must vanish for physical quantities, this approach avoids complex cancellations. As a first application, we evaluate all integral topologies relevant to the three-loop $Hggg$ and $Hgq\bar{q}$ amplitudes in the leading-colour approximation and heavy-top limit. We describe the derivation of canonical differential equation systems and present a method for fixing boundary conditions without the need for a full functional representation. Using multiple numerical reductions, we test the maximal transcendentality conjecture for $Hggg$ and identify a new letter which appears in functions of weight 4 and 5. In addition, we provide the first direct analytic computation of a three-point form factor of the operator $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^2)$ in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ sYM and find agreement with numerical and bootstrapped results.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Impact of Irrep Truncations on Quantum Simulations of QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories with continuous gauge groups require a choice of basis (how states of the gauge theory map to the qubit computational basis) and truncation scheme (which of the infinitely many gauge theory basis states should be omitted in the map to the finite dimensional qubit Hilbert space.) The most common choices are adapted to an electric basis for the gauge theory, where the basis states for each link are associated with irreducible representations of the gauge group. Electric bases and truncations are generally advantageous for preserving gauge symmetries and simulating the strong coupling regime, but their effectiveness in the weak coupling regimes of physical interest are less well understood. In this work, we compute relative probabilities $p(R')/p(R)$ for finding a link in the irreps $R,R'$ in the ground state of SU(3) lattice gauge theory using Euclidean Monte Carlo methods and weak-coupling lattice perturbation theory. The observables that compute these relative probabilities are constructed by introducing seams into an anisotropic lattice, and by a similar construction we are also able to measure relative probabilities of different site singlets (ways that electric flux braids together into a gauge singlet) at each vertex. With these methods we can quantify, for example, the importance of higher electric flux states in the weak coupling ground state. These results directly inform what truncations are needed to accurately capture non-abelian gauge dynamics near the continuum limit.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Complete $g^6$ pressure of hot Yang-Mills theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the full order $g^6$ term in the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of hot $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory, resolving a problem that has remained open for more than two decades. To achieve this, we evaluate nine previously unknown nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals using the thermal loop-tree duality method with novel local ultraviolet and infrared subtractions, thereby completing the hard-scale contribution to the pressure for general $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$. Combining this result with known chromoelectric and chromomagnetic contributions, available for $N_c=3$, we demonstrate the analytic cancellation of infrared divergences originating from different momentum scales and obtain the complete $O(g^6)$ pressure for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$. Our result displays quantitative agreement with data from four-dimensional lattice simulations over a broad range of temperatures, providing a stringent test of the dimensionally reduced effective-field-theory paradigm.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, perturbatively
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We determine the four-loop hard-scale matching correction to the pressure of the gluon plasma at high temperature. This result completes the long-standing calculation through $\mathcal{O}(g_s^6)$, where $g_s$ is the strong coupling. Our result agrees, within uncertainties, with the value obtained in arXiv:1204.6184 by fitting the perturbative series to continuum-extrapolated lattice data, thereby providing the first direct test of the weak-coupling expansion at this order.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Equiprobability Anomaly Detector Using Angular Distributions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We use the angular distribution of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in the semileptonic final state $b\bar{b}\,\ellνq\bar{q}'$ to construct an anomaly detector for non-$t\bar{t}$ events. Wigner $D$ functions expand the distribution with coefficients determined by orthogonal series density estimation. Its equiprobable surfaces bin the events, the non-$t\bar{t}$ concentrate at low $t\bar{t}$ density. The separation is quantified by the Kullback-Leibler divergence, which makes connection to variational autoencoders. The performance is comparable to normalizing flows at parton level, but is limited by jet assignments at reconstruction level.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Mass, forces, and the dark sector in a Kaluza-Klein model with 6 compact dimensions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: (1) Objective: This study seeks to calculate the meson and baryon masses and to investigate the dynamics within hadrons and lepton pairs by formulating a unified physical framework that, in addition to gravitation, simultaneously incorporates the strong, electromagnetic and weak interactions. (2) Method: A framework inspired by the Standard Model and based on Kaluza-Klein theory is formulated using an extended general-relativistic description in a spacetime of one temporal, three spatial, and six compactified dimensions. The model suggests that excitations, deformations of the 10-dimensional spacetime traveling at light-speed, contribute to mass and distinct spin characteristics in a 4-dimensional setting. Using the electron g-factor, charged-lepton masses, and masses of the proton, neutron, and neutral and charged pion, neutral and charged rho, phi, psi, upsilon mesons, the parameters compactification radius rho, weak interaction coupling alpha_w, strong interaction coupling alpha_s, flavor constants A_i and the antineutrino/neutrino density ratio delta3 are determined and used to compute the masses of the hadrons. (3) Key results: Masses of 102 hadrons are obtained; comparison with data from 71 measurements shows relative errors below 0.05 in 70%, below 0.1 in 89% and below 0.2 in 100%, with a correlation coefficient r=0.997 between the measured and calculated masses. Thirty-one additional hadron masses are predicted, and the model identifies asymmetries in electric and weak forces, as well as distance- and velocity-dependent interactions. (4) Implications: The framework offers testable predictions for hadron spectroscopy, predicts sterile, exclusive gravitationally interacting bosons as dark-matter candidates, states the equations for the elementary forces, and suggests possible connections between force asymmetries and dark energy.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The Effect of Mass Loss and Convective Overshooting on the Pre-Collapse Structure, Composition, and Neutrino Emission of Red Supergiants
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Prior to core collapse, the neutrino emission from red supergiants (RSGs) is so large that a nearby ($\lesssim1\:$kpc) RSG will become visible in current and near-future neutrino detectors. The rate of emission and the spectra of the pre-supernova (pre-SN) neutrinos from RSGs are sensitive to the temperature, density, and detailed isotopic composition of the core. During the last year of the star's life, these properties change considerably as the nuclear burning accelerates and deleptonization begins. Uncertainties in stellar evolution modeling - including the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting - alter the thermal conditions and composition of the RSG core as it approaches collapse, and thus one expects a consequent effect upon the pre-SN emission. In this paper we present the first study of how varying the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting together affects the pre-collapse core properties and neutrino emission of RSGs. We use the stellar evolution instrument MESA and construct a grid of 32 RSG models with zero-age main sequence masses of $\{ 12, 15, 18, 20\}$ M$_\odot$, apply the so-called "Dutch" mass-loss scheme with wind efficiencies of $\{0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0\}$, and consider two convective overshooting schemes. Our models use a large 206-isotope nuclear network in order to accurately compute the structure and composition of the star. We find that varying the treatment of mass loss and overshooting results in significant differences in core properties and the strength and timing of shell burning episodes, and that the onset of silicon shell burning leads to a localized peak in the pre-SN neutrino event rate observed by a JUNO-like detector $\sim 10$ hours to $\sim 1$ hour prior to collapse.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. 23 pages, 14 figures

High Energy Phenomenology.title: AgentRivet: an automated system for producing Rivet routines from journal publications
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Particle physics collider experiments provide Rivet routines as part of the analysis preservation strategy for model-independent measurements. Rivet is a C++ toolkit that allow new theoretical models to be compared to the measurements, thus aiding the development and tuning of Monte Carlo event generators as well as searches for physics beyond the Standard Model. However, analysis coverage is known to be incomplete, with only 39% of measurements having documented and publicly available Rivet routines. In this article, we design and implement an automated workflow based on Large Language Models with the goal of providing the missing routines. This multi-step workflow, referred to as AgentRivet, extracts the physics analysis information from published papers and writes the missing Rivet routines, with intermediate code- and physics- reviews as part of an autonomous quality control. We report the results obtained using commercial Large Language Models, provided by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, for two recent measurements from the ATLAS and CMS experiments. We find that AgentRivet produces competent Rivet routines with few syntax errors. The physics fidelity of the routines is reasonable and follows the explanations given in the relevant publications. Nevertheless, physics-implementation issues do arise and are investigated using the artefacts produced by AgentRivet. The majority of physics implementation issues arise from subtle-but-ambiguous definitions in the given publication, although some models struggle to implement complex observables even when clear definitions are given.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Principle of no paradoxical Universe
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In the standard $Λ\rm CDM$ model, the Universe will keep expanding forever and its lifetime is infinite. Therefore, even the heaviest supermassive black hole will eventually evaporate and the universal occurrence of the black hole information paradox is unavoidable. However, the recent DESI results seem to indicate that dark energy is dynamical and, more importantly, it is possible that the Universe has a finite lifetime and will experience a ``Big Crunch" in some billion years from now. In light of this, the lightest confirmed black hole with mass of order one solar mass may not have a chance to evaporate before the Universe ends. Inspired by these observations, we thus raise an intriguing conjecture: Does the Universe choose a configuration such that the ``in-principle" black hole information paradox can never actually happen in reality? We derive a lower bound on black hole mass as a function of the Universe's lifetime such that the information paradox cannot be realized in nature and some resulting predictions are made. Some profound implications for other related big ideas in physics are briefly discussed.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron: parameter-free inflation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a model of slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity, where the connection is independent of the metric. We require that the Einstein-Hilbert term is the only operator that breaks three out of four shift-symmetries of the connection, and impose them on the metric-affine Starobinsky term $αR(Γ)^2$. This replaces it by $α\mathring{R}^2$, the square of the invariant part of the scalar curvature. The theory propagates only the graviton and one healthy scalar, the metric-affine $\mathring{R}^2$ scalaron. Its potential approaches a plateau polynomially, $U\simeq U_0(1-μ^2/χ^2)$, with $μ=\sqrt{6}\,M_P$ fixed by the curvature of the connection. Once $α\simeq2\times10^{8}$ is set by the scalar amplitude, the model has no free parameters. It predicts $n_s\simeq1-3/(2N_*)$ and $r\simeq2\sqrt3\,N_*^{-3/2}$ at leading order in $N_*$, and $n_s=0.968$--$0.974$ and $r=0.011$-$0.008$ with exact slow-roll for $N_*=50$-$60$ $e$-folds. These values agree with current data, and $r$ is within reach of the next generation of $B$-mode measurements.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Charged-current neutrino opacity within the relativistic Hartree-Fock framework for astrophysical simulations of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neutrinos and their weak interactions play a vital role in the physics of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers. Their description within astrophysical simulations, including the weak rates, is of pivotal importance not only for the prediction of accurate neutrino fluxes and spectra, including the associated conditions relevant to nucleosynthesis, neutrinos are also responsible for heating and cooling of the stellar plasma as well as the transport of lepton number and entropy. In the present article, we develop an essential improvement of the description of the underlying nuclear medium, necessary for the calculations of charged-current weak rates, with the inclusion of explicitly momentum-dependent nuclear interactions. To this end, we introduce the relativistic Hartree-Fock (RHF) approach and the associated momentum-dependent nucleon self-energies. We discuss the resulting neutrino and antineutrino opacities and find large discrepancies comparing the weak rates at the RHF level with those of commonly used relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. In particular, we observe a substantial shift of previously reported large medium-dependent modifications associated with the RMF approach.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Neutrino Anomalies and Tensions: Experimental Status and Theoretical Interpretations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neutrino oscillations successfully describe flavor conversion across a wide range of experiments, yet the origin of several excesses and deficits remains unresolved. This review connects these observations and long-baseline parameter tensions to their proposed physical explanations, clarifying what remains open and how it can be tested. We examine reactor and gallium measurements, accelerator appearance and disappearance searches, and atmospheric constraints, focusing on sterile neutrinos, non-standard interactions, and decoherence in open-system dynamics. For each mechanism, we assess what it modifies, which observations it can address, and which theoretical assumptions and independent constraints limit its viability. Recent results have restricted several interpretations and weakened some earlier tensions; no single extension provides an uncontested account of all observations. We identify the flavor, baseline, energy, and event-topology signatures needed to distinguish competing explanations and assess whether the remaining anomalies require new physics or reflect unresolved flux, interaction, and detector uncertainties.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 24 pages, 1 figure. Review article, submitted to MDPI Particles

High Energy Phenomenology.title: A New Look at the X Compositeness from its Lineshape
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Available data on the $X(3872)$ lineshape have been fitted with a Flattè parametrization derived from an effective Lagrangian in which $X$, $D$, and $D^*$ are all elementary fields. A molecular $X$, i.e., a deuteron-like bound state of $D$ and $\bar{D}^*$, must instead be described by an effective theory where the $X$ field is initially absent or introduced as an auxiliary, unphysical, field, yielding a lineshape parametrization that differs significantly from the Flattè one. We demonstrate, in the analogous theory of nucleons with an auxiliary deuteron field, that this parametrization gives a fully consistent description of $np\to\text{deuteron}\to np$ scattering data, and motivate applying the same method to the $X$ lineshape. The analysis proposed here is novel and has not previously been carried out on the available data.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 7 pages, 2 figure, to appear in Phys Rev D. Discussion enlarged, results unchanged

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics and non-perturbative renormalization of the shear viscosity of incompressible fluids
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose a regularization of stochastic fluid dynamics that preserves all relevant symmetries. By considering an incompressible fluid, we demonstrate explicitly that the regularized theory is UV finite, and therefore admits a continuum limit. Strikingly, the regularized theory of stochastic fluid dynamics is not only amenable to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory, but also to functional methods in the continuum. We exploit this to perform renormalization group improved perturbative calculations of the renormalization of the shear viscosity of an incompressible fluid in two and three spatial dimensions, and compare our results to direct numerical simulations of the lattice discretized theory.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Effects of kinematic cuts on $v_0(p_T)$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We show that the analysis of $v_0(p_T)$ is biased when low-$p_T$ particles are not detected. The low-$p_T$ threshold shifts $v_0(p_T)$ by a constant negative value, which depends on the threshold. We evaluate the shift using hydrodynamic simulations. Correcting for this bias significantly improves agreement between ALICE and ATLAS results for $v_0(p_T)$ in Pb+Pb collisions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Reference frame dependence of the periodically oscillating Coulomb field in the Proca theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The Proca theory of the real massive vector field admits non-equilibrium solutions, where the asymptotic dynamics of its electric field is dominated by the periodically oscillating Coulomb component. We discuss how such field configurations are seen in different reference frames, where we find an intriguing spatial pattern of the vector field of the Proca theory and the electromagnetic field associated with it.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Neural Network Representation of Generalized Parton Distributions (NNGPD)
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Extracting generalized parton distributions (GPDs) from experimental observables, the convolution structures denoted as Compton form factors (CFFs), requires solving an intrinsic inverse problem. We presented results using NNGPD, a flexible regression method based on a physics-informed neural-network framework, for reconstructing GPDs using integral constraints -- including CFFs and Mellin moments -- and symmetry and endpoint constraints. The approach does not require pointwise training information on the underlying GPDs. Closure tests using pseudodata generated from a phenomenological model demonstrate the ability of the framework to reproduce the principal features of the underlying distributions across a range of kinematics. A Bayesian neural-network formulation is also introduced to address uncertainties associated with the reconstruction. Finally, we discussed a broader question in GPD phenomenology: whether the complete momentum-fraction dependence of GPDs is necessary to extract physical quantities such as partonic angular momentum. This motivates investigating approaches that infer Mellin moments directly from experimentally constrained CFFs, while quantifying the remaining ambiguities.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, Proceedings of The 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4 - 8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Constraints from big bang nucleosynthesis and cosmological observations on varying Higgs vacuum expectation value
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The Higgs vacuum expectation value (VEV) alters both the electroweak and strong interaction rates. We study both effects on big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) and seek concordance between observed primordial abundances of light elements and cosmological constraints from CMB fluctuations and anisotropies. We find a strong negative correlation between primordial 4He abundance and the Higgs VEV. Consequently, using a 1.58% uplift of the Higgs VEV during BBN from the current value, an agreement can be achieved among the new primordial 4He abundance, observed by the EMPRESS group, Deuterium abundance determined from absorption lines in the Lyman-alpha forest along the line-of-sight of high-redshift quasars, and the lithium abundance on the Spite plateau. This agreement requires a baryon-to-photon ratio different from the CMB determination, indicating the need for nonstandard cosmological evolution between BBN and recombination epochs. We also demonstrate that a 0.2% uplift in the Higgs VEV can partially alleviate the "cosmic Li problem," keeping consistency with the CMB with remaining discrepancy potentially accounted for by stellar depletion mechanisms.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Spinors, Doppelgängers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelgänger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Correlated $b \to s$ and $s \to d$ Rare Semileptonic Transitions in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The persistent anomalies observed in $b \to s\,(\ell^+\ell^-,\,ν\barν)$ transitions continue to provide strong motivation for exploring possible extensions of the Standard Model (SM). Motivated by these discrepancies, we present a comprehensive analysis of semileptonic flavor changing neutral current processes within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), encompassing both $b \to s\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ and $s \to d\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ transitions. We perform a combined fit to $b \to s\,(μ^+μ^-,\,ν\barν)$ observables, allowing the relevant dimension-six Wilson coefficients to be complex. We find that the four-fermion operators involving left-handed quark and lepton doublets provide the preferred description of the current $b \to s$ data, while the electroweak operator modifying the $Z$-boson couplings also plays an important role in improving the fit. We show that flavor-universal SMEFT couplings lead to strongly enhanced rare semileptonic kaon decay branching ratios, in conflict with current experimental bounds and thus motivating the implementation of Minimal Flavor Violation. In particular, we demonstrate that flavor-symmetric frameworks based on $U(3)^5$ and $U(2)^5$ naturally restore the required CKM hierarchies and bring the predicted kaon observables into agreement with present data. We further analyze the differential distributions with respect to the dineutrino invariant mass squared $q^2$, as well as the reconstructed variable $q^2_{\mathrm{rec}}$, in $B \to K^{(*)}ν\barν$ decays, demonstrating their sensitivity to different new physics operators. In addition, we investigate the impact of complex Wilson coefficients on $\mathcal{CP}$ asymmetries in $B \to K^{(*)}μ^+μ^-$ decays and find that percent-level effects can arise in specific $q^2$ regions.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 32 pages, 2 figures, 13 Tables, references added, numerical results and text updated, to be submitted to a volume of "Journal of Physics G" honouring Ashutosh Kumar Alok

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_π\approx 200$ MeV and $M_π\approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1σ$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing Quantum Foundations in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations: Wave Packet Approach from MINOS Data to DUNE Predictions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the wave packet formalism, extending the standard planewave treatment to incorporate the finite spatial coherence of neutrino mass eigenstates.We derive the full three flavor oscillation probability with MSW matter effects, decoherence, and localization suppression governed by the wave packet width, benchmarking against MINOS disappearance data and extending to DUNE predictions under the same parameters. To quantify how sharply the oscillation data constrain the wave packet width, we compute the classical Fisher information FC as a function of neutrino energy for both MINOS and DUNE, and show that its sensitivity is concentrated precisely in the low-energy regime where the wave-packet and plane-wave predictions diverge. Beyond the oscillation probability analysis, we compute wave particle entanglement complementarity quantities within a quantum information theoretic framework and explore the complete triality description involving entanglement, predictability, and visibility as functions of neutrino energy for both experiments such as MINOS and DUNE. We show that even when the oscillation probability is numerically indistinguishable from the planewave result, the wave packet structure leaves observable imprints in these triality measures. Our results demonstrate that the wave packet approach provides a theoretically consistent and experimentally motivated framework for probing quantum foundations in long-baseline atmospheric neutrino oscillation experiments.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $ψ(3S)$ and $η_c(3S)$ production in the $B^+$ decay processes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In the present work, we investigate the production of psi(4040) in the B+ -> K+ psi(4040) process. Our estimations indicate that the unexpectedly large branching fraction could be well reproduced by taking both the short-range perturbative and long-range non-perturbative QCD contributions into account, where the long-range non-perturbative part plays an important role. Considering the structural similarity of eta_c(3S) and psi(3S), we apply the same model parameters to investigate the production of eta_c(3S) in the B+ decay process, and the branching fraction is predicted to be (0.81 +0.31 -0.29) x 10^-3. Based on the estimations in the present work and the relevant experimental measurements, we suggest that the experimentalists search for eta_c(3S) in the J/psi omega invariant mass distributions of B+ -> J/psi omega K+ process at Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $χ_{c1}(4010)$ as a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ Molecular State: Mass, Decay Constant, and Width
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The charmonium-like state $χ_{c1}(4010)$, recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration in $B^+ \to D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}K^+$ decays, is investigated as an axial-vector $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular state within the QCD sum rule approach. A two-point sum rule incorporating quark, gluon, and mixed vacuum condensates up to dimension $10$ yields the mass and decay constant, $m_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (4005.89 \pm 47.15)~\text{MeV}$ and $f_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (2.87 \pm 0.55)\times 10^{-3}~\text{GeV}^{4}$, in agreement with the LHCb measurement. Since this mass lies above the $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ threshold, the strong coupling constants at the $χ_{c1}(4010)D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ vertices are extracted from three-point sum rules and used to compute the partial widths of the $D^{*-}D^{+}$ and $D^{*+}D^{-}$ channels. The resulting total width, $Γ_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (57.64 \pm 9.64)~\text{MeV}$, is compatible with experiment within uncertainties. These results support a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular interpretation of $χ_{c1}(4010)$ and offer sum-rule predictions for comparison with future measurements at BESIII, LHCb, and Belle~II.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Gauge-Covariant Wavelets for Quark-Propagator Sparsening and Distillation in Lattice QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We develop a novel gauge-covariant wavelet framework for computing hadronic correlation functions in lattice QCD. Two complementary approaches connect spatial localization and resolution-scale separation to propagator sparsening and distillation. A gauge-covariant fast wavelet transform, based on compactly supported biorthogonal filters, coarse-grains quark propagators and reduces early-time excited-state contamination relative to direct decimation at equal spatial reduction. A second construction applies a resolvent filter of the spatial covariant Laplacian to localized sources, generating a distillation subspace without computing Laplacian eigenpairs. We detail its gauge covariance, smearing profiles, and implementation in exact and stochastic distillation. Spatial localization enables unbiased Hansen-Hurwitz sampling of hadronic contractions, reducing their computational cost substantially. We also examine momentum aliasing induced by fixed coarse grids and the use of random grid shifts to remove unwanted contributions in expectation. Numerical benchmarks of the proposed methods are performed with single hadrons, the I = 2 two-pion system, the deuteron channel, and boosted nucleons. The extracted energy levels agree very well with full or conventional distillation calculations within statistical uncertainties. We quantify the costs of on-demand basis construction and contractions, demonstrate contraction speedups at comparable statistical precision. These studies establish a practical foundation of wavelet-based propagator compression and operator construction for multi-operator calculations of hadronic and nuclear systems, particularly at larger lattice volumes.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Bayesian inference of the magnetic component of quark-gluon plasma
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The chromo-magnetic monopoles (CMM), emergent topological excitations of non-Abelian gauge fields carrying chromo-magnetic charge, have long been postulated to play an important role in the vacuum confinement of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the deconfinement transition at temperature $T_c\approx 160\rm MeV$, as well as the strongly coupled nature of quark-gluon plasma (QGP). While such CMMs have been found to provide solutions for challenging puzzles from heavy-ion collision measurements, they were typically introduced as model assumptions in the past. Here we show how their very existence can be determined and their abundance extracted in a data-driven way for the first time. Using the \textsc{cujet3} framework for calculations of jet energy loss and analyzing a comprehensive experimental data set for nuclear modification factor ($R_{\mathrm{AA}}$) and elliptic flow ($v_2$) of high-transverse-momentum hadrons, the fraction of CMMs in the QGP is obtained by Bayesian inference and is found to be substantial in the $1\sim 2 T_c$ region. The posterior CMM fraction is further validated by excellent agreement with additional data and is also shown to predict QGP transport properties quantitatively consistent with the state-of-the-art knowledge.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Consistency Checks for Λ positive Quantum Cosmology
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this paper we improve and further analyze the recently derived quantum gravity equations which apply in accelerating cosmological spacetimes and whose solutions re-sum leading logarithms from all orders of perturbation theory. We show the consistency of these upgraded equations against 1-loop non-trivial exact perturbative computations. The upgraded equations retain their remarkably simple form.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0π^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar Kπ$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: KKpi-mass-dependent efficiency considered. Conclusions do not change. 11 pages, 5 figures and 5 tables

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=κ_Qσ_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $κ_Q$ and $σ_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $NΛ$ interaction from a quark model: $pΛ$ femtoscopy and the hypertriton
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Understanding the low-energy nucleon--$Λ$ interaction is essential for describing hypernuclear structures, while its spin dependence remains insufficiently constrained by experimental data.
