Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Temporal entanglement transition in chaotic quantum many-body dynamics
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Temporal entanglement (TE) of an influence matrix (IM) has been proposed as a measure of complexity of simulating dynamics of local observables in a many-body system. Foligno et al. [Phys. Rev. X 13, 041008 (2023)] recently argued that the TE in chaotic 1d quantum circuits obeys linear (volume-law) scaling with evolution time. To reconcile this apparent high complexity of IM with the rapid thermalization of local observables, here we study the relation between TE, non-Markovianity, and local temporal correlations for chaotic quantum baths. By exactly solving a random-unitary bath model, and bounding distillable entanglement between future and past degrees of freedom, we identify a regime where TE is extensive and reflects genuine non-Markovianity. This memory, however, is entirely contained in highly complex temporal correlations, and its effect on few-point temporal correlators is negligible. An IM coarse-graining procedure, reducing the allowed frequency of measurements of the probe system, results in a transition from volume- to {subvolume- (area or logarithmic)} law TE scaling. We demonstrate the generality of this TE transition in 1d circuits by analyzing the kicked Ising model analytically at dual-unitary points, as well as numerically away from them. This finding indicates that dynamics of local observables are fully captured by a subvolume-law IM. We provide evidence that the compact IM MPS obtained via standard compression algorithms accurately describes local~evolution.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Quantum Fisher Information in semiclassical magnon systems
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) is a powerful spectroscopic tool to witness many-body quantum entanglement in solid state materials, but it is not always obvious how to relate it to other characteristics of condensed matter systems. In this study we elaborate on the meaning and interpretation of QFI in condensed matter by examining simple theoretical spin systems. We use finite sized spin systems to illustrate that QFI quantifies the momentum- dependent degree of quantum entanglement (that is the entanglement depth at a given wave vector) within a wave function. We subsequently use semiclassical frustrated spin models to show that, in the context of linear spin wave theory (LSWT), QFI quantifies the momentum-dependent degree of magnon squeezing in the ground state. In antiferromagnets with a zero-energy Goldstone mode, LSWT breaks down and QFI (and entanglement depth) diverges at the magnetic ordering wave vector. We also show examples of emergent quantum phases in frustrated spin systems that do not appear in classical phase diagrams. When these emergent phases are approached, QFI diverges across multiple wave vectors in momentum space. Taken together, QFI is not only helpful as a lower bound for entanglement depth, but serves as a momentum-resolved probe of entanglement that offers a novel perspective on quantum critical phenomena.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Phase Optimization Complexity in Variational Wave Functions for Heisenberg Antiferromagnets
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: We study the computational complexity of learning the ground state phase structure of Heisenberg antiferromagnets. Representing Hilbert space as a weighted graph, the variational energy defines a weighted XY model that, for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ phases, reduces to a classical antiferromagnetic Ising model on that graph. For fixed amplitudes, reconstructing the signs of the ground state wavefunction thus reduces to a weighted Max-Cut instance. This links sign optimization of wavefunctions directly to combinatorial optimization.
Strongly Correlated Electrons.comment: The NP-hardness claim has been corrected, and the connection to variational Monte Carlo has been revised

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. We show that these features can arise from two competing fates of the inner hole pocket in an annular Fermi sea: collapse into a simply connected Fermi liquid or crystallization into an anticrystal, in which localized holes coexist with itinerant electrons. Pocket collapse contracts the outer Fermi contour at fixed density, whereas hole crystallization preserves a larger contour that supports magnetic-breakdown orbits. This contrast provides a possible explanation for the frequency jump, while additional reconstructed orbits produce a multitone spectrum. Our results support the anticrystal as a candidate normal state near superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Field Theory of the Gutzwiller Projection
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: The Gutzwiller projection produces a well-known ansatz for spin-liquid and quantum Hall ground-state wavefunctions that is amenable to numerical simulation, with the Laughlin wavefunction being the most celebrated example. A long-standing issue is the precise relation between the Gutzwiller projection and the closely related parton gauge theory. Here, we clarify this issue by providing a field-theoretic description of the Gutzwiller projection. In a path integral description, the universal physics of the projected state is described in terms of a gauge field supported on a temporal slab of vanishing width $ε\rightarrow 0$ coupled to the bulk matter fields. We analytically derive the universal physics of various Gutzwiller projected states. Our construction is also applicable to discrete symmetries, and we use it to analyze various projected SPT states. Among our results, we show that the Gutzwiller projection is not a good ansatz for the long-distance properties of $U(1)$ Dirac spin liquids, spinon Fermi surface spin liquids or composite Fermi liquids, and that the Gutzwiller projection of a quantum spin Hall state has only quasi-long range order. In contrast, in examples where the gauge field is gapped, including Laughlin states, $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquids and Luttinger liquids, we show that the slab gauge theory from Gutzwiller projection reproduces the correct universal physics of the full parton gauge theory. We also present a generalization of our field theory that describes $G$-intertwining defects, with application to self-duality defects of recent theoretical interest.

Strongly Correlated Electrons.title: Spectral signatures of hidden order and hidden quantum critical points
Strongly Correlated Electrons.summary: Hidden-order phases elude the conventional Ginzburg-Landau framework: although they spontaneously break symmetry, their order remains invisible to standard local two-point correlators. Instead, they are typically characterized by nonlocal (string) order parameters and are believed to underlie a range of exotic quantum states, such as symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. While hidden correlations have previously been detected through nonlocal observables in quantum gas microscope experiments, in realistic solid-state systems multipoint observables are typically inaccessible and the signatures of hidden order remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show that hidden order in doped spin chains can be directly probed through dynamical two-point response functions measurable by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and neutron scattering. Focusing on a minimal model, we numerically identify clear spectral fingerprints of both the hidden-order phase, its associated hidden quantum critical point as well as a specific group of gapless SPT phases. Complementing our numerical results with analytical insights, we uncover the microscopic origin of these spectral signatures and demonstrate how they emerge from the interplay between spin and charge degrees of freedom. Together, our results establish spectroscopy as a practical probe of hidden order and gapless SPT phases and provide a unified understanding of the low-energy physics governing these unconventional quantum phases.

Nuclear Theory.title: Hyperonic Direct-Urca Neutrino Emission with Lattice-QCD-Informed Form Factors
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of direct-Urca neutrino emission in hyperonic neutron-star matter to the structure and momentum dependence of baryonic transition form factors. Using the zero-temperature FSU2H relativistic mean-field equation of state, we derive the relativistic emissivity for general spin-$1/2$ baryon transitions with the complete six form-factor contribution. We compare conventional static flavor-SU(3) couplings with vacuum lattice-QCD-informed form factors, using direct lattice vacuum input for $n\rightarrow p$ and $Λ\rightarrow p$ and a hybrid construction for the remaining hyperonic channels. Evaluating the latter both at $q^2=0$ and at the kinetic momentum transfer sampled at the Fermi surfaces separates changes in the zero-momentum couplings from momentum-transfer effects. The sensitivity is strongly channel dependent. The nucleonic transition probes $q^2\simeq0$ and is only weakly affected, whereas hyperonic channels can sample substantially larger momentum transfers and receive correspondingly larger corrections. These modifications propagate to the integrated neutrino luminosity of stellar configurations. Our results estimate the possible scale of the sensitivity coming from momentum transfer dependence, absent from static-coupling treatments and motivate future first-principles studies of baryonic weak currents in dense matter.

Nuclear Theory.title: Expansion schemes for finite density QCD equation of state: which one is the best?
Nuclear Theory.summary: The finite density equation of state of QCD is a fundamental quantity for understanding the phase structure of the theory, and also for the realistic modeling of the QCD medium in simulations. While direct lattice simulations at finite density are extremely challenging, several expansion schemes have been devised to extrapolate into the QCD phase diagram. All of these schemes are based on susceptibilities of conserved charges, i.e. derivatives of the pressure with respect to the chemical potential(s). In this work we set out to determine which of these schemes possesses the best convergence properties. To this end, we employ extreme-statistics lattice simulations on a $16^3\times8$ lattice, which allow us to obtain susceptibilities up to order eight with remarkably small errors. We compare in particular two methods, based on contours of constant (normalized) baryon density and of constant entropy density. We find that the latter converges more quickly, effectively requiring susceptibilities only up to order four to cover the chemical potential range up to at least $μ_B \approx 500$ MeV. We also extend the comparison to the three dimensional space of chemical potentials, and find that the entropy-based method consistently shows superior convergence.

Nuclear Theory.title: Statistical Analysis of Neutron Star Cooling: Implications for the Nuclear Equation of State and Nucleon Pairing
Nuclear Theory.summary: We perform a statistical analysis of the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars by confronting theoretical cooling curves with luminosity-age measurements for 24 sources. For each object, we explore five purely nucleonic equations of state (APR4, FSU2R, DD2, IST, and NL3$ωρ$) combined with representative models of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity, while varying the gravitational mass and envelope composition. The analysis spans approximately $10^5$ cooling curves. Within this framework, we find that only the NL3$ωρ$ equation of state and, to a lesser extent, IST, both including neutron triplet pairing, provide an overall satisfactory description of the data. The remaining equations of state are in significant tension with the observations. These results demonstrate that NS cooling provides complementary constraints on dense matter, alongside nuclear structure, global NS observables, and gravitational-wave observations, while probing the interplay between the EoS and nucleon pairing.

Nuclear Theory.title: Real-time quantum simulation of hadron production in deep inelastic scattering
Nuclear Theory.summary: We develop a quantum simulation framework for meson production in deep inelastic scattering based on light-front QCD Hamiltonian formalism. A quark-antiquark dipole, prepared either as a single-momentum state or as the $q\bar q$ component of a virtual photon, is evolved in real time through the color field of a nuclear target via Trotterized unitary evolution. We consider both proton and gold nuclear targets, each characterized by their respective saturation scale. From the evolved state we extract the transverse momentum broadening, the total and elastic cross sections, and the $J/ψ$ production rate by projecting onto the $J/ψ$ light-front wavefunction. We then extract the nuclear modification factor $R_A$ at different photon virtuality $Q^2$ and analyze nuclear modification effect. Results of classical simulations show good agreement with analytical eikonal predictions across a broad range of parameters. For the single-momentum dipole, quantum simulation is demonstrated on a quantum circuit emulator with a smaller lattice size, and results are consistent with the classical benchmark. This work establishes a first-principles, amplitude-level pathway toward computing exclusive hadron production in deep inelastic scattering, directly relevant to the physics program of the Electron-Ion Collider.

Nuclear Theory.title: Investigating forward-backward asymmetry in D-meson production and anisotropic flow in p-Pb collisions at the LHC
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate the forward--backward asymmetry in the production and elliptic flow of prompt D0 mesons in proton--lead (p--Pb) collisions at$\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=8.16$ TeV using the heavy-flavor improved string-melting version of the AMPT model. The model calculations provide a simultaneous description of nuclear modification factor $R_{\mathrm{pPb}}$ and $v_2$ in forward and backward rapidities. We find that the observed asymmetry arises from the interplay of initial-state cold nuclear matter effects and final-state partonic interactions, with the competition between coalescence and fragmentation playing a critical role in shaping the transverse momentum and rapidity dependence of both observables. This work suggests that a partonic medium is formed in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at LHC energies.

Nuclear Theory.title: Neutron-star dark-matter limits measure the maximum-mass headroom
Nuclear Theory.summary: Neutron stars constrain dark matter that is present inside them, through their maximum mass and the tidal deformability. The standard approach adds a dark component to one nuclear equation of state (EoS) and compares the stars with pulsar masses and with GW170817, so each limit inherits an EoS dependence that has not been quantified. In this paper we add a QCD axion and a $Z'$-portal dark fermion to the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model, in the formulation of the public code of Kumamoto et al.\ [Phys.\ Rev.\ D \textbf{112}, 043008 (2025)], and compute the stars for $257$ published RMF parameter sets from the compilation of Sun, Bhattiprolu, and Lattimer [Phys.\ Rev.\ C \textbf{109}, 055801 (2024)], with the dark matter either moving with the baryons or in its own equilibrium. We find that the stars constrain only the dark rest mass per baryon, and that its upper limit is the maximum-mass headroom of the EoS above the pulsar-mass bound divided by a quasi-universal rate, whose residual follows the compactness of the maximum-mass star; a compact dark core roughly doubles the rate, and the axion condensate barely changes it. Capture cannot supply the dark matter the stars could detect, and the portal reaches the EoS only at couplings disfavoured by anomaly cancellation, so a neutron-star limit on dark matter is a statement about the headroom of the nuclear EoS.

Nuclear Theory.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
Nuclear Theory.summary: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $Δ(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $Δ$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $Δ$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. We derive the relativistic matrix elements for the charged-current $Δ\to N$ and $Δ\toΔ'$ transitions, evaluate all electronic and muonic Urca processes over the full phase space using the nucleon width approximation, and include the in-medium $Δ\to Nπ$ width with Pauli blocking. The bulk viscosity is obtained from the coupled linear response of the electron and muon fractions about the finite-temperature flavor equilibrium. We find that the $Δ^-$ takes over the negative charge from the leptons, which raises the proton fraction and opens the nucleonic direct Urca process. Up to about 3~MeV this change in composition, rather than the $Δ$ reactions themselves, controls flavor equilibration. As a consequence, the resonant maximum of the bulk viscosity moves to lower temperatures for all oscillation frequencies we consider, and kHz density oscillations near resonance are damped several times faster than in nucleonic matter. We also show that, for nucleonic matter, the choice of the equilibrium state about which the rates are linearized shifts the resonance temperature by up to a few MeV at high density.

Nuclear Theory.title: Energy Correlators in Semi-Inclusive Electron-Positron Annihilation
Nuclear Theory.summary: We investigate energy correlators in semi-inclusive electron-positron annihilation as precision probes of parton-to-hadron transition. Using soft-collinear effective theory, we analyze the correlation patterns between the examined hadron and the accompanying QCD radiation in both large-angle and small-angle limits. We derive complementary factorization formulas in the back-to-back and collinear limits, involving TMD fragmentation functions and fragmentation energy correlators, respectively. We compute the NNLO twist-two matching coefficients of the latter and obtain renormalization-group-improved predictions at N\(^3\)LL accuracy in the back-to-back region and NNLL accuracy in the collinear region. Our results demonstrate that semi-inclusive energy correlators provide direct, theoretically controlled access to QCD dynamics underlying hadronization, opening new avenues for precision studies at future lepton colliders as well as through reanalyses of archival LEP data.
Nuclear Theory.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. Normalization of 1/2 is corrected, the consistency of our analysis with the dihadron fragmentation framework is confirmed

Nuclear Theory.title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
Nuclear Theory.summary: We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Robustness of Neural Networks for CMB Polarization Foreground Removal
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The detection of Cosmic Microwave Background primordial $B$-mode polarization would constitute a ``smoking gun" signal of primordial gravitational waves. However, this measurement requires accurate removal of polarized Galactic foregrounds to avoid systematic biases when estimating the tensor-to-scalar ratio. Methods based on Machine Learning techniques (ML), such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have recently been proposed as alternative foreground cleaning techniques, but their applicability to real data relies on their ability to generalize beyond the models assumed during training. In this work, we focus on a variety of foreground models (FMs) used for training and conduct a systematic study of the generalization properties of a CNN-based method. We train various CNN architectures on simulations generated from different Galactic FMs, and test their performance on models not used during the training. By characterizing the statistical properties of the FMs using variance, skewness, and Shannon entropy, we define a statistical complexity hierarchy among them. We show that training on the more complex FMs reduces bias and improves precision when testing on unseen FMs, whereas training on the simplest model could introduce systematic errors. These results evidence that a lack of generalization is a relevant source of systematic uncertainty, and emphasize the importance of understanding the impact of the models assumed during training in ML-based methods before applying them to real data.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points and beyond of far-from-equilibrium dilute system: ultra-cold Fermi gas
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The far-from-equilibrium dynamics driven by the scattering from next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections in the quantum field theory has stationary solutions for the particle distribution characterized as the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points corresponding to scale-invariant particle/energy flux. The dynamics of the spatially homogeneous dilute ultra-cold Fermi gas is investigated, and its kinetic equation confirms the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points in the perturbation theory by the quasi-particle assumption, in contrast to the wave turbulence of the ultra-cold Bose gas. In addition, other stationary states are discussed when the the vertex correction becomes significant in the kinetic equation. It is found that conditions for the scale-invariant flux in this case no longer hold when the quasi-particle assumption is applied.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Exothermic Dark Matter with a Dark Higgs: The LZ 248 keV Event and the Galactic Center Excess
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) reported a $248~\mathrm{keV}$ nuclear-recoil event. Exothermic dark matter can explain it in a dark $U(1)$ model whose dark Higgs generates the dark photon mass and the mass splitting. A computed excited-state fraction gives two branches with dark photon masses near $1$ and $26~\mathrm{GeV}$ for kinetic mixing $ε=10^{-4}$. INTEGRAL/SPI limits on excited-state decays bound the LZ rate, and cosmic microwave background limits exclude the lighter branch at its likelihood minimum. For a dark Higgs boson near the dark photon mass, the heavier branch agrees with the southern-sky Galactic Center $γ$-ray excess.
