By adjusting the renormalization group variables to the geometry of the effective theory modes, our method naturally extends to a broad spectrum of physical problems including massive, massless, small, and wide angle scattering. We present applications to the benchmark processes of electron-positron forward annihilation and light quark mediated Higgs boson production/decays.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Changed IR regularization scheme for NLL evolution kernel in the case of electron-muon forward annihilation. Solution now retains full dependence on the electron-to-muon mass ratio

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $μ/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\leμ/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Photon and gluon gravitational form factors of proton in QCD
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The energy momentum tensor allows us to probe the internal gravitational structure of the proton. The corresponding gravitational form factors contain information about its different contributions. In this work, we investigate the photon and gluon gravitational form factors of the proton within the QCD sum rule approach. Four independent gravitational form factors are computed in the range $0<Q^2<2\ \mathrm{GeV}^2$. The mass and scalar radii of the photon and gluon sectors are obtained in the forward limit. We find that the gluon mass radius is smaller than the photon mass radius. These results may be useful for future lattice QCD calculations and phenomenological studies.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $ρ_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $ρ_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $τ$ electric dipole form factor
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We compute the four-loop matching of a CP-odd four-$τ$ interaction onto the electron electric dipole moment (EDM), together with the leading timelike $τ$ dipole form factor generated by the same source. Both results are scale independent at this order. Without a local electron dipole, exact electron-EDM cancellation still leaves a timelike $τ$ signal proportional to the four-$τ$ coefficient. Its absorptive part cannot be canceled by a real local dipole, allowing collider limits to constrain the cancellation direction and complement static electron-EDM searches.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures. Calculation code and reproduction instructions are included as ancillary files

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Nonflow Subtraction Beyond Two-Particle Correlations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Establishing collective flow in small collision systems is a crucial and necessary condition for pinning down the minimum conditions for quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formation. In two-particle correlations, nonflow has been subtracted with good control, pushing the reach of flow measurements down to very small event particle multiplicity $N$. However, the multi-particle nature of collectivity has not been established in the same $N$ regime, because the residual nonflow surviving the subevent procedure in multi-particle cumulants has never been quantified. We develop a general nonflow subtraction framework for $m$-particle cumulants, built around the approximate $1/N^{m-1}$ scaling of nonflow in the independent-source picture. Correlators containing $v_1$ serve as nonflow-dominated estimators, since the $p_{\mathrm T}$-integrated dipolar flow is expected to be small. Using HIJING as a controlled nonflow-only environment, we test the subtraction for three target observables ($\langle v_2^2\rangle$, $\langle v_2^2δp_{\mathrm T}\rangle$, and $c_2\{4\}$) in O+O at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV and 200 GeV and in $d$+Au at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 200$ GeV. Most of the nonflow is removed, with residual fractions typically within 20-30% when converted to the two-particle level, though the best estimator differs across the three targets. We identify a multiplicity-reweighting correction, previously overlooked in two-particle correlations, that explains the long-standing undersubtraction of the naive $1/N$-scaling method; its impact grows as a power of the correlator order. The framework gives a systematic route to nonflow subtraction beyond two-particle correlations, broadening the class of multi-particle observables accessible to the small-system flow program.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Exceptional Jordan spectra and conditional fermion mass relations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We formulate a conditional fermion-mass ansatz motivated by the exceptional Jordan algebra, separating its geometric order parameters from the physical chiral matter representation. A real coassociative octonionic configuration has Jordan spectrum $(s-δ,s,s+δ)$; the choice $δ^2=3/8$ specifies its normalization rather than a derived physical mass scale. An explicit compression of a positive operator on $Sym^3(C^3)$ reproduces the proposed quark mass formulas for stated weight selections. The selected three-dimensional spaces are not $SU(3)$ subrepresentations, and the charged-lepton formulas require an additional cross-sector transport rule. Eliminating the spectral parameter yields exact consistency relations, including $\sqrt{m_c/m_u}=2\sqrt{m_t/m_c}-1$. A common-scale comparison using a published 2026 Standard-Model running-Yukawa analysis, supplemented by PDG 2026 checks, exhibits substantial discrepancies. In particular, the up-sector relation fails at the electroweak benchmark even when $δ$ is released. We identify the interaction, localization and kinetic-normalization data needed to derive or modify the ansatz. The construction retains a geometric interpretation but establishes neither three generations inside a single $E_6$ representation $27$ nor a precision explanation of the measured fermion masses.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: v7. 13 pages. Title modified. Article revised in response to referee comments

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Holographic Calculation of Semileptonic Form Factors and the Isgur--Wise Function for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ Decays
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a holographic analysis of the semileptonic decays $B \to D \ell \barν_\ell$ and $B_s \to D_s \ell \barν_\ell$ within the Softwall Model (SWM) and the Non-Quadratic Softwall Model (NQSWM). We extract the Isgur-Wise function from the overlap integral of bulk wavefunctions, with model parameters fixed by the heavy-light meson spectra. We impose Heavy Quark Symmetry (HQS) at zero recoil and address the apparent paradox of a non-conserved electroweak current dual to a massless bulk vector field. We argue that the non-conservation, arising from explicit flavor-- symmetry breaking by quark masses, does not generate an anomalous dimension. Hence the bulk field remains massless, and the non-conservation is \emph{encoded} in the independent boundary couplings $g_+$ and $g_-$. Our predictions for the branching fractions are in good agreement with LHCb data for $B_s \to D_s$ decays. The lepton-flavor universality ratios $R(D)$ and $R(D_s)$ are consistent with Standard Model and lattice QCD predictions. We find that the holographic models reproduce the universality of the Isgur-Wise function near zero recoil, while discrepancies at maximum recoil suggest that a more complete treatment of higher-order $1/m_Q$ corrections is needed.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Precision electroweak predictions for future $e^+e^-$ colliders will require levels of precision unmatched in collider physics and the modelling of multiple-photon emissions, and the exponentiation of the associated logarithms needs to be carefully considered. The Yennie-Frautschi-Suura theorem subtracts the infrared singularities to all orders and exponentiates them, leaving infrared-finite remainders which can be calculated order-by-order. Coherent exponentiation performs this subtraction at the amplitude level, preserving the interference between emissions, but has so far been available only for fermion-pair production, with hand-coded amplitudes. We present ACRAIC, an automated, amplitude-level realization of this subtraction for general scattering processes in Sherpa. This method allows us to construct an $\mathcal{O}(α)$ and $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ amplitude level subtraction scheme, in which the infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by the Berends--Giele recursion, and the one-loop electroweak virtual enters through a per-helicity factor from the loop provider. At $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ two independent matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to $\sim10^{-3}$, and the estimated perturbative uncertainty shrinks by about an order of magnitude relative to $\mathcal{O}(α)$.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $S_3$ gaugings of $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}'_N$ non-invertible symmetries: quark texture zeros and phenomenology
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate texture zeros in the quark Yukawa matrices arising from the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $S_3$ gauging of $\mathbb{Z}_N\times\mathbb{Z}'_N$, associated with the non-invertible $Δ(3N^2)$ and $Δ(6N^2)$ symmetries, respectively. We construct the equivalence classes and their fusion rules and use them as selection rules for the Yukawa interactions. We systematically classify the full-rank quark Yukawa textures generated by the two gaugings for $N=2,3,4,$ and $5$. The two gaugings yield the same texture spectrum for $N=2$ and $N=4$, whereas the $S_3$ gauging produces additional textures for $N=3$ and $N=5$. We further analyze the most restrictive texture pairs compatible with quark data and find that there are at most nine zeros in these texture pairs. For up- and down-quark mass matrices with a total of nine texture zeros, one sector is allowed to contain six zeros while the other contains three, or one contains five zeros while the other contains four. The former case has been studied in previous works. We perform numerical fits for the latter and find it consistent with experimental data. Some viable textures also admit real quark-mass determinants while retaining a physical CKM phase, suggesting a possible connection to the strong CP problem.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Models for differential cross section in neutron-proton scattering and their implications
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: A few analytic exponential models of the elastic differential cross section are proposed to analyse elastic neutron-proton (np) scattering. The models incorporate energy-dependent exponential slopes, power-law prefactors, and localized Gaussian modifications. Sub-leading exponential terms representing charge conjugation and isospin roles increase the applicability and quality of fit of the models to describe the differential cross section data of np, n \bar{p}, pp, and p \bar{p} elastic scattering. The models describe the characteristic features of all the elastic scattering data such as the dip-bump structure, shrinkage of the forward peak, and controlled curvature around the diffractive dip. Parameter values of the models are found by fitting the np experimental data in an energy range of (\sqrt{s}\) = 3.363 to 26.019 GeV and a momentum transfer range of 0.065 to 5.341 GeV^2. Employing the proposed models, total, elastic, and inelastic cross sections, slope parameters, interaction radii, and cross-section ratios for np scattering are calculated. A multi-stage error analysis is performed to evaluate the error in the calculations of the models. Implications of the results obtained by the models for nucleon structure and dynamics are discussed. The results show that the proposed models can be used for effective description of the np elastic differential cross section and for accurate estimation of the observables of elastic hadronic scattering. The findings of this study emphasize the significance of combining theoretical and phenomenological approaches, providing valuable information for investigations of future experimental data on the differential cross section from various colliders.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing a heavy neutral lepton in a radiative neutrino model at a muon collider
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate direct and Higgs-mediated production of a Dirac heavy neutral lepton in a radiative neutrino-mass model at a future $3~\mathrm{TeV}$ muon collider. We consider heavy neutral lepton masses in the window $m_Z<m_N<m_h$, where the decays $N\to\ell W$ and $N\toνZ$ can proceed with on-shell weak bosons. We consider both direct production, $μ^+μ^-\to Nν$, and Higgs-mediated production through $μ^+μ^-\toν_μ\barν_μh$, $h\to Nν$. Both channels lead to the common $\ell^\pm jj+p_{\mathrm T}^{\mathrm{miss}}$ final state. We perform a detector-level analysis with an integrated luminosity of $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, assuming unpolarized muon beams, and derive median expected $95\%$ confidence-level upper limits on the visible signal cross section ranging from approximately $0.027$ to $0.113~\mathrm{fb}$, corresponding to limits on the mixing strength parameter $|U_{μN}|^2$ ranging from $6.7\times10^{-6}$ to $8.3\times10^{-5}$ for six benchmark points. The Higgs-mediated production channel contributes $\sim15$--$72\%$ of the signal after the common event selection, but improves the expected limits by $\sim0.18$--$1.19\%$ within the common classifier and binning scheme. This small improvement reflects the classifier-score distribution of the Higgs-mediated events. The limits on $|U_{μN}|^2$ account for the benchmark-specific flavor mixings and assume an independent $10\%$ background uncertainty in each classifier-score bin.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hadronization in QCD and Fragmentation Functions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The hadronization of quarks and gluons is reviewed within the framework of collinear parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions closely associated with the notion of factorization in hard scattering processes in QCD. The state-of-the-art in calculating both the scale evolution of fragmentation functions and the partonic cross sections pertinent to their determination from data up to next-to-next-to-leading order accuracy is presented. Potential improvements up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic order are outlined as well. All relevant experimental data sets for single-inclusive pion, kaon, and unidentified charged hadron production are listed. The most recent sets of fragmentation functions and their uncertainties extracted from these data in global QCD analyses utilizing various different strategies are presented and compared to each other.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 34 pages, 7 figures. Contribution prepared for the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics by Elsevier

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Soft Breaking Naturalness in Majorana Fermion Loop induced Scalar and Majoron Amplitudes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Majorana fermion loops contribute a shift-symmetry violating effective potential to the coupled scalar field. When the Majorana fermion is light, a larger number of symmetry violating insertions let the loop contribution to grow increasingly infrared sensitive to the Majorana mass. With explicit calculations, we calculate the symmetry violating amplitudes, show that the scalar potential's natural scales serve as nonzero kinematic matching points which remove the superficial sensitivity to the symmetry-violating Majorana mass, continuously restoring the shift symmetry in agreement with 't Hooft naturalness. In the spontaneous broken phase, the scalar radial vacuum expectation value readily ensures the infrared safety of symmetry violating Majorana fermion loops, and all $n$-point Majoron functions develop a leading linear dependence on the symmetry violating parameter in the soft breaking limit, which matches the expansion of the Coleman-Weinberg determinant.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Investigating three-body resonances in $ααΩ/Ω_{ccc}$ clusters within the $^{9}_{Ω/Ω_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ nucleus
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the bound and resonant states of the $α+α+Ω$ and $α+α+Ω_{ccc}$ three-body systems, corresponding to $^{9}_Ω{\mathrm{Be}}$ and $^{9}_{Ω_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$, within the Gaussian expansion method combined with the complex scaling method. The $αΩ$ and $αΩ_{ccc}$ interactions are constructed by folding the $NΩ$ and $NΩ_{ccc}$ potentials obtained from lattice QCD calculations by the HAL QCD Collaboration with the nucleon density distribution of the $α$ particle. The uncertainty associated with the $α$-particle matter radius is also examined. For the $Ω$ sector, the strong $NΩ$ attraction generates deeply bound $0_1^+$, $2_1^+$, and $4_1^+$ states in $^{9}_Ω{\mathrm{Be}}$, accompanied by a pronounced contraction of the $αα$ core, demonstrating a strong gluelike effect of the $Ω$ baryon. An unconventional inversion between the $0_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ levels is also predicted. In contrast, the $Ω_{ccc}$ baryon produces considerably weaker attraction: the $0_1^+$ state of $^{9}_{Ω_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ is weakly bound, whereas the $2_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ states remain resonances. Their resonance energies and widths exhibit a clear dependence on the strength of the $αΩ_{ccc}$ interaction. These results reveal qualitatively different gluelike behaviors of the $Ω$ and $Ω_{ccc}$ baryons and provide predictions for the spectroscopy of exotic multistrange and triply charmed hypernuclei.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures and 5 tables. Accepted by Phys. Rev. D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Soft-Collinear Chiral Perturbation Theory for $B \to π$ form factors at large recoil
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We develop an effective hadronic theory for heavy-meson decays into energetic pions, organized by the approximate heavy-quark and chiral symmetries. The dynamical degrees of freedom of the theory consist of quasi-static heavy-meson fields coupled to soft and collinear pions, relevant for exclusive $B \to π$ transitions at large recoil energy ${E_π\simeq M_B/2}$. Our approach exploits the factorization of soft and collinear quarks in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), leading to an emergent duplication of chiral symmetry in the two kinematic sectors. Promoting the soft and collinear chiral transformations to local symmetries enables us to systematically match non-local four-quark operators in SCET -- governing the soft-overlap contribution to heavy-to-light form factors -- onto effective operators constructed from hadronic fields below the scale of chiral symmetry breaking. As a first application, we compute the logarithmically enhanced pion-mass dependence of the $B \to π$ form factors at large recoil by calculating the one-loop matrix elements of the leading hadronic operators. We find that the non-local transition currents in our effective theory lead to a pattern of chiral-logarithmic corrections that is not compatible with the existing formulation provided by Hard-Pion Chiral Perturbation Theory.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 31 pages, 4 figures. v2: Simplified hadronic soft operator basis. Main conclusions unchanged

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing the $τ$ anomalous magnetic and electric dipole moments in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production at the FCC-hh
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The sensitivity of the FCC-hh to the anomalous magnetic moment $a_τ$ and the electric dipole moment $d_τ$ of the $τ$ lepton is studied in photon-induced $γγ\toτ^+τ^-$ production with both $τ$ leptons decaying hadronically. Central exclusive (elastic) signal events, in which both protons remain intact, are generated with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO using a FeynRules UFO model of the anomalous $γττ$ vertex merged with the TauDecay model, so that the $τ$ decays and their spin correlations are included in the matrix element. Single- and double-dissociative production is estimated with SuperChic and added to the elastic signal with its own coupling dependence and with normalisation and shape uncertainties of 25%. Pythia 8 decays the unstable hadrons in the signal, decays the $τ$ leptons and simulates the parton shower and hadronisation in the backgrounds, and hadronises the dissociated protons. Signal and backgrounds are passed through the Delphes simulation of the FCC-hh detector. Hadronic $τ$ decays are reconstructed from particle-flow tracks and photons with an algorithm based on the hadrons-plus-strips approach, with an efficiency of 73.4% within the acceptance. Requiring no additional tracks from the $τ$ vertices retains part of the dissociative contribution and reduces the Drell-Yan and $γγ\to WW$ backgrounds to 0.9% of the SM yield. The couplings are constrained from the shape of the total transverse mass distribution. For a centre-of-mass energy of 84 TeV and 30 ab$^{-1}$, the expected 95% CL limits are $-3.38\times10^{-4} < a_τ< 3.36\times10^{-4}$ and $|d_τ| < 1.88\times10^{-18}\,e\,$cm, about an order of magnitude beyond the current bounds. Results are also given for FCC-hh scenarios between 72 and 120 TeV and for an optimistic detector parametrisation.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Polarization signatures of mixed scalar - pseudoscalar ALP - photon couplings in intense laser pulses
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. Varying the collision angle between the strong pulse and the probe provides a continuous kinematic scan of the resonant ALP mass. For fixed kinematics in this setting, the scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type ALP conversion amplitudes interfere coherently, making both the photon-to-ALP conversion probability and the polarization rotation depend on the difference between the probe polarization angle $α$ and the coupling angle $θ_g$. Conversion is maximal at $|α-θ_g|=90^\circ$, where the polarization rotation vanishes, while the rotation magnitude peaks at $α-θ_g=45^\circ$ modulo $90^\circ$, where conversion is half-maximal. These complementary polarization-angle dependences provide polarization-resolved signatures of mixed scalar--pseudoscalar photon couplings.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: A Catalog of Lepton Mass Textures from Koide and Alikhanov Relations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The empirical Koide relation for charged-lepton masses and the recently proposed Alikhanov relation for neutrino mass-squared differences offer intriguing hints toward understanding the structure of lepton mass matrices. Motivated by these observations, we systematically explore charged-lepton and neutrino mass-matrix textures that satisfy these relations and confront their predictions for lepton mixing with experimental data. For the charged-lepton sector, we investigate representative positive Hermitian square-root matrices classified by the number of common eigenvector directions of their generators: three, one, or none. For the neutrino sector, an exhaustive enumeration of real symmetric integer matrices with entries between $-5$ and $5$ identifies six signed-permutation classes with $m_1=0$ and six with $m_1>0$ that satisfy the Alikhanov relation. Combining these neutrino textures with the charged-lepton constructions, allowing for different relative flavor orientations and phase alignments, yields $400$ viable structural pairs consistent with the measured lepton mixing parameters. All retained solutions satisfy the adopted cosmological bound on the sum of neutrino masses and existing laboratory constraints. In particular, the full-rank neutrino textures predict $m_1\simeq16.77$-$17.22\,\mathrm{meV}$. Representative viable solutions yield effective Majorana masses $m_{ββ}\simeq1.29$-$4.03\,\mathrm{meV}$ and $4.07$-$18.67\,\mathrm{meV}$ for the $m_1=0$ and $m_1>0$ branches, respectively, providing potential targets for future high-sensitivity searches.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 21 pages + references; 3 figures and 12 tables. Comments are welcome!

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Form factors and weak decays of $Λ_b\toΛ_c^*(2595)$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ_c^*(2790)$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this article, we reanalyze the mass and pole residue of $Λ$-type singly heavy baryons with spin-parity $J^P=1/2^{\pm}$ using two-point QCD sum rules. Then, we investigate the electroweak transition form factors of $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ^*_c(2790)$ within the framework of three-point QCD sum rules. At the hadron side, all possible couplings of the interpolating currents to hadronic states are taken into account, while at the QCD side, both the perturbative part and vacuum condensate contributions up to dimension-8 are included. Using the obtained form factors, we calculate the decay widths and branching ratios for the semileptonic decays $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)\ell\barν_\ell$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ^*_c(2790)\ell\barν_\ell$ ($\ell=e,μ$ and $τ$), as well as for the corresponding nonleptonic decays $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)π[ρ]$, $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)K[K^*]$, $Ξ_b\toΞ^*_c(2790)π[ρ]$ and $Ξ_b\toΞ^*_c(2790)K[K^*]$. Our predictions for the branching ratios of $Λ_b\toΛ^*_c(2595)\ell\barν_\ell$ are comparable with the experimental data and other theoretical results. In addition, we present predictions for several observables, including the lepton universality ratio, the forward-backward asymmetry $A_{FB}$, and the asymmetry parameter $α$, which may be useful for future experimental tests. These results can provide valuable references for future measurements.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. We evaluate, to our knowledge for the first time, the speed at which the shape of the proton's momentum distribution changes, measured by how well distributions at neighboring resolutions can be told apart statistically. At leading order, with one-loop splitting functions and running coupling, five fixed quark flavors, nonnegative quark and gluon densities and sufficiently regular inputs, we obtain a closed-form lower bound on this speed. Once the coupling is specified, three numbers of the input (the distribution at the starting resolution) fix the bound at every scale without computing the evolved distribution. For three of the five model inputs at four scales from 2 GeV to 10 TeV, the squared bound is at least 94.8 percent of the squared speed. The bound is reached when the distribution's relative rate of change is linear in the logarithm of the inverse momentum fraction. For these three model inputs at the four scales, the relative rate of change is close to this linear form in mean square weighted by momentum.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 28 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Supplemental material (14 pages, 1 figure) and the program codes and stored outputs that reproduce every number in the paper

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langleσv\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langleσv\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langleσv\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Direct Detection of Leptophobic Dark Matter with Electronic Collective Excitations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Some new-generation dark matter detection experiments are primarily designed to search for the dark matter-electron interactions, but they can also be utilized to probe models in which dark matter couples exclusively to nucleon via the quantum effects. The hadronic loop-induced interactions can directly excite plasmons in semiconductors, thereby providing an additional channel for detecting the leptophobic dark matter. In this work, we investigate plasmon excitations in silicon detectors induced by boosted dark matter and cosmic-ray up-scattering dark matter via the hadronic loop process. By analyzing the available experimental data, we derive new exclusion limits on the leptophobic dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section in the sub-MeV mass range.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table; Accepted by Chinese Physics C

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Femtoscopic correlation functions between the lightest charmed hadrons
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Femtoscopic momentum correlations probe low-energy interactions of short-lived charmed hadrons that are inaccessible to conventional scattering experiments. We calculate the correlation functions of $D^{+}D^{+}$, $D^{0}D^{0}$, $D^{+}D^{0}$, and $Λ_c^+Λ_c^+$ in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.02$~TeV, using species-dependent non-Gaussian PHSD sources constructed from hadronization points and strong interactions calibrated to lattice-QCD scattering lengths: OBE and EFT-contact models for $DD$, and an EFT-contact model for $Λ_cΛ_c$. Coulomb and quantum-statistical effects are included consistently. Although the calibrated interactions are weakly repulsive, the channels separate the relevant effects: $D^{+}D^{0}$, free of Coulomb distortion and identical-particle interference, gives the cleanest access to the $DD$ strong interaction, whereas $Λ_c^+Λ_c^+$ is most pronounced in peripheral collisions, where the compact source enhances the low-momentum signal. The $Λ_cΛ_c$ input is taken from lattice QCD at a nonphysical pion mass, so its physical-point shift is not quantified here. Within these stated inputs, the results provide ALICE-ready benchmark correlations and background references; the quoted bands propagate only the lattice scattering-length uncertainty.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Multi-scale improved predictions for $\boldsymbol{pp \to t\bar{t}W^+ +X}$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We compare standard fixed-order NLO QCD predictions for the full off-shell $pp \to e^+ν_e\, μ^-\barν_μ\, τ^+ν_τ\, b\bar{b} \, (j) + X$ processes in the multi-lepton decay channel with the results obtained using the MiNLO approach. The MiNLO method, now also implemented in the Helac-NLO framework, provides a dynamic determination of the renormalization and factorization scale settings by identifying the most likely branching histories of the additional jets through an inverse $k_T$-clustering algorithm. The inclusion of Sudakov form factors accounts for the large logarithms that arise in the presence of widely separated scales. We perform a dedicated comparison of the two approaches at both the integrated and differential (fiducial) cross-section levels for the LHC Run II energy of $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. Finally, we present the merging of the full off-shell predictions for $pp \to e^+ν_e\, μ^-\barν_μ\, τ^+ν_τ\, b\bar{b} \, + X$, $pp \to e^+ν_e\, μ^-\barν_μ\, τ^+ν_τ\, b\bar{b} \, j +X$ and $pp \to e^+ν_e\, μ^-\barν_μ\, τ^+ν_τ\, b\bar{b} \, jj$, with the aim of improving the description of the underlying $pp \to e^+ν_e\, μ^-\barν_μ\, τ^+ν_τ\, b\bar{b} + X$ process.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 32 pages, 12 figures, and 4 tables, version to appear in JHEP

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Partial reconstruction of the decay $B_{s}^{0}\rightarrow φ(K^{+}K^{-})η' (π^{+}π^{-}η)$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
The decay $B_s^0 \to φ(K^+K^-)η'(π^+π^-η)$ is of particular interest in flavour physics because in the Standard Model it proceeds predominantly through the quark transition $\bar{b} \to \bar{s}s\bar{s}$. However, the reconstruction of this decay is experimentally challenging due to the presence of the neutral $η$ particle, which significantly reduces the overall reconstruction efficiency.
  In this study, the feasibility of using the partial reconstruction technique to reconstruct the invariant mass of the $B_s^0$ meson without explicitly detecting the $η$ particle is investigated. Monte Carlo simulated events corresponding to an FCC-ee environment are used, and the effects of detector momentum and vertex resolutions on the reconstruction performance are examined.
  The results show that improved vertex resolution substantially improves the global reconstructed mass response and partial-reconstruction efficiency, while improvements in momentum resolution are manifested primarily through a narrowing of the fitted central DCB component. These findings suggest that future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders such as FCC-ee could effectively exploit the partial reconstruction technique to study rare decay modes containing undetected neutral particles.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Displaced e+e- Signatures from an X17-Mediated Inelastic Dark-Sector Cascade
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate displaced electron-positron signatures from an inelastic dark sector mediated by a light vector boson associated with the X17 anomaly. A heavy neutral fermion decays into a lighter stable state and the mediator, whose subsequent decay produces a single visible vertex after two stages of neutral propagation. We calculate the decay width, displacement distribution, lepton kinematics, and production rate in electro-positron collisions, including vector polarization. At Belle II, stronger dark-sector couplings increase production but require finely adjusted masses to preserve a macroscopic decay length. We quantify off-shell contributions and assess the validity of the two-body approximation. We show that the electron-positron pair cannot satisfy simultaneously the moment and opening-angle cuts of an existing search proposal for the configuration studied. Less restrictive selections allow nonzero kinematic acceptance. Our results clarify the experimental requirements for searching these signatures at Belle II.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Pion chemical potentials as seen from transverse momentum distributions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We examine the transverse momentum spectra of negatively charged pions emitted in proton-proton, proton-antiproton, and nucleus-nucleus collisions at beam momenta from tens to hundreds of GeV$/c$. The measured spectra are described within the framework of nonextensive Tsallis statistics, allowing the corresponding chemical potentials to be determined through a quantitative comparison with experimental data. The extracted thermodynamic parameters are subsequently employed to explore the structure of the phase diagram in the chemical potential-temperature ($μ$-$T$) plane, with particular emphasis on identifying possible signatures of a phase transition. Within this interpretation, pion production in the midrapidity region is associated with a phase characterized by broken chiral symmetry, whereas increasing rapidity corresponds to an evolution toward a regime in which chiral symmetry is restored.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
High Energy Phenomenology.summary:
We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO)
  nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of
  normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected
  trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion
  is organized. Through the isometric embedding
  $Φ=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on
  a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration
  determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based
  total-valence trajectory over
  $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but
  weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted
  principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions
  capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The
  corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a
  small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees
  with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration.
  An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion
  is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability
  weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions
  contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse
  bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary
  perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the
  collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results
  establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization
  of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized,
  near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Unveiling dark forces with measurements of the Large Scale Structure of the Universe
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Cosmology offers opportunities to test Dark Matter independently of its interactions with the Standard Model. We study the imprints of long-range forces acting solely in the dark sector on the distribution of galaxies, the so-called Large Scale Structure (LSS). We derive the strongest constraint on such forces from a combination of Planck and BOSS data. Along the way we consistently develop, for the first time, the Effective Field Theory of LSS in the presence of new dynamics in the dark sector. We forecast that future surveys will improve the current bound by an order of magnitude.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 5+18 pages, 4 figures; v2: minor modifications, matches version published in PRL; v3: fixed some coefficients in analytical sub-horizon solutions, all results unaffected

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 25 pages, 8 figures, one new figure and a section added, matches published version in JCAP

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/μ$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 12 pages, 5 tables,1 figure. The version is accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $λ$, $ρ$, and $σ$ Regge trajectories for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ in the triquark-antitriquark picture
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose Regge trajectory relations for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ by using the Regge trajectory relations for diquarks and triquarks. With these newly derived relations, we investigate five series of hexaquark Regge trajectories: the $λ$-, $ρ_1$-, $ρ_2$-, $σ_1$-, and $σ_2$-trajectories. We demonstrate that, apart from the simplest $λ_1$-trajectories, the $ρ_1$-, $ρ_2$-, $σ_1$-, and $σ_2$-trajectories cannot be constructed by merely mimicking the meson Regge trajectories, since mesons possess no internal substructures. To derive these trajectories, one must account for the structure and internal substructure of hexaquark. Without this structural information, the $ρ_1$-, $ρ_2$-, $σ_1$-, and $σ_2$-trajectories could only be obtained through direct fits to available theoretical predictions or future experimental data. We demonstrate that the $ρ_1$-, $ρ_2$-, $σ_1$-, and $σ_2$-trajectories for the hexaquark do not correspond respectively to the Regge trajectories for the triquark, antitriquark, diquark, and antidiquark. Nevertheless, their behaviors match those of the Regge trajectories for the triquark $(\bar{u}(cc))$, the antitriquark $(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))$, the diquark $(cc)$, and the antidiquark $(\bar{b}\bar{b})$, in that respective order. Furthermore, we present rough mass estimates for the excited states corresponding to the $λ$-, $ρ_1$-, $ρ_2$-, $σ_1$-, and $σ_2$-trajectories.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 9 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Parameter dependence of the mapping of the mean-field Ising model onto QCD in the first-order phase transition regime
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We map the mean-field Ising equation of state onto the QCD phase diagram and investigate how scaling parameters alter the metastable and unstable regions, as well as the symmetrized pressure and density along an isotherm on the QCD $T-μ_B$ phase plane. We find that, for both the conventional mapping scheme and the scheme valid in the small-quark-mass limit, increasing the scaling parameters $w$ and $ρ$ narrows the metastable and unstable regions. In the small-quark-mass-limit scheme, larger $w$ and $ρ$ reduce both the Ising-symmetrized pressure and density. For the conventional scheme, increasing $w$ reduces these quantities, while increasing $ρ$ raises the Ising-symmetrized pressure and has only a small effect on the density.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Inelastic Scattering Effects on Attenuation of Boosted Dark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Earth attenuation is crucial for interpreting direct-detection constraints on boosted dark matter (DM), since scatterings with terrestrial nuclei can significantly modify the flux and energy spectrum reaching underground detectors. At boosted energies, inelastic nuclear channels beyond ordinary elastic scattering can become relevant, including quasi-elastic scattering, deep-inelastic scattering, and resonant scattering. In this work, we incorporate the resonant scattering of boosted dark matter (DM) off nuclei into the Earth-attenuation framework, in combination with the elastic, quasi-elastic, and deep-inelastic channels. We find that, in the heavy-mediator regime, resonant scattering can give a non-negligible contribution to the attenuation of boosted DM. Using the latest PandaX-4T data, we derive new constraints on the spin-independent boosted DM-nucleon cross section $\barσ_n$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Multiparameter Quantum Estimation and Degeneracy Structure in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate three-flavor neutrino oscillations within the framework of quantum estimation theory using the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM). We analyze all six independent elements of the QFIM for the parameters $θ_{23}$, $δ_{\mathrm{CP}}$, and $Δm^2_{31}$, together with the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds and normalized parameter correlations. To connect the intrinsic quantum sensitivity of the neutrino state with experimentally accessible information, we further compare the QFI with the classical Fisher information (CFI) associated with flavor-probability measurements. We find that the difference between the quantum and classical information bounds is strongly dependent on the oscillation parameter and $L/E$, demonstrating that the efficiency with which the available quantum information is accessed depends on the measurement. We also investigate probability-degenerate solutions in the $(θ_{23},δ_{\mathrm{CP}})$ parameter space. Although different parameter sets can produce identical $ν_μ\rightarrowν_e$ appearance probabilities at specific $L/E$ values, their corresponding quantum states can remain distinct, as demonstrated by the quantum fidelity. The QFIM differences further reveal distinct local quantum-information geometries for these probability-degenerate solutions, while the corresponding CFIM differences show a parameter and $L/E$ dependent degree of distinguishability accessible through the flavor-probability measurement. Our results demonstrate that QFI and CFI provide complementary information for neutrino parameter estimation, with the QFIM serving as a measurement-independent quantum benchmark and the CFI characterizing the information accessible through a specified measurement.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Beyond Half-Life Limits: Robust Operator-Level Interpretation of Multi-Isotope Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Current and future neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0νββ$) searches are usually characterized by half-life limits or projected sensitivities. For operator-level interpretation, however, the relevant question is not only the strength of the limit, but also the stability of the inferred constraints on low-energy lepton-number-violating (LNV) coefficients under changes of isotope and nuclear matrix-element (NME) method. Using $ν$DoBe, we convert half-life limits or projected sensitivities into limits on low-energy LNV coefficients for several choices of isotope, operator class, and NME method. We then compare the resulting limits across isotopes and NME methods. We quantify the stability by the spread of coefficient limits in non-observation scenarios and, for single-operator post-discovery benchmarks, by the spread of isotope-to-isotope half-life ratios. For the operator examples considered in this paper, the light-Majorana exchange mechanism gives the most stable interpretation. The selected dimension-six operators remain reasonably robust, while the short-range dimension-nine examples show a stronger dependence on isotope and NME-method choices. The same hierarchy appears in post-discovery benchmarks based on isotope-to-isotope half-life ratios: the reliability of such tests depends on whether the predicted half-life pattern remains stable across NME methods. A multi-isotope $0νββ$ program therefore provides information beyond half-life reach by testing the stability of the operator interpretation. This spread-based analysis provides a practical way to identify which low-energy operator scenarios are suitable for isotope-ratio tests after a possible discovery, and which require more care before being connected to ultraviolet models of lepton-number violation.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures and 6 tables. Published in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: New Face of Standard Model: Neutral Magnetic Monopole
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We show that the standard model has a totally new type of monopole which has the neutral magnetic charge $4π/\be$, where $\be$ is the neutral charge. This tells that the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type which has the magnetic charge $4π/e$ and the neutral type which has the neutral magnetic charge $4π/\be$. This necessitates the new neutral charge quantization rule $\be=4πn/\bar g$, in addition to the Dirac's electric charge quantization rule $e=4πn/g$. The mass of the new monopole could be less than the Cho-Maison monopole, around 3.28 TeV. We show how to construct the neutral monopole and clarify the topological origin of the new monopole. We discuss the implications of the new monopoles in physics.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Unfolding the low-energy reactor neutrino flux from CE$ν$NS data with a finite Dirac sum
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present a novel method to analyze coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) data to extract the reactor antineutrino spectrum below the inverse beta decay threshold of 1.8 MeV, where it remains unmeasured. Adapting halo-independent analysis techniques developed for direct dark matter detection, we show how to obtain a best-fit and a pointwise confidence band for the integrated neutrino flux, without assuming a parametric form or smoothness prior for the spectrum. In our approach, which follows from convex geometry arguments, the differential neutrino rate is written as a linear combination of Dirac delta functions -- a finite Dirac sum (FDS) -- with a maximum number of terms determined by the number of data points. We apply our "FDS method" to mock CE$ν$NS data for a low-threshold Ge detector and compare it with Tikhonov-regularized unfolding.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Where to find $X(17)$?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The Atomki group puts forward the hypothesis of an $X(17)$ particle to explain its anomaly observation in ${^{8}\text{Be}^{*}} \to {^{8}\text{Be}} e^+e^-$ transition. Utilizing experimental results from the Atomki experiments, measurements of the electron's anomalous magnetic moment (AMM), the parity-violating Møller scattering experiment, the NA64 experiment, the KLOE-2 experiment, and the PADME experiment, we derive constraints on the $Xee$ coupling of the hypothetical $X(17)$ boson to electrons. A joint $χ^2$ analysis of the electron's AMM (Cs and Rb measurements) and the parity-violating Møller scattering yields two mutually exclusive solutions. The Cs and Rb AMM constraints restrict the combination $(\varepsilon_e^v)^2-5(\varepsilon_e^a)^2$ with opposite signs. Cs+Møller combination favours a dominant axial-vector coupling $|\varepsilon_e^a|\approx5.3\times10^{-4}\gg|\varepsilon_e^v|$, whereas Rb+Møller favours a dominant vector coupling $|\varepsilon_e^v|\approx6.9\times10^{-4}\gg|\varepsilon_e^a|$. The Møller bound suppresses the subdominant coupling for both solutions. Incorporating NA64 and KLOE-2 limits on $(\varepsilon_e^v)^2+(\varepsilon_e^a)^2$ introduces mild tension for the Cs+Møller solution, while the Rb+Møller solution remains nearly unchanged.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: New Bounds on Heavy QCD Axions from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraints on heavy QCD axions. BBN offers a powerful probe of new physics that modifies the neutron-to-proton ratio during the process, thanks to the precisely measured primordial Helium-4 abundance. A heavy QCD axion provides an attractive target for this probe, because not only is it a well-motivated hypothetical particle by the strong CP problem, but also it dominantly decays to hadrons if kinematically allowed. A range of its lifetime is thus excluded where the hadronic decays would significantly alter the neutron-to-proton ratio. We compute axion-induced modification of the neutron-to-proton ratio, and obtain robust upper bounds on the axion lifetimes, as low as 0.017 s for the axion mass higher than 300 MeV. Remarkably, this is stronger than projected future CMB bounds via $N_{\rm eff}$. Our bounds are largely insensitive to uncertainties in hadronic cross sections and the axion's branching fractions into various hadrons, as well as to the precise value of the initial axion abundance. We also incorporate, for the first time, several key improvements, such as scattering processes by energetic $K_L$ and secondary hadrons, that can also be important for studying general hadronic injections during BBN, not limited to those from axion decays.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 25 pages + appendices 35 figures 1 table. v3: corrected errors in the hadronic cross sections in Appendix C.2 and Eq. (C24); Figs. 14-24, 26, and 33 updated. Conclusions unchanged

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: v1:14pp + appendices; AI research protocol available at http://jacomearmas.org/research/BDNK

High Energy Phenomenology.title: CT25: the new generation of CTEQ-TEA PDFs
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This contribution reviews CT25, a new generation of CTEQ--TEA parton distribution functions (PDFs) for precision QCD. With its first member sets released in 2025, the CT25 family addresses common uses of parton distributions in diverse contexts. We describe the CTEQ--TEA Parton Cloud, an online database of exploratory global fits to precision QCD measurements, from which we select PDF solutions for general- and special-purpose calculations. These solutions are published as complementary error PDF ensembles---the baseline CT25, CT25m, CT25pd, and ensembles with conservative priors---optimized for distinct uses. They implement new approaches to quantifying uncertainties and different treatments of theoretical, parametrization, and nuclear-target uncertainties. In particular, they provide complementary frameworks for exploring PDF uncertainties at large partonic momentum fractions relevant to HL-LHC and EIC studies. Further details will appear in the forthcoming CT25 publication.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: The CTEQ-TEA Collaboration. Contribution to the Conference proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026) Affiliation to MSU corrected

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Agentic AI Detector Co-design and Optimization in Vertically Integrated Differentiable Full Simulations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the first implementation of AI agents into the design and optimization of detectors in high-energy physics experiments via a bi-level optimization framework that vertically integrates detector geometry, front-end digitization, and high-level reconstruction algorithm parameters in differentiable full simulations. Using the example of a dual-readout, segmented crystal EM calorimeter with a baseline resolution of $3\%/\sqrt{E}$, we investigate the capabilities and value propositions of AI agents in the identification and reduction of key detector parameters and in the nonlinear traversal of design space. We find that frontier LLM reasoning-models today, without being given additional experiment-specific context, are able to effectively execute complex workflows and proactively suggest generic but relevant avenues for further study or improvement. Here, we demonstrate an AI agent's ability to find an optimal design point amidst three competing performance criteria, showing that effective integration of agents into the complex workflows of frontier research areas can yield higher performance for key physics goals while reducing labor and compute. This study establishes the foundation for a future demonstration of the first fully AI-designed detector for future scientific facilities.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures. Presented at 2026 Stanford Conference on Physics and AI (PAI26)

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Relativistic corrections to heavy quarkonium $+γ$ production at super Z factory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In the framework of nonrelativistic quantum chromodynamics, we study the $\mathcal{O}(v^2)$ relativistic corrections to heavy-quarkonium production associated with a photon at future electron-positron colliders operated in the Z-factory mode. S-, P-, and D-wave heavy quarkonia as well as the mixed state $ψ(3770)$ are considered. We comprehensively investigate tree-level $s$-channel processes for all states, together with $t$-channel contributions that apply only to ${}^3L_1$ states. It is found that the relativistic corrections substantially reduce the LO cross sections for charmonium states by roughly $20\%$-$70\%$, while the reduction is milder for bottomonium, at the level of $10\%$-$30\%$. Event yields for all studied channels are calculated, and sizable event yields are expected for $η_c$, $J/ψ$, $ψ(2S)$, $Υ$, and $ψ(3770)$, especially at FCC-ee.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Fine-Tuning Small Reasoning Models for Quantum Field Theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Despite the growing application of large language models (LLMs) to theoretical physics, there has been little academic exploration of how domain-specific physics reasoning ability develops during training. To investigate this, we perform the first academic comparison of reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for LLMs on verifiable problem-solving tasks in theoretical physics. Because the open-source verifiable training data required to develop such capabilities is scarce, we built a robust data generation pipeline that can both create synthetic problems and make existing human-authored problems suitable for model training. Selecting quantum field theory (QFT) as our primary domain, we generated over 2,500 synthetic problems alongside a curated collection of human-adapted problems sourced from arXiv and standard pedagogical resources. We conduct both reinforcement learning (RL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) experiments, benchmarking performance gains as well as generalization to other physics domains. Although both methods improve over the base model on every dataset, SFT gains are concentrated on in-distribution synthetic tasks, while RL generalizes better, outperforming SFT on the human-adapted datasets and TPBench. We perform an extensive analysis of model chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning before and after fine-tuning to understand how reasoning errors evolve during RL and SFT. Finally, we publicly release our data pipeline, verifiable QFT training data, and ~200M tokens of QFT reasoning traces.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Updating arXiv after publication in IOP Science MLST Journal with minor revisions to the original pre-print

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Scale Anomaly in Supersymmetric Quantum Electrodynamics: Ward Identities, Supersymmetry Breaking, and Decoupling
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study the breaking of the scale symmetry both within classical and quantum frameworks in the supersymmetric quantum electrodynamics (SQED) by applying a four-dimensional regularization that preserves supersymmetry. At the classical level, scale symmetry is shown to be broken by mass terms. At the quantum level, it is demonstrated to be broken by a term proportional to the SQED beta function in the massless limit. It is also shown how this anomaly manifests itself in the low- and high-energy limits and how the Appelquist-Carazzone theorem reproduces the usual quantum electrodynamics result in the limit of heavy selectrons.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Towards anomaly detection searches for new physics signatures including Higgs bosons with weakly supervised machine learning
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The Higgs boson, with its universal coupling to mass, provides a broadly applicable portal to sectors beyond the Standard Model and is therefore a natural anchor for anomaly detection (AD) at collider experiments. The Higgs And X Anomaly Detection (HAXAD) strategy offers a principled approach to searching for such anomalies occurring in association with a Higgs boson by combining machine-learning-based feature embedding, background estimation, and weakly supervised classification. This work extends the previous HAXAD approach towards the level of maturity required for application to recorded collider data. A major addition is the introduction and comparison of two new embedding strategies, which in turn shape the background estimation and classification. In addition, a new inference framework is developed, yielding signal-agnostic and signal-specific cross section limits and thereby completing the statistical machinery needed for future AD analyses built on HAXAD. The set of investigated signal models is also significantly expanded, allowing for the evaluation of sensitivity on a much broader phase space. Improvements to the method increase signal sensitivity with respect to the original method, and when benchmarked against an example cut-based search on the same final state, HAXAD matches or exceeds the best individual cut-based limits for a wide variety of considered signal models. These developments strengthen the case for HAXAD as a viable and compelling AD-based search strategy with novel discovery potential at colliders.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, This version adds model-independent limits as well as links to the used software and dataset

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the $Λ$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $η(z)\equiv D_{\rm L}/[{(1+z)}^2D_{\rm A}]=α{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon\neq0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $Λ$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $Λ$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $Ω_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $η(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $η(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z<0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $α\simeq0.942\pm0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also discuss photon-loss and varying-$G$ interpretations: ordinary positive opacity cannot explain the negative central tilts $\varepsilon$ found for a $Λ$CDM background, while local gravity tests strongly constrain the illustrative unscreened varying-$G$ scenario.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: V2: 16 pages, 5 figures, minor clarifications included. V1: 15 pages, 5 figures. The numerical analysis files for the production of the results and figures of V2 can be found in the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/Rivillion/Sensitivity_test_distance_duality

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Exclusive Determination of $|V_{cb}|$ from Semileptonic Decays $B\to D^{(*)}\ell ν_{\ell}$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present an updated exclusive determination of the CKM matrix element \(|V_{cb}|\) from the semileptonic decays \(B\to D^{(*)}\ell\barν_{\ell}\). Our analysis combines the latest Belle II measurements, updated lattice-QCD calculations of the \(B\to D^{(*)}\) form factors at small hadronic recoil, and correlated large-recoil SCET sum-rule predictions incorporating next-to-leading-order QCD corrections and several power-suppressed contributions. We consider three fit scenarios with progressively enlarged input sets and find that the inclusion of the large-recoil sum-rule constraints substantially reduces the form-factor uncertainties. From the full global fit, we obtain\(|V_{cb}|=(39.18 \pm0.47)\times10^{-3}\). Using the combined lattice-QCD and LCSR fit, we predict \(R(D)=0.3069\pm0.0080,\qquad R(D^*)=0.2548\pm0.0043\), and provide differential decay distributions in the momentum transfer and angular variables for both the muon and tau channels. Comparisons of the individual and correlated predictions for \(R(D)\) and \(R(D^*)\) with the experimental averages reveal a persistent tension. In particular, our theoretical 68\% confidence region shows little overlap with the experimental average. All correlations among the fitted parameters are retained in the uncertainty propagation. Our results therefore provide updated Standard Model benchmarks for tests of lepton-flavor universality. Improved lattice-QCD calculations, sum-rule predictions, and Belle II measurements will be essential for determining whether the remaining discrepancies originate from theoretical systematic uncertainties or from physics beyond the Standard Model.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: The muon collider: expected physics, technological challenges, and the prospects for reusing the 21 km UNK tunnel
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: A multi-TeV muon collider is among the main options for the post-LHC energy frontier. Muons radiate about 10^9 times less synchrotron power than electrons of the same energy, so a compact circular collider could combine the energy reach of a 100 TeV-class proton machine with the clean final states of a lepton collider. This review summarizes the expected physics programme, including Higgs couplings and self-coupling, electroweak and top-quark physics, and searches beyond the Standard Model. It also describes the technological challenges: muon production, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field HTS magnets, the machine-detector interface and the neutrino-flux constraint. None of these technologies has yet been demonstrated at the required performance. Scaling the parameters of the International Muon Collider Collaboration (IMCC), the review examines three ways of reusing the existing 21 km UNK tunnel near Protvino. With the last rapid-cycling synchrotron in the tunnel, the centre-of-mass energy is limited to about 6 TeV. With the collider ring in the tunnel, 11-16 T dipoles give about 14-21 TeV, but the acceleration chain needs a separate 50-73 km tunnel. With both in the tunnel, the reach is about 6-10 TeV at 35-57% of the target luminosity. Non-collider applications of intense muon beams are also discussed.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 40 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. Revised version addressing the referees' comments

High Energy Phenomenology.title: New CP-violating sources beyond the reach of EDMs
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The Standard Model does not contain sufficient amount of CP violation to account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe. Beyond Standard Model scenarios that aim to explain this asymmetry introduce new sources of CP violation, but these generically feed into electric dipole moments (EDMs), which are severely constrained by experiment. We indentify a new class of CP-violating sources that cannot generate EDMs directly: EDM operators are C conserving and P violating, whereas CP violation introduced here is, by construction, C violating and P conserving. We give a concrete model realisation accommodating such sources and discuss their relevance for baryogenesis.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Quark TMDPDFs from Large to Small $x$: A Unified Description of CSS, DGLAP, and Small-$x$ Double Logarithms
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We extend the full-kinematic background-field construction developed for gluon transverse-momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMDPDFs) in Mukherjee et al. [Phys. Rev. D 109, 034035 (2024)] to quark TMDPDFs, providing a common framework for their large- and small-$x$ dynamics. We compute the leading-power quark TMD beam function at next-to-leading order using the background-field method. The background fields retain both longitudinal and transverse momenta, with neither collinear nor eikonal ordering imposed. We distinguish the renormalization scales that define the TMD operator from the factorization scales that separate its perturbative and non-perturbative modes. With standard TMD renormalization, the quark TMDPDF obeys Collins-Soper-Sterman (CSS) evolution, while the lower-scale separation is organized directly in terms of background-field TMD operators. We refer to this full-kinematic construction as the MSTT scheme. In the MSTT scheme, the leading term of the resulting operator expansion reproduces both the Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi (DGLAP) logarithm and the small-$x$ double logarithm in the appropriate limits, while retaining parts of the higher-twist and sub-eikonal corrections. We also formulate a rapidity-only scheme for quark TMDPDFs with distinct renormalization and factorization cutoffs. We derive its evolution equation, which reduces to DGLAP evolution in the collinear limit and to double-logarithmic quark evolution at small $x$, and establish its matching to the MSTT and standard TMD schemes.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The hierarchical assembly of dark matter haloes and galaxies via mergers and anisotropic mass accretion naturally imprints non-trivial velocity anisotropy onto haloes and galaxies, an empirical fact emerging from cosmological simulations.
