In contrast to previous studies, which usually adopt a Gaussian wave function, we obtain the molecular wave function by numerically solving the coupled-channel Schrödinger equation with the one-boson-exchange potential fitted to the mass spectrum of $T_{cc}^+$. The resulting wave function, well described by a Lorentzian in momentum space (a Yukawa-type exponential in coordinate space), is the universal form of a weakly bound $S$-wave molecule and thus more suitable for such a state. As the input of the coalescence model, we use the transverse-momentum distributions of the constituent $D$ and $D^*$ mesons fitted to the ALICE and LHCb data, and also generated by PYTHIA for comparison. We compute the transverse-momentum distributions of $T_{cc}^+$ in $pp$ and Pb-Pb collisions. The resulting spectrum, together with its insensitivity to the binding energy, highlights the universal character of the coalescence production of a weakly bound molecule, which is governed by the long-range tail of the wave function rather than by short-range details. These results provide a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of $T_{cc}^+$.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $B_{sJ}(6114)$ as a Higher-Partial-Wave $\bar{K}^{*}B^{(*)}$ Molecular Candidate
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In 2021, the LHCb Collaboration observed the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ state in the $B^\pm K^\mp$ invariant mass spectrum. It is currently the highest-mass bottom-strange state listed by the Particle Data Group (PDG). However, its spin-parity quantum numbers have not yet been experimentally determined, and its internal structure remains under debate. Although several quark-model interpretations have been proposed, including the $1^3D_1$ state and a member of the $1D(2^-,3^-)$ doublet, the possibility of a hadronic molecular structure for this state has not yet been systematically investigated. We investigate the possibility of interpreting \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) as a \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state within the one-boson-exchange model. By solving the Schrödinger equation using the Gaussian expansion method, we study the bound-state properties with different spin-parity assignments, taking into account partial-wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. We further calculate the strong decay widths into the allowed \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}\) channels and compare them with the experimental data. Our results show that the mass spectrum alone cannot uniquely determine the spin-parity of \(B_{sJ}(6114)\). However, the decay-width analysis disfavors the \(J^P=0^+\), \(0^-\), \(1^+\), \(2^+\), and \(3^-\) assignments, while the \(J^P=1^-\), \(2^-\), and \(3^+\) configurations remain compatible with the experimental constraints. Among these possibilities, the \(J^P=1^-\) assignment provides the best agreement with the measured decay width. These findings suggest that \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) may be a higher-partial-wave \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Magnetic monopoles produced by first-order phase transition
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We present the first 3D lattice simulations of magnetic monopole production from a first-order phase transition, using the Press-Ryden-Spergel method, capturing the subsequent annihilation stage and the entry into the scaling regime in an expanding universe. We establish the quantitative relationship between the initial bubble number and the residual monopole abundance, and calculate the magnetic field and gravitational wave power spectra sourced by monopole dynamics. Crucially, we find that the magnetic field spectrum displays a steep $k^{-5}$ decline beyond the monopole size $w_M$, whereas the peak of the gravitational wave spectrum aligns with the scale of the mean monopole separation $d_M$, governed by $k^3$ and $k^{-3}$ scalings on the low- and high-wavenumber sides of the peak, respectively. However, since the resulting magnetic field strength is excluded by blazar observations, magnetic monopoles cannot be the origin of primordial cosmic magnetic fields. Finally, we determine the allowed monopole mass under the constraints of the Parker bound ($m_M\lesssim2.18\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) and dark matter abundance ($m_M\lesssim1.58\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$).

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Production of excited $Λ_c^+$ baryons through $Λ_b$ hadronic weak decays
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this work, to establish a more abundant $Λ_c$ baryon spectrum, we discuss the production potentials of the excited $Λ_c$ baryons through $Λ_b$ hadronic weak decays within a constituent quark model. Based on our successful explanations of the existing experimental data for the $Λ_b \to Λ_c(π^-, K^{-}, D^{-}, D^{-}_s, D_s^{*-})$ processes, we further calculate the decay rates of the $Λ_b$ baryon into the $1P$-, $1D$-, $2S$-, $3S$-, $2P$-, $1F$-, and $2D$-wave $Λ_c$ excited states. It is found that these $Λ_c$ excitations have large production rates in the $Λ_b$ hadronic weak decay process associated with $π^-$ meson emitting, i.e., $Λ_b\to Λ_c^{*}π^-$, their branching fractions can reach up to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$. To search for the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $1F$-, and $2D$-wave $Λ_c$ states, the $Λ_b \to Λ_c (3S) π^-\to D^{*0}p π^-$, and $Λ_b\to Λ_c(2P,2D,1F) π^-\to D^{(*)0}pπ^-$ decays are worth observing in future experiments.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Heavy Pseudo-Dirac Doublet Dark Matter and Non-Thermal Leptogenesis in Light of the LZ Event
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Motivated by the recent LZ candidate nuclear-recoil event, we study pseudo-Dirac electroweak doublet dark matter in the mass range $10^2$--$10^4\,\mathrm{TeV}$, where bounds from searches for neutrinos produced by dark matter annihilation in the Sun can be evaded. To suppress the excessive thermal relic abundance, we consider freeze-out during inflaton domination followed by entropy production during reheating. We examine whether this cosmological history can also accommodate non-thermal leptogenesis. Our analysis includes dark matter production through the emission of virtual electroweak gauge bosons in right-handed-neutrino decays and through thermalization cascades. Our estimates suggest that the two scenarios can be reconciled if dark matter pair emission in right-handed-neutrino decays is kinematically forbidden and cascade production is sufficiently suppressed. Such a realization, however, requires enhanced CP violation, typically involving fine-tuning in the seesaw mechanism or the right-handed-neutrino mass spectrum.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Spin - resolved momentum distributions and vortex evolution in multiphoton pair production within a modified two-level model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate spin-resolved momentum distributions and phase vortices in multiphoton electron-positron pair production within a modified two-level model. This model retains the diagonal spinor inner-product terms neglected in the adiabatic approximation, thereby inducing spin-resolved transverse asymmetries in the momentum distribution. For a circularly polarized pulse, the handedness determines the winding direction of the quantized vortices, whereas for a linearly polarized pulse, the phase distribution exhibits nodal lines rather than quantized vortices. For two time-delayed circularly polarized pulses, the time delay introduces a relative phase that governs the multiphoton interference, which in turn drives the vortex evolution in each spin configuration. These results demonstrate that pulse polarization and time delay enable coherent control over vortex topology in pair production.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Prompt charmonia hadroproduction in High Energy Factorization with tree-level NLO corrections
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We consider prompt $J/ψ$, $χ_{cJ}$ and $η_c$ production in high energy $pp$ collisions in the framework of non-relativistic QCD. We apply high-energy factorization with taking into account tree-level next-to-leading order corrections to the production amplitudes. Using several CCFM-evolved gluon densities in the proton and a previously proposed matching scheme to merge the leading and higher-order contributions, we extract the long-distance matrix elements for the entire charmonium family from a simultaneous fit to available LHC data. We provide predictions for the transverse momentum spectra and relative production rates $σ(ψ^\prime)/σ(J/ψ)$ and $σ(χ_{cJ})/σ(J/ψ)$ and find them to be in good agreement with the LHC data within the theoretical and experimental uncertainties across a wide kinematic region. We demonstrate that taking into account the tree-level NLO corrections improves the global description of the data.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Mass Spectra of Doubly Heavy Strange baryons $Ω_{QQ^{'}}$ and their Decay properties
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This study investigates baryons $Ω_{cc}$, $Ω_{bc}$ and $Ω_{bb}$ composed of two heavy quarks and one strange light quark, focusing on their radial and excited state mass spectra. We employ the Hyper Central Constituent Quark Model (hCQM), incorporating higher-order corrections, including second-order mass corrections with explicit consideration of spin-dependent interactions. This approach improves the accuracy of spin splitting predictions. Additionally, we present a detailed comparison between our predicted resonance masses and those obtained from other theoretical models. We assign all possible spin-parity quantum numbers, offering a comprehensive understanding of the properties of doubly heavy baryons. Furthermore, we compute key properties such as magnetic moments, transition magnetic moments, radiative decay widths. The analysis also reveals a linear behavior in the Regge trajectories.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Can Mirror Symmetry Challenge Local Realism? Probing Photon Entanglement from Positronium via Compton Scattering
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: This study investigates photon entanglement generated from para-positronium decay by analyzing azimuthal correlations after the double Compton scattering with stationary electrons. We introduce a normalized correlation observable $\mathcal{O}_1 = \cos(2φ_1 - 2φ_2)/C_1$ to witness entanglement. In the absence of decoherence, $\langle\mathcal{O}_1\rangle = -1$, corresponding to a maximally entangled Bell state. With decoherence parameterized by $ρ$, the expectation becomes $-(1-ρ)$, allowing direct experimental quantification of coherence loss. A prior symmetry analysis of the Compton scattering process within the quantum field theory (QFT) is provided, which establishes the mirror-symmetric nature of the single-photon angular distribution. We further examine a local hidden-variable theory (LHVT) under the angular-momentum conservation and the rotation invariance. Imposing the mirror symmetry with respect to the plane defined by the photon spin and momentum leads to a non-negative LHVT prediction for $\langle \sin^2θ_1 \sin^2θ_2 \cos(2φ_1-2φ_2)\rangle$, contradicting the negative QFT prediction value for any $ρ< 1$. Thus, mirror symmetry serves as a novel criterion to exclude LHVT descriptions of the entangled state, whereas without preserving this symmetry, LHVTs can reproduce the correlations.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Measuring Ultralight-Axion Coherence with Galaxy Polarization Correlations
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Ultralight axion-like particles coupled to photons rotate the linear polarization of distant sources. We propose using the three-dimensional two-point correlation of galaxy polarization-rotation angles to measure not only the amplitude of this birefringence field but also its spatial coherence scale. For a nonrelativistic ALP component with an isotropic Gaussian velocity distribution, the equal-time field correlation has an $e^{-1}$ scale $L_{\rm G}^{\rm phys}=\sqrt{6}/(m_a v_a)$, where $v_a$ is the three-dimensional rms ALP velocity dispersion. A detected turnover in the galaxy-pair correlation therefore measures the characteristic momentum scale $m_a v_a$, while the correlation amplitude constrains $g_{aγ}\sqrt{Ω_a/Ω_{\rm DM}}$. For a fiducial survey with $10^6$ polarized galaxies over a quarter of the sky to $z=2$ and effective per-galaxy scatter $σ_{\rm tot}=10^\circ$, we find $5σ$ sensitivity to sub-degree correlated rotations over $m_a(10^{-3}c/v_a)\sim10^{-29}$--$10^{-27}\,{\rm eV}$, with $σ[\log_{10}(m_a v_a)]\lesssim0.1$ for detected signals across much of this range. This provides a geometric late-time probe complementary to CMB birefringence and structure-formation constraints.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: The author is withdrawing this manuscript because its key predictions, namely a 5σ detection and a 0.1 dex precision constraint on ultralight axion coherence, cannot be adequately substantiated under realistic observational conditions. These predictions rely on idealized assumptions, and the calculations do not provide sufficient support for the claimed observational sensitivity

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the radiative decays $χ_{bJ}\to J/ψ+γ$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization, we calculate the next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to $χ_{bJ}\to J/ψ+γ$ with $J=0,1,2$. We determine all six independent helicity amplitudes, including the one-loop corrections to the QED amplitude and the two-loop corrections to the QCD amplitude, and retain the interference between the QED and QCD amplitudes in the decay widths. The NLO corrections substantially enhance the $χ_{b0}$ and $χ_{b1}$ decay widths, while reducing the $χ_{b2}$ decay width by approximately $36\%$. Including the QED amplitude leads to sizable destructive interference for $χ_{b0}$ and an enhancement for $χ_{b2}$, but has only a small effect on the $χ_{b1}$ decay width. Two treatments of photon fragmentation, based on the NRQCD matrix element and the experimentally determined $J/ψ$ decay constant, yield NLO unpolarized decay widths that agree at the few percent level or better. Using the decay constant scheme at $μ_R=m_b$, we obtain NLO central branching fractions of $1.03\times10^{-6}$, $1.45\times10^{-5}$, and $1.99\times10^{-6}$ for the three channels, respectively. The NLO corrections reduce the renormalization scale dependence, particularly for $χ_{b2}$, although a sizable dependence remains for $χ_{b0}$. At fixed $m_b$, the branching fractions decrease with increasing $r=m_c/m_b$, more strongly for $χ_{b1}$ and $χ_{b2}$ than for $χ_{b0}$. For $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=14\,{\rm TeV}$ and an integrated luminosity of $100\,{\rm fb}^{-1}$, we estimate about $1.9\times10^4$ and $4.8\times10^4$ $\ell^+\ell^-γ$ events from $χ_{b0}$ and $χ_{b2}$ decays, respectively. Measurements with the existing Belle $Υ(2S)$ sample remain challenging because of the small expected yields. A larger $Υ(2S)$ sample at Belle II would improve the prospects for observing these radiative decays.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Anatomy of RHN DM relic in the vanilla scotogenic neutrino mass model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The scotogeneic neutrino mass models are very popular choices to generate light neutrino masses via radiative mechanism. In these models, the particles running in the loop are distinguished from the standard model due to an imposed $\mathcal{Z}_2$ symmetry under which the loop particles are odd. Therefore, the lightest particle running in the loop can be a viable dark matter candidate. In this paper, we revisit the minimal scotogenic neutrino mass model and study the anatomy of right handed neutrino (RHN) DM relic, taking into account contributions from self-annihilation, co-annihilation, conversion-driven processes, as well as production via the freeze-in mechanism. We impose the constraints from direct detection and collider searches of DM including anomalous magnetic moment of muon, charged lepton flavor violation and low-energy neutrino oscillation data to show that the lightest RHN can be a viable DM in the mass range: $M_{h}/2\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim2000 {\rm GeV}$ (thermal DM) and $0.1 ~{\rm GeV}\lesssim M_{\rm DM}\lesssim 1000 {\rm GeV}$ (non-thermal DM), where $M_h$ denotes the Standard Model Higgs mass and $M_{\rm DM}$ is the RHN dark matter mass. We also find the displaced vertex signatures of long lived particles which can be probed at future colliders.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Orbital angular momentum at small $x$ in the large $N_c\&N_f$ limit
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We extend the small-$x$ analysis of the quark and gluon orbital angular momentum (OAM) distributions in the proton from the large-$N_c$ limit considered in our earlier works to the large-$N_c\&N_f$ limit, in which the numbers of quark colors $N_c$ and flavors $N_f$ are large with their ratio held fixed. Working in the double-logarithmic approximation (DLA), summing powers of $α_s \ln^2(1/x)$ with $α_s$ the strong coupling and $x$ the proton's momentum fraction carried by a parton, we correct the small-$x$ operator expression for the quark OAM distribution suggested earlier in \cite{Kovchegov:2024wjs} and relate both the quark and gluon OAM distributions to the impact-parameter moments of the polarized dipole amplitudes. We derive the large-$N_c\&N_f$ evolution equations for these moment amplitudes in the DLA; these include a new equation for the moment amplitude governing the quark OAM. We then solve these evolution equations numerically together with the helicity evolution for $N_f = 2,3,4,5,6$ and $N_c =3$. We find that, similar to the large-$N_c$ case, the OAM distributions share a common small-$x$ intercept with the helicity distributions, $L_{q+\bar{q}}(x,Q^2) \sim L_G(x,Q^2) \sim ΔΣ(x,Q^2) \sim ΔG(x,Q^2) \sim \left(\frac{1}{x} \right)^{α_h}$ with the intercept $α_h \approx {3.48 \sqrt{α_s N_c/2π}}$ for $N_f = N_c = 3$ (cf.~\cite{Borden:2025ehe}): this result, along with $α_h$ for other values of $N_f \neq 0$ that we studied, is smaller than the intercept of $3.66\sqrt{α_s N_c/2π}$ found in the large-$N_c$ limit. We also compute the ratios of the OAM distributions to the helicity parton distribution functions as $x\to 0$, obtaining $L_{q+\bar{q}}(x,Q^2)/ΔΣ(x,Q^2) = -1$ and $L_G(x,Q^2)/ΔG(x,Q^2) = -2$ at $Q^2=10\, \mathrm{GeV}^2$, with both ratios being independent of $N_f$.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 47 pages, 6 figures; v2: 48 pages, 6 figures, minor corrections; v3: minor minus signs and factors of 2 corrected which caused minor corrections to the ratios. This paper is the first one in a two-paper sequence: the second paper will employ the formalism developed here to perform a feasibility study of measuring quark and gluon OAM distributions at the future Electron--Ion Collider (EIC)

High Energy Phenomenology.title: 8-type electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We consider electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory with scalar fields in the fundamental representation, for an electric field in the $λ_8$ direction (8-type). In temporal gauge, the 3-type electric field rotates within a single SU(2) subgroup at one frequency, whereas the 8-type electric field necessarily rotates within three SU(2) subgroups with at least two different frequencies. We construct the homogeneous 8-type electric field with three scalar fields and show that two scalar fields are sufficient only on a one-parameter family of gauge field backgrounds. Like the 3-type field, the homogeneous 8-type field is immune to decay through Schwinger pair production of gauge bosons. We then construct an 8-type electric string solution in temporal gauge. Its electric field is of 8-type on the string axis and, unlike the 3-type string, the string is only net color neutral, which results in a weak radial electric field.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Ancillary files contain the string profile functions and scripts that check the solutions

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Reformulation of the pionless effective field theory for practical few- and many-body applications
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The effective field theory (EFT) of contact forces which describes few-nucleon systems at distance scales larger than the pion Compton wavelength ${\rm EFT}({π\hskip-0.54em /})$ can be defined in terms of momentum-dependent potentials that contain a fixed number of simple poles and generate the effective-range expansion to a given fixed order. These potentials provide a practical generalization of the standard ${\rm EFT}({π\hskip-0.54em /})$ power-counting scheme which, for instance, naturally accounts for the large effective ranges in the s-wave channels. Nucleon-nucleon phase shifts computed in this formulation of ${\rm EFT}({π\hskip-0.54em /})$ are compared to modern phase-shift analyses, and effective-range parameters are tabulated. The ${\rm EFT}({π\hskip-0.54em /})$ potentials, which provide a rational approximation of the S-matrix, are easily extended into the regime of pion physics through the inclusion of additional S-matrix poles and zeros, and provide an accurate description of data up to pion-production threshold. The potentials in this scheme are in an important sense weak over all relevant distance scales, and are therefore of utility for systematic calculations of many-nucleon observables.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Low Primordial Helium as a Probe of Non-Unitary Neutrino Mixing
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The EMPRESS collaboration has reported a primordial helium mass fraction \(Y_P = 0.2402 \pm 0.0040\), which lies more than \(1σ\) below the standard Big Bang Nucleosynthesis prediction. Combined with the deuterium abundance and the Planck baryon density, this corresponds to a mild \(\sim 2σ\) tension with the standard value of the effective number of relativistic species, or to a \(\sim 2σ\) indication of a non-zero electron-neutrino degeneracy. We show that it can be explained by non-unitary three-neutrino mixing, a generic feature of seesaw extensions of the Standard Model. Non-unitarity makes the Fermi constant in beta decay exceed that in muon decay, enhancing the neutron-to-proton conversion rate and lowering \(Y_P\). A full numerical BBN calculation, combined with the EMPRESS \(Y_P\) determination and the deuterium abundance gives the best fit point at \(α_{22}=0.982\), while the standard values \(N_{\mathrm{eff}}=3.044\), \(ξ_e=0\) remain allowed; the required level of non-unitarity is consistent with current experimental constraints.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: What if dark matter is composite of least interacting particles?
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: In this work, we investigate the possibility that Dark Matter contains particles that interact with known matter only through gravity, the least interacting particles (LIPs). Specifically, we consider the case of a dark Proca vector field, which does not mix in the kinetic term with any of the vector bosons of the Standard Model if a discrete symmetry (Z2 ) is imposed. Breaking this symmetry introduces kinetic mixing. Here, we study two realization mechanisms, namely kinetic mixing with the electromagnetic field after electroweak symmetry breaking (Scenario A) and kinetic mixing with the weak hypercharge gauge field (Scenario B). We also consider generalized kinetic terms that violate parity and time-reversal symmetries.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Localized Neutrinos in Two Dark Dimensions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study neutrino masses in a six-dimensional framework with two compact dark dimensions. In the conventional flat-bulk realization, the sterile-neutrino zero mode is strongly volume suppressed, so a fundamental scale near $10~\mathrm{TeV}$ requires a large higher-dimensional Yukawa coupling to reproduce the observed neutrino masses, while the accompanying two-dimensional Kaluza--Klein tower is strongly constrained by oscillation data. We show that localizing the sterile-neutrino wave function near the Standard-Model brane substantially alleviates both effects. Using a Gaussian localizer, realistic Dirac neutrino masses are obtained with perturbative, order-one Yukawa couplings, while the brane-visible sterile excitations form a shell spectrum with $M_s^2=8μ^2 s$, and squared active--sterile mixings that decrease as $1/s$. The localization scale therefore separates the experimentally relevant sterile-neutrino spectrum from the gravitational compactification scale. We derive the resulting three-flavour structure and study its phenomenological consequences for reactor oscillations and tritium beta decay, including comparisons with current flat-LED and KATRIN constraints.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Understanding Big Bang Nucleosynthesis: the physics and its history
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Big-bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) is a pillar of modern cosmology. It was the first major test of the hot big bang model, and today remains its earliest and most precise test. It all began with the trailblazing 1948 paper of Alpher, Bethe and Gamow, who proposed non-equilibrium nuclear processes in the early Universe and an early radiation-dominated phase to explain the abundances of all the chemical elements in the periodic table. While their neutron-capture model was deeply flawed, it initiated the path to the modern theory of BBN and the discovery of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). In this paper I clarify the basic physics of BBN, adding some new insights, and describe how the modern theory developed. I finish with a discussion of the pre-discovery predictions of the temperature of CMB, including the missteps and the missed opportunities. The legacy of big bang nucleosynthesis is enormous, and it is yet another illustration of how foggy it can be at the frontiers of discovery.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: Significantly revised for submission to European Physical Journal H. Content is largely the same; presentation changes reflect valuable comments from colleagues

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Same Events, Weaker Bound: Model Dependence in Magellanic Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: OGLE microlensing of the Magellanic Clouds sets the leading bounds on primordial black holes (PBHs) as dark matter from $10^{-8}$ to $10^{3}\,M_\odot$. Holding the detected events and survey efficiencies fixed, we show that changes to the Milky Way halo, the stellar lens populations and the Large Magellanic Cloud halo, each motivated by recent data, weaken the published strict 20-year bound by up to $\simeq6$, and by over an order of magnitude in an extreme stress test. With primordial clustering, the planetary-mass bound weakens by a factor $3.4$--$6$. We strongly recommend that compact-object dark matter limits be quoted together with their modeling assumptions and, generally, be derived under conservative assumptions.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 9 pages with 3 figures, comments very welcome

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Crowdsourcing Gravitational Waves from Superradiant Axions
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Black hole superradiance is a powerful probe of ultralight axions. If nature contains a boson with a mass of order $10^{-12}\,$eV, $\textit{mere vacuum fluctuations}$ will lead to its efficient production around spinning stellar mass black holes, forming a gravitational atom that both drains the black hole spin and decays to produce near-monochromatic gravitational waves. Existing superradiance constraints derive primarily from spin measurements of a handful of identified black holes. Here we instead present a detailed study of the population level effect: gravitational waves arising from both the 100 million black holes in the Milky Way and the stochastic signal from axion clouds throughout the universe. We study the impact of a broad range of systematic uncertainties on the black hole properties and compute the projected axion sensitivity for LIGO, as well as the future instruments Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer, and a high-frequency Magnetic Weber Bar. We demonstrate that LIGO can robustly probe axion masses from roughly $10^{-13}\,$eV to $4 \times 10^{-12}\,$eV. If the black hole population extends to masses slightly below $5\,M_{\odot}$ - as hinted for by LIGO inspiral observations - LIGO would approach $10^{-11}\,$eV. Under that same assumption we show that a future high-frequency detector could push considerably higher, potentially beyond $10^{-10}\,$eV in the most optimistic scenarios, reaching towards the lowest masses within the projected sensitivity of axion dark matter searches.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Hadronisation of in-medium $c\bar c$ pairs to the exotic $X(3872)$
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The production ratios of hidden-charm hadrons observed in nuclear collisions reflect the degree of separation that the precursor $c\bar c$ pair develops inside the quark-gluon plasma. The respective hadronisation amplitude manifests this relation through the position-space inner products of the in-medium and in-vacuum $c\bar c$ wave functions. The exotic $X(3872)$, whose structure accommodates a dominant loosely bound molecular component together with a smaller compact component, stands as a novel hard probe of this spatial dependence. In this Letter, relative production measurements of $J/ψ$, $ψ(2S)$ and $X(3872)$ hadrons performed by the LHC collaborations are understood through the spatial dispersion of in-medium charm anti-charm systems.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Excited States Of Positronium From The Two Body Dirac Equations Of Constraint
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The binding energies of the excited states of positronium are calculated using the two body Dirac equations of constraint formalism. The results from nonperturbative evaluation are compared to those from perturbative evaluation. Explicit forms of the coupled equations are presented in addition to the decoupled equations. The equations for decoupled sates with J=0 are compared to an alternate formulation of the model. Some misprints in the literature are identified and corrected.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 29 pages, 6 figures, 12 tables, minor updates, to appear

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Gravitational Waves From an Entangled SO(3) Cosmic String Network
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Discrete non-Abelian symmetries such as $\mathrm{A_4}$ are widely used in models of lepton flavor to explain neutrino mass hierarchy and their large mixing. If such a symmetry arises from the spontaneous breaking of a continuous group, cosmic strings can form. We study the breaking $\mathrm{SO}(3)\to \mathrm{A_4}$, for which the strings are classified by the non-Abelian group $π_1(\mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{A_4})\cong \mathrm{T}'$, the binary tetrahedral group. Because the string fluxes do not commute, colliding strings may reconnect, pass through each other, or become joined by a bridge whose flux can belong to a different string network. We derive the probabilities of these outcomes directly from the group structure; in network models they are usually treated as free parameters. Including them in a multi-network velocity-dependent one-scale model, we find that the correlation length of the networks decreases and their energy density increases relative to Abelian $\mathrm{U}(1)$ strings of the same tension. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background is enhanced by up to nearly three orders of magnitude, showing that the algebraic structure of $π_1$ leaves a direct imprint on the gravitational-wave spectrum.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2θ_{23}$, $Δm^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $δ_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Top quark differential distributions in the SMEFT
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We discuss top quark processes, in particular $tW$ production and top-antitop pair production, as probes of dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). We calculate top-quark double differential distributions in transverse momentum and rapidity, and we perform SMEFT fits at LO, NLO and, by adding second-order soft-gluon corrections, at approximate NNLO.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; presented at ICHEP 2026, 30 July - 5 August 2026, Natal, Brazil

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Spin correlations in the $τ$-lepton pair in polarized electron-positron annihilation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Possible anomalous New Physics contributions to dipole and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton rise considerable interest in theoretical and experimental studies of the $τ$-pair production in electron-positron annihilation and in proton-proton collisions at the LHC. In the present paper we discuss and calculate the spin-correlation matrix in the $e^+ e^- \to τ^+ τ^-$, and in general $f \bar{f} \to τ^+ τ^-$ processes, including New Physics contributions to the $γττ$ and $Z ττ$ vertices and longitudinally polarized beams of initial fermions. The $τ$ decays are included as well. This work is an upgrade of our previous studies of the spin correlations in the $ττ$ system produced in the processes with unpolarized initial fermions ($e^- e^+$ and $q\bar{q}$). A corresponding numerical code is developed. Brief information on how to use and configure the MC programs with a new subroutine is also given.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: axionbloch: an Open-Source Python Package for Simulating Axion-Induced Spin Dynamics
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: The interaction of ultralight bosonic dark matter with spins can be interpreted as a pseudomagnetic field acting on normal matter. Such interactions can be modeled as usual magnetic interactions using spin-evolution (Bloch) equations. axionbloch, an open-source Python package for simulating spin dynamics induced by both usual and exotic interactions, is presented. The numerical simulations serve as a tool for deriving axion signal signatures, which are crucial for designing experimental searches and data analysis. Simulations are calibrated against theoretical expectations, ensuring the accuracy of the simulated signals. axionbloch is available at https://github.com/Yuzhe98/AxionBloch, allowing researchers to simulate pseudomagnetic signals under specific configurations of the axion models and experimental setups. The package is documented at http://axionbloch.readthedocs.io/ and includes example scripts for application.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of dipole-charged fields in the Proca theory
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We discuss the dynamics of field configurations encoded in the certain class of electric (magnetic) dipole-charged states in the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. We construct such states so as to ensure that the long distance structure of the mean electromagnetic field in them is initially set by the formula describing the electromagnetic field of the electric (magnetic) dipole. We analyze then how such a mean electromagnetic field evolves in time. We find that far away from the center of the initial field configuration, the long range component of the mean electromagnetic field harmonically oscillates, which leads to the phenomenon of the periodic oscillations of the electric (magnetic) dipole moment. We also find that near the center of the initial field configuration, the mean electromagnetic field escapes from its initial arrangement and a spherical shock wave propagating with the speed of light appears in the studied system. A curious configuration of the axisymmetric mean electric field is found to accompany the mean magnetic field in magnetic dipole-charged states.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Symmetry-Preserving and Scalable Variational Circuits for the Lattice Gross-Neveu Model
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study variational preparation of ground states and sector-resolved excited states in the $(1+1)$-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model. We construct fixed circuits preserving either total fermion number or every flavor number, and a problem-specific scalable-circuit adaptive variational quantum eigensolver (SC-ADAPT-VQE). Classical circuit benchmarks cover massless and massive systems through 30 qubits, using exact-diagonalization and tensor-network reference results. Imposing flavor-number conservation improves the achieved energies in the completed two-flavor comparisons. Selected massive fixed-ansatz benchmarks with one to four flavors have relative energy errors of approximately $1 \times 10^{-5}$ - $2 \times 10^{-4}$, smaller than the quoted literature errors where available, although discretizations and computational resources differ. The adaptive pool combines translated bulk and boundary-sensitive generators with an interaction-sensitive cross-flavor family. Selected massive SC-ADAPT benchmarks with one to three flavors have relative energy errors below $2.1 \times 10^{-3}$. For one flavor, matrix-product-state evaluations extend the transferred circuits to 60-400 qubits without target-side operator selection or parameter optimization, giving energy deviations of approximately $0.35\%$ - $1.76\%$ from density-matrix renormalization-group reference values at maximum bond dimension 256. At fixed flavor number, range caps, and append count, the adaptive construction has a precompilation local-factor count linear in volume and a volume-independent shared-parameter count; fixed-accuracy performance at arbitrary volumes remains unestablished. Sequential deflation also prepares low-lying states within a fixed flavor-number sector, with projector fidelities providing a basis-independent assessment of degenerate target eigenspaces.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Variable-phase methods and data for long-range scattering
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Long-range interactions play an important role in dark-matter phenomenology, affecting the relic abundance, indirect-detection signals, and structure formation on galactic scales. Reliable predictions often require nonperturbative solutions of the Schrödinger equation over broad parameter ranges and many partial waves. We present a numerical framework based on the variable-phase method, which recasts the radial Schrödinger equation as a system of first-order equations and allows both regular and irregular solutions to be computed efficiently. The former determine phase shifts and Sommerfeld factors, while the latter provide additional information relevant for the self-consistent unitarization of contact-like inelastic interactions. We discuss the numerical implementation, integration-domain selection, partial-wave convergence, and comparisons with analytic limits. We release the code together with tables for the Yukawa potential containing phase shifts, Sommerfeld factors, elastic and angularly weighted cross sections, and the irregular-solution information relevant for unitarization. These resources facilitate dark-matter studies without requiring repeated computationally intensive scans.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 48 pages, 13 figures; for the associated code and instructions for accessing the data, see https://github.com/mmfloresnm/YukawaVPS

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections. Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $φ$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_φ$, the decay $N\toνφ$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $φ\toγγ$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: $γ$hosts from the past: reheating neutron stars with supernova-sourced ALPs
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can be copiously produced in the hot and dense environment of a core-collapse supernova. If their mass is within an order of magnitude of the supernova temperature, a non-negligible fraction of them will remain gravitationally bound to the neutron star remnant. This basin of ALPs can then decay to photons over the lifetime of the neutron star, thereby reheating it. Using the measured luminosities of several neutron stars, we close multiple windows in ALP parameter space while also satisfying the SN 1987A cooling constraint on the ALP-nucleon coupling. In particular, using the 35000 K upper limit on the temperature of the coldest neutron star observed, PSR J2144$-$3933, we derive the strongest upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling for 1$-$400 MeV ALP masses. Ceilings on these limits arising from ALP decays occurring within the neutron star lifetime may be overcome by using younger neutron stars such as the one in Cas A, probing couplings orders of magnitude higher. Observations of a $2000 \, {\rm K}$-hot neutron star in infrared observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope could reach ALP-photon couplings three orders lower and ALP masses one order lower than our current limits.
High Energy Phenomenology.comment: 6 pages + references, 4 figures, 1 table. Comments are welcome

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Continuous Measurement of Quantum Axion Dark Matter
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We provide a fully quantum-mechanical description of the continuous measurement of wavelike dark matter. Our focus is cavity haloscopes, although our results inform a broad range of axion searches. We extend the input-output formalism by treating the axion as a quantum field, finding how its quantum state is imprinted onto higher-order moments of observables of the outgoing transmission-line modes. We further develop a novel measurement-record formalism, which computes the joint probability distribution of all measurement outcomes and is well suited to studying the axion in the time domain. With it, we compute the exact axion-induced number distribution for the first time, demonstrating that it is not Poisson. We argue that virialized axion dark matter is expected to be in a Gaussian quantum state, and show that number or quadrature measurements can distinguish this from the predictions of a coherent state or even a Bose-Einstein condensate. Finally, we show that intrinsically quantum effects, such as those from Fock or squeezed axion states, are far too weak to detect.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Sequential SBI for Resonance Searches at the LHC
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Neural simulation-based inference has been shown to extract significantly more information from LHC data than histogram-based analyses. So far, it has mostly been applied to couplings, for which the polynomial structure of the scattering amplitude can be exploited. Masses and widths instead move and deform the signal in phase space, and learning their likelihood requires many event samples covering the continuous theory parameter space. We show how sequential simulation-based inference can address this by iteratively concentrating the simulations where the observed data points. Using a parton-level example with an exact reference likelihood and reconstruction-level analyses of $A\to ZH\to \ell\ell b\bar b$ and $Y\to HH\to (t\bar t)(t\bar t)$, we demonstrate that sequential training produces significantly more accurate and better calibrated likelihoods than single round training with the same amount of training events.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Faithful Uncertainties in ML-Based Inverse Problems: GPs, NNs and NTKs for the Triplet PDF
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Machine-learning methods are increasingly used to solve inverse problems in physics, where a faithful estimate of the uncertainty on the reconstructed function is as important as its central value. We address this question in the simplest instance of a parton distribution function (PDF) determination: the reconstruction of the non-singlet triplet distribution $T_3(x,Q_0^2)$ from deep-inelastic scattering data. Within a closure-test framework, in which the underlying PDF is known and the pseudo-data carry correlated experimental uncertainties, we compare Gaussian processes with different kernels, neural-network ensembles trained with different loss functions, and empirical neural tangent kernel approximations. We find that methods yielding comparable central reconstructions can produce markedly different uncertainties, and we identify the ingredients that control them: a likelihood that includes the full experimental covariance, the functional prior encoded in the kernel or in the endpoint preprocessing, and, for tangent-kernel approximations, the stage of training at which the kernel is evaluated. A normalised-bias diagnostic shows that calibration depends on the correlations of the predictive covariance, not only on its pointwise width. Our results illustrate why closure tests and covariance-aware diagnostics are essential to validate uncertainties in ML-based approaches to inverse problems.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing Heavy Neutral Leptons through New Gauge Interactions at the Forward Physics Facilities
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We investigate the prospects for improving the heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at the far-forward LHC experiments FASER and FASER$ν$, as well as their proposed HL-LHC successors, FASER2 and FASER$ν$2, using new HNL production mechanisms. We consider scenarios in which HNLs couple directly to a new $U(1)$ gauge boson and decay into visible Standard Model final states through mixing with active neutrinos. Focusing on the $U(1)_{B-L}$, $U(1)_{B-3L_τ}$, and $U(1)_B$ gauge extensions as benchmark models, we study HNL production through proton bremsstrahlung and Drell--Yan processes, which probe complementary mediator-mass regimes. We analyze several visible decay channels, including charged leptons, neutral mesons, and other hadrons, and evaluate the projected sensitivities for different neutrino-flavor mixing patterns. We find that these new production mechanisms that differ qualitatively from the conventional picture in which both production and decay are controlled by active-sterile mixing enable the far-forward LHC program to probe previously unexplored regions of HNL parameter space, with the first-ever demonstration of FASER$ν$ having sensitivity to HNLs and FASER2 and FASER$ν$2 offering substantially enhanced sensitivity during the HL-LHC era, even reaching the canonical seesaw prediction for all three lepton flavors. Our results demonstrate that new gauge interactions can substantially enhance HNL production independently of the active-sterile mixing that governs their visible decays, opening complementary opportunities to explore HNLs at the forward physics facilities.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Probing imperfect axions with nuclear clocks
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We show that $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks can probe departures from the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) solution to the strong CP problem. Explicit PQ breaking or additional CP-violating interactions can shift the minimum of the axion potential and generate CP-violating couplings to matter, inducing a clock response linear in the axion field. We investigate explicit PQ breaking and quark chromo-electric dipole operators as representative realizations of these \textit{imperfect axion} scenarios, consistent with electric dipole moment constraints. For axion dark matter, the linear signal oscillates at the Compton frequency and can dominate the quadratic response. Even without axion dark matter, the Earth can source a static axion field, enabling fifth-force searches with nuclear clocks.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: General-purpose equations of state for hadron-quark matter: first application to accretion-induced phase transitions in neutron stars
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Strong first-order phase transitions in the cores of neutron stars (NSs) can have profound implications for astrophysical observables, however, their existence remains an open question. Since most NSs form in binary systems, they are expected to experience prolonged episodes of mass accretion that gradually increase their central density and can potentially trigger such a transition. This might, in turn, generate observable multi-messenger signals, as suggested by previous studies. Motivated by this prospect, we generate a new set of equations of state for hadron--quark matter with first-order phase transitions of various strengths, including neutrino absorption opacities in the quark phase as well. We then perform general-relativistic radiation hydrodynamics simulations of NSs undergoing accretion-induced phase transitions. In contrast to previous findings, our results indicate that these systems do not produce unbound ejecta for the models considered, making accretion-induced phase transitions unlikely sources of observable electromagnetic transients. However, we find that transitions are accompanied by intense neutrino emission, with peak luminosities reaching $\sim10^{52}~\mathrm{erg/s}$ for the strongest transition considered. To facilitate future numerical studies, we make the family of equations of state and neutrino opacities used in this work publicly available, enabling the systematic exploration of the role of the phase transition strength.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

High Energy Phenomenology.title: Meson-isospectral pair interactions and the residual three-quark force
High Energy Phenomenology.summary: Meson-isospectral pair rotations can closely reproduce low-lying baryon energies while producing a substantial connected action under their consistent three-body embedding. Starting from an independently calibrated S-wave meson model, we compare ground-mass fits, joint ground-level and gap fits, and direct minimization of the connected remainder. With eighteen shared coefficients, a four-packet joint fit reproduces the nine calibration ground masses and first gaps with RMS errors of $\JointGroundTrain$ and $\JointGapTrain$ MeV, respectively. The excluded ground masses and gaps have RMS errors of $10.7$ and $8.1$ MeV in the same enlarged radial space. Its connected action on the eighteen calibrated inputs is $\JointActionCal$ times the unrotated source action. Eigenvalue agreement and removal of the connected interaction thus impose different tests. Separately optimizing the action with five packets gives a normalized residual of $\ShortActionAll$ for an intermediate-distance fifth packet; a long-distance extension also leaves a substantial remainder. An eliminated-state construction realizes the central color--color structure of an intermediate-configuration mechanism together with correlated pair dressing. These results favor a connected operator basis with three fitted strengths as an economical description within the tested pair family, and quantify its relation to the representation freedom of equivalent few-body Hamiltonians.

High Energy Theory.title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
High Energy Theory.summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. Solving wave equations of bulk fields with different spins outside the black brane, we calculate exponentially small contributions to retarded Green's functions in the dual CFT at large real frequency. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

High Energy Theory.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity, with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating operator product coefficients. Our construction starts from compact regions assembled from generalized hyperbolic tetrahedra. We analytically continue the gravitational amplitudes computed from these triangulations to de Sitter parameters and use them to infer OPE correlations. We recover matching normalized amplitudes from a complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction. A non-Gaussian fourth moment encodes the hyperbolic core volume in an oscillatory semiclassical phase. We construct the associated Lorentzian de Sitter spacetime and show that derivatives of this phase recover its boost holonomies. Its spacelike future boundary carries a positive-definite conformal metric, while the wavefunction obeys Euclidean conformal Ward identities. These relations connect the proposed OPE statistics to both the Euclidean boundary description and the Lorentzian bulk geometry. Integrating the absolute square of the cosmological wavefunction over boundary moduli gives cosmological observables. Their long-collar factorization reproduces the edge measure of the two-matrix model.

High Energy Theory.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
High Energy Theory.summary: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

High Energy Theory.title: AnyonWiki.org
High Energy Theory.summary: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.
High Energy Theory.comment: 10 pages, for the associated website see https://anyonwiki.org/

High Energy Theory.title: Inaccessibility of the Cosmological Singularity to Quantum Probes
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose an operational resolution of the FLRW big bang singularity using quantum probes satisfying a curvature coupled Klein-Gordon equation. Applying the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of a Klein-Gordon field on a classical near-singularity FLRW background, we show that the induced conformal geometry renders curvature invariants finite and makes past directed causal geodesics complete. The classical big bang surface is therefore inaccessible to this class of quantum probes in finite effective proper time, while the underlying FLRW spacetime remains singular.

High Energy Theory.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
High Energy Theory.summary: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

High Energy Theory.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
High Energy Theory.summary: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

High Energy Theory.title: Local tests of Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime
High Energy Theory.summary: We study weak field local tests of Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime, which describes a static black hole embedded in an external magnetic field. Perihelion precession, deflection of light rays and time delay of radar echoes are the phenomena considered in this work to understand the possible effects of this external magnetic field on these observationally important tests. We not only derive weak field analytical results by employing appropriate methods, but also consider an exact approach to directly integrate the relevant geodesic equations, to both confirm those weak field analytical results and to obtain results beyond the weak field approximation.

High Energy Theory.title: Gravitational Waves from New Inflation
High Energy Theory.summary: Gravitational waves provide one of the most powerful observational probes for discriminating among inflationary models. In particular, it has recently become clear that the high-frequency gravitational-wave spectrum encodes a wealth of information about the properties of the inflaton and the post-inflationary dynamics. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive prediction of the complete gravitational-wave spectrum in the new inflation scenario, a prototypical realization of small-field inflation, incorporating all known production mechanisms including both the classical and quantum sources.

High Energy Theory.title: Carrollian Symmetries and Dynamical Entropy
High Energy Theory.summary: Carrollian geometry has recently emerged as the proper language to understand the geometry of null hypersurfaces from an intrinsic perspective. In this paper, we demonstrate that the Noether charge associated with the intrinsic conformal symmetry of Carrollian manifolds yields exactly the dynamical entropy formula recently proposed by Hollands, Wald and Zhang. This result follows directly from the requirement that the gravitational phase space induced on a finite distance null hypersurface be anomaly-free, in a covariant phase space sense. We then show that a linearized perturbation of this dynamical entropy charge, sourced by an external matter perturbation falling across the hypersurface, satisfies a physical process first law. Moreover, upon imposing the classical null energy condition, a linearized second law holds for the dynamical entropy. We then turn to a semi-classical generalization of this construction, where we argue that a notion of dynamical generalized entropy follows from considering perturbations sourced by external quantum matter. By imposing the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), we find a generalized second law for a linearized perturbation of the dynamical generalized entropy. Finally, we use our results to speculate on relations to the quantum focusing conjecture.

High Energy Theory.title: Asymptotic limits in class-$\mathcal{S}$ theories and non-Abelian Hodge theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We develop a non-Abelian Hodge-theoretic refinement of asymptotic limits in type-$A$ class-$\mathcal S$ theories, enriching the geometric description of the degenerating UV curve with gauge-theoretic data encoded by the associated Hitchin system. A degeneration of the UV curve produces a long plumbing tube, which we equip with the local monodromy data of a Hitchin-Simpson flat connection admitting a regular-singular logarithmic model. The semisimple and unipotent parts of the monodromy govern, respectively, the power-law and logarithmic growth of flat sections through the tube. Combining this non-Abelian holonomy with the geometric Picard-Lefschetz monodromy yields a decorated cusp label that incorporates Higgs-bundle information and extends tube-wise to intersections of boundary divisors. We also discuss a particular class of monodromy labels for which the weak gauge algebra specified by the fixture and gluing data lies in the reductive monodromy centralizer. In type $A$, we organize the local monodromy labels into discrete types specified by the eigenspace multiplicities of the semisimple part and the Jordan type of the nilpotent logarithm of the unipotent part. Finally, we illustrate the construction for $SL(3,\mathbb C)$ on the four-punctured sphere and $SL(4,\mathbb C)$ on the two-punctured torus.
High Energy Theory.comment: 54 pages, 9 figures, and 3 tables; references added; clarifications added

High Energy Theory.title: Cosmological Gravitational Wave Collider Physics
High Energy Theory.summary: Primordial tensor non-Gaussianity can probe massive particles present during inflation. We investigate this possibility in an effective field theory where the massless graviton mixes with the helicity-two mode of an additional massive spin-two field $σ_{ij}$ with cubic self-interactions. For constant sound speed, we compute the leading tensor power-spectrum correction and the tree-level bispectrum, finding novel analytical expressions for these quantities. In the $m_σ>3H/2$ regime, we find a nonanalytic squeezed contribution that exhibits logarithmic oscillations with characteristic dependence $(k_L/k_S)^{3/2\pm iμ}$, where $μ=\sqrt{m_σ^2/H^2-9/4}$. The oscillation frequency is set by the mass $m_σ$, while the polarisation contractions determine the relative amplitudes of the different graviton helicity configurations. The same mixing generates corrections to the power spectrum and the bispectrum. We derive the associated quadrupolar modulation of short-scale tensor power spectrum and relate its amplitude to the model parameters. Finally, we explore how a slowly varying sound speed modifies the squeezed signal.~These results connect the two-point, three-point, and quadrupolar tensor signatures of massive spin-two fields in the cosmological gravitational wave collider.

High Energy Theory.title: Semiclassical effects on ultramassive spacetimes
High Energy Theory.summary: A recent work [Senovilla, Port. Math. 80 (2023)] has shown that accretion of matter by a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole can take this object beyond a critical limit where the event and cosmological horizons coalesce, transforming it into a collapsing universe resembling a Kantowski-Sachs cosmology. In these configurations, dubbed ``ultramassive spacetimes'', future asymptotic infinity and the event horizon associated with the black hole cease to exist. In this work, we take the first steps toward exploring semiclassical gravity effects on such geometries. In particular, we examine the fate of Hawking radiation in these backgrounds and analyze the behavior of the renormalized stress-energy tensor within the Polyakov approximation. We also explore the effect of semiclassical backreaction on the evolution of the horizons, focusing on cases in the vicinity of the extremal limit, and on the subsequent universal collapse.

High Energy Theory.title: Strong coupling spectrum of $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3$ from string field theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We consider type IIB string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$ in a large AdS radius expansion at arbitrary values of the relative RR and NS-NS fluxes. We develop a method for computing scaling dimensions in the dual CFT in this limit by combining a string field theory calculation, valid at finite quantized NS-NS flux but perturbative in RR flux, with a finite mixed-flux ansatz, which is constrained by worldsheet parity and motivated by classical string solutions. We apply the method to three families of states. In the pure-RR limit, our results agree both with a family of states computed using the worldsheet bootstrap and with another family computed using integrability.
High Energy Theory.comment: 86 pages, additional references and minor textual clarifications

High Energy Theory.title: Decrease of the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation induced by backreaction in the Bose-Einstein condensate
High Energy Theory.summary: We analytically study the effect of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation on its entanglement entropy in the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). The backreaction is expected to play an essential role in the decrease of the entanglement entropy and in realizing the Page curve. Since the BEC theory has microscopic Hamiltonian and thus exhibits unitarity, it is desirable to reproduce the Page curve explicitly by using the Hamiltonian. As the first step towards this goal, we concretely study the BEC with a step-like configuration that has been extensively studied in the literature. By using the microscopic theory, we derive an explicit form of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation. Combining it with the known results of the Bogoliubov coefficients, we analytically compute the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation, and show that the backreaction reduces the growth of the entanglement entropy as expected for sufficiently low energy modes over a wide range of the parameter characterizing the step-like configuration.
High Energy Theory.comment: 26 pages, 5 figures, v2: Arguments on the case with D near one are corrected, typos corrected, references added, v3: typo corrected, reference added, v4: published version

High Energy Theory.title: The Fock Space Dynamics of Causal Fermion Systems: Non-Abelian Gauge Fields
High Energy Theory.summary: A limiting case is worked out in which the causal action principle for causal fermion systems describing Minkowski space gives rise to the linear Fock space dynamics of perturbative quantum field theory, including non-abelian gauge fields and Dirac fields.

High Energy Theory.title: Batalin-Vilkovisky quantization with an angular twist
High Energy Theory.summary: We construct cubic scalar field theory on $λ$-Minkowski space by combining the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism with harmonic analysis, and produce two inequivalent noncommutative quantum field theories. The braided theory is based on a braided $L_\infty$-algebra whereby covariance dictates a spectral decomposition into cylindrical Bessel functions that diagonalise the angular Drinfel'd twist; in this theory we find the usual logarithmic ultraviolet divergences and confirm the absence of UV/IR mixing. The standard noncommutative theory is based on a classical $L_\infty$-algebra; in this theory we relate the spectral decompositions into plane wave and cylindrical harmonic eigenmodes of the Klein-Gordan operator, we verify the planar equivalence theorem, and we demonstrate a periodic form of UV/IR mixing in which non-planar correlators are generically ultraviolet finite but become non-analytic on an infinite lattice of exceptional momenta.
High Energy Theory.comment: 42 pages, 1 table; v2: presentation improved; Final version to be published in JHEP

High Energy Theory.title: Fermion Hierarchies from Fricke Modular Symmetry
High Energy Theory.summary: We show how Fricke modular symmetry can generate realistic fermion hierarchies and quark CP violation from a single modulus in a supersymmetric effective theory. Matter fields are labelled by the two one-dimensional characters of $Γ_0^+(N)$ that are trivial on $Γ_0(N)$, and interactions use complete spaces of cusp-regular holomorphic modular forms. At level three, the Fricke extension enlarges an interior stabilizer from order three to order six, allowing its parity to enforce three additional powers of the displacement $t$. An explicit assignment gives quark mass powers $(7,3,0)$ and $(5,4,2)$ and CKM powers $(1,2,3)$. The leading textures conserve CP, but an exact relation among the modular generators produces an appreciable CKM phase at finite displacement. A fit at $|t|\simeq0.306$ reproduces the quark and lepton reference values with order one coefficients in a fixed normalization. We also relate the Fricke double-coset algebra to coset non-invertible symmetry; on the coefficient spaces used here its action reduces to ordinary Fricke parity.

High Energy Theory.title: A group theoretic calculation of multi-invariants of some stabilizer states
High Energy Theory.summary: We study multi-invariants---a multi-partite generalization of Renyi entropies---of simple stabilizer states, for an arbitrary replica symmetry group. We develop a group theoretic technique for evaluating such invariants, which operates on the replica group and involves counting intersections among its cosets.
