Our techniques streamline the calculations of multi-invariants for graph states with two GHZ-like nodes and for certain generalizations thereof. The methodology developed here is most suitable when the quantum state is simple but flexibility over the replica group is desired.

High Energy Theory.title: Mellin Moments of Proton Unpolarized GPDs at Nonzero Skewness from Lattice QCD with a Neural-Network Parametrization
High Energy Theory.summary: We use lattice QCD to determine the generalized form factors (GFFs) entering the first four Mellin moments of the unpolarized isovector $u-d$ proton GPDs at nonzero skewness. The framework combines the polynomiality of the moments in the skewness $ξ$, with the short-distance expansion formalism, allowing the lattice-extracted reduced Ioffe-time distributions (ITDs) to be expressed in terms of GFFs. In order to extract the GFFs by fitting these relations to the lattice data, we parameterize each GFF with an artificial neural network (ANN) as a continuous function of the invariant momentum transfer squared $t$, which accommodates the kinematic coverage of the data in a flexible way. With this fit, we determine the fourteen GFFs that enter the first four Mellin moments, including the skewness-dependent GFFs. From the extracted GFFs, we obtain the quark total angular momentum of the isovector combination, $J^{u-d}=0.296(11)(7)$ in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $μ=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, in agreement with previous lattice determinations based on nonlocal operators and with a smaller total uncertainty. We also determine the impact-parameter distributions of the first three Mellin moments in an unpolarized and in a transversely polarized proton. We finally identify and discuss the principal systematic uncertainties which enter this extraction, and the challenges specific to the nonzero-skewness regime.

High Energy Theory.title: Scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety
High Energy Theory.summary: The unitarity and causality properties of asymptotically safe quantum gravity are still unsettled. Scattering amplitudes provide a direct test, but their computation requires fully momentum-dependent correlation functions. In this light, we compute the full scalar-scalar-graviton vertex from Asymptotic Safety within a mostly analytic approximation. Qualitatively, we find the expected logarithmic branch-cut structure, and we correctly recover the double-eikonal soft divergences predicted by Weinberg's soft theorem. Quantitatively, we find that non-minimal operators are generally as important as the minimal vertex stemming from the scalar kinetic term.

High Energy Theory.title: Local uniqueness of the Black String with small circle size
High Energy Theory.summary:
In this article we study uniqueness of the Black String, i.e. the product of 4-dimensional Schwarzschild space with a circle of length L.
  In arXiv:2410.20967, this was reduced to a non-linear elliptic PDE, and we use this setup to show that for small L the Black String is infinitesimally rigid as a Ricci-flat metric.
  Using a fixed point theorem, we prove that this implies local uniqueness, i.e. there exist no other Ricci-flat metrics near the Black String, and we give bounds for the size of the neighborhood in which the Black String is unique.
  We compare this with the toy problem of a scalar field satisfying an elliptic equation that was already solved in arXiv:2410.20967 using different methods.
  In this case we can use the fixed point theorem method to prove not just a local but a global statement.
High Energy Theory.comment: changed Dirichlet boundary conditions to physical ones for solutions in a box, results unchanged

High Energy Theory.title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
High Energy Theory.summary: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.
High Energy Theory.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. v2: Added references and improved explanations

High Energy Theory.title: The Residual $288$ in an $E_8\timesωE_8$ Program: Representation Accounting and Physical Matter Interfaces
High Energy Theory.summary: We examine the accounting identity $496=208+288$ in an octonionic $E_8\timesωE_8$ unification program. The dimensions count selected representation labels, not a closed particle spectrum. In a consistent trinification convention, the quark-doublet labels descend from the $E_6$ adjoint, whereas the lepton-doublet labels descend from the mixed $E_8$ sectors. Their occurrence supplies useful nonabelian multiplicities but does not establish three complete chiral generations. We prove that the stated doublet assignments cannot acquire their Standard-Model hypercharges from a single $E_6$ generator commuting with the full family, colour and weak groups. Separately, a chosen charge-first Clifford benchmark carries three complete families on a $48$-dimensional internal Weyl coefficient space and admits an anomaly-free common family action. We construct explicit subgroup-equivariant lifts of physical scalar currents into $\overline{27}\otimes27=1\oplus78\oplus650$, and show that their nonuniqueness prevents a coupling prediction from normalization alone. The full comparison square contains fundamental family channels; a narrower exclusion applies only to undressed matter bilinears trivial under an independent geometric group. We identify the localization maps, interaction matrix elements, vacuum correlations and kinetic matrices needed to connect the exceptional geometry to physical matter. The geometric interpretation is retained, while generation selection, scalar binding and mass matching remain dynamical problems.
High Energy Theory.comment: v2. 18 pages. Title modified. Significantly revised to add new results and improve clarity of presentation

High Energy Theory.title: Fermion-Number Variation for Several Coupling Schemes in an $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Chiral Soliton Background
High Energy Theory.summary: When topological solitons are coupled to fermions, they often induce a nontrivial fermion number. In the chiral quark soliton model (CQSM), this phenomenon underlies the identification of soliton topology with baryon number. However, whether this topology--fermion-number correspondence is determined solely by soliton topology or also depends on the fermion--soliton coupling scheme remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate this question by comparing several coupling schemes to the same $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ chiral soliton background. To treat the corresponding Dirac Hamiltonians within a common framework, we evaluate the variation of the regularized fermion-number along a model-parameter space. For the standard chiral Yukawa coupling of the CQSM, this variation reproduces the topological charge $Q$ associated with $π_3(\mathrm{SU}(N))$. The same result is obtained for an axial-vector coupling, whereas the fermion number variation vanishes for a vector coupling, despite the nontrivial topology of the chiral soliton background. These results provide an explicit example in which soliton topology alone does not determine the fermionic response; the topology--fermion-number correspondence also depends on how the background field is coupled to fermions.

High Energy Theory.title: Duality-covariant particles and exotic branes
High Energy Theory.summary: In this paper we construct duality-covariant worldvolume dynamics of particles and branes. We extend known actions and phase space formulations to include the hidden $E_8$ symmetry of 11D supergravity, analogous to the Ehlers symmetry of 4D gravity. Making the worldvolume theory manifestly duality-covariant requires the ancillary structure of $E_8$ exceptional field theory to be taken into account. For zero-branes, we propose an enlarged worldline model with a coadjoint orbit term to encode this. More generally, we propose worldvolume theories for arbitrary exotic branes in a way that generalises the known gauged sigma model of the Kaluza-Klein monopole. These are natural in the duality-covariant Hamiltonian formulation employed here. We discuss the case of zero-branes in eleven dimensions as an illustrative example.
High Energy Theory.comment: 52 pages (v3: more minor changes, published version)

High Energy Theory.title: Universal Statistics of Measurement-Induced Entanglement in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the statistics of measurement-induced entanglement (MIE) after partial measurement on a class of one-dimensional quantum critical states described by Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids at low energies. Using a replica trick to average over measurement outcomes in the charge basis and tools from conformal field theory (CFT), we derive closed-form expressions for the cumulants of MIE. We show that exact Born-averaging over microscopic measurement outcomes becomes equivalent at low energy to averaging over conformal boundary conditions weighted by their corresponding partition functions. Our results yield distinctive critical behavior across all cumulants in the regime where the unmeasured parts of the system are maximally separated. We also obtain the full distribution of MIE, finding that it is generically bimodal and exhibits fat-tails. We corroborate our analytical predictions by numerical calculations and find good agreement between them.

High Energy Theory.title: Quantum mechanical Gaussian wavepackets of single relativistic particles
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the evolutions of selected quasi-(1+1) dimensional wavepacket solutions to the Klein-Gordon equation for a relativistic charged particle in uniform motion or accelerated by a uniform electric field in Minkowski space. We explore how good the charge density of a Klein-Gordon wavepacket can be approximately described by a Gaussian state with the single-particle interpretation. We find that the minimal initial width of a wavepacket for a good Gaussian approximation in position space is about the Compton wavelength of the particle divided by its Lorentz factor at the initial moment. This can be considered as a manifestation of relativistic length contraction, which is also observed numerically in the spreading of the wavepacket's charge density.
High Energy Theory.comment: 17 pages, 8 figures. v2: Ref.[6] has been added. v3: Eq.(24) has been corrected, and Figs. 6 and 7 have been revised accordingly. The observation and conclusion remain unchanged

High Energy Theory.title: Linearised gravitational radiation in de Sitter spacetime at all multipole orders
High Energy Theory.summary: We derive the linearised gravitational waves generated by a localised matter source in the Poincare patch of de Sitter spacetime at arbitrary multipole order. The linearised de Sitter problem is mapped exactly to an auxiliary flat-space problem in harmonic gauge, with a conserved source built from the physical stress tensor. This allows us to use the multipole expansion of Damour and Iyer verbatim, and yields the exterior metric at all orders in terms of two families of radiative multipole moments given as explicit integrals of the physical stress tensor. The de Sitter tail is absorbed entirely into the auxiliary stress tensor, so that neither the moments nor the canonical exterior metric carry an integral over the past history of the source. As a check, we recover the known quadrupolar metric: in the quadrupolar truncation it is our canonical field up to a residual gauge transformation, which we construct explicitly.
High Energy Theory.comment: 36 pages, no figures; v2: note added

High Energy Theory.title: Ellis-Bronnikov Wormhole Shadows with Spherically Symmetric Accretion Flow
High Energy Theory.summary: We investigate the observational differences between the Ellis--Bronnikov (EB) wormhole and the Schwarzschild black hole (BH) by performing general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) simulations. We consider a spherically symmetric steady-state accretion flow and perform GRRT simulations incorporating synchrotron emission. For both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH, the simulated images consist of a central shadow region and a bright photon ring. We find that both the shadow region and the photon ring of the EB wormhole are brighter than those of the Schwarzschild BH. These differences arise from the absence of an event horizon in the EB wormhole, allowing the emission from the accreting matter around and beyond the throat to contribute to the intensity. We also compare the simulated images with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) observations of M87*. Although the total flux and the ring diameter are comparable with the EHT results, our models with the spherically symmetric accretion flow cannot reproduce the deep central brightness depression observed by the EHT, for both the EB wormhole and the Schwarzschild BH. This indicates that a non-spherical accretion flow is required for a detailed comparison with the EHT image.

High Energy Theory.title: Non-Geometric T-Duality as Higher Groupoid Bundles with Connections
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose a description of T-duality between general geometric and non-geometric backgrounds as higher groupoid bundles with connections. Our description extends the previous observation by Nikolaus and Waldorf that the topological aspects of geometric and half-geometric T-dualities can be described in terms of higher geometry. We extend their construction in two ways. First, we endow the higher geometries with adjusted connections, which allow us to discuss explicit formulas for the metric and the Kalb-Ramond field of a T-background. Second, we extend the principal 2-bundles to principal 2-groupoid bundles, which accommodate the scalar fields arising in T-dualities along two directions as well as $Q$-fluxes. Our proposals reproduce key examples from the literature. They are manifestly covariant under the full T-duality group $\mathsf{GO}(n,n;\mathbb{Z})$ and have interesting physical and mathematical implications. Eventually, we also comment on the case of T-duality in the presence of scalar fluxes.

High Energy Theory.title: Fortuitous BMN Cohomology at Every $N$
High Energy Theory.summary: Finite-$N$ trace relations can produce $Q$-cohomology classes with no stable large-$N$ ancestor. The brane-fused construction at $SU(3)$ suggests that such states can retain an $SU(2)$ nonabelian core accompanied by scalar hair. We develop this idea into a general construction for every $SU(N)$, $N\geq3$. Starting from the $SU(2)$ threshold operator $O_{24}$, we select pairs of eigenvalues of one scalar and construct corrected two-colour letters whose $Q$-transformations obey the $SU(2)$ rules exactly. Substitution into $O_{24}$ gives a closed rational operator for each pair. Multiplying by eigenvalue-separation factors removes the denominators, and summing over all pairs produces a gauge-invariant polynomial. An exact block-restriction identity recovers a nonzero multiple of $O_{24}$. The restriction maps every stable class to a stable $SU(2)$ class, proving that the resulting operator is non-exact and fortuitous, even when non-Coulombic stable classes are included. This proves the existence of fortuitous BMN cohomology at every $N\geq3$. The construction is an exact algebraic realization of a nonabelian core with scalar dressing.
High Energy Theory.comment: 25+1 pages, no figures. v2: presentation improved and ancillary mathematica notebook included in submission

High Energy Theory.title: Adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
High Energy Theory.summary: The Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.

High Energy Theory.title: $B_{sJ}(6114)$ as a Higher-Partial-Wave $\bar{K}^{*}B^{(*)}$ Molecular Candidate
High Energy Theory.summary: In 2021, the LHCb Collaboration observed the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ state in the $B^\pm K^\mp$ invariant mass spectrum. It is currently the highest-mass bottom-strange state listed by the Particle Data Group (PDG). However, its spin-parity quantum numbers have not yet been experimentally determined, and its internal structure remains under debate. Although several quark-model interpretations have been proposed, including the $1^3D_1$ state and a member of the $1D(2^-,3^-)$ doublet, the possibility of a hadronic molecular structure for this state has not yet been systematically investigated. We investigate the possibility of interpreting \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) as a \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state within the one-boson-exchange model. By solving the Schrödinger equation using the Gaussian expansion method, we study the bound-state properties with different spin-parity assignments, taking into account partial-wave mixing and coupled-channel effects. We further calculate the strong decay widths into the allowed \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}\) channels and compare them with the experimental data. Our results show that the mass spectrum alone cannot uniquely determine the spin-parity of \(B_{sJ}(6114)\). However, the decay-width analysis disfavors the \(J^P=0^+\), \(0^-\), \(1^+\), \(2^+\), and \(3^-\) assignments, while the \(J^P=1^-\), \(2^-\), and \(3^+\) configurations remain compatible with the experimental constraints. Among these possibilities, the \(J^P=1^-\) assignment provides the best agreement with the measured decay width. These findings suggest that \(B_{sJ}(6114)\) may be a higher-partial-wave \(B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{*}\) molecular state.

High Energy Theory.title: Asymptotically Safe Gravitational Form Factors from the Proper-Time Flow Equation
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the renormalization group flow of nonlocal form factors in four-dimensional quantum gravity within the proper-time formalism at quadratic order in the curvature expansion. We show that, in the presence of a running Newtonian coupling and a fixed negative cosmological constant, the flow equations can be integrated down to $k=0$, allowing the reconstruction of the full momentum dependence of the form factors. The running of Newton's coupling generates nontrivial momentum-dependent corrections to the effective field theory behavior, with the Planck scale setting the crossover between the IR and UV regimes. In the infrared, these corrections are organized as an expansion in powers of $q^2/m_p^2$, while in the ultraviolet they are organized in powers of $m_p^2/q^2$. Within this framework, we also analyze the properties of the dimensionless flow, identifying its fixed-point structure and constructing asymptotically safe solutions. We show that the integrated asymptotically safe solutions admit a finite and cutoff-independent $Λ\to\infty$ limit when the non-Gaussian fixed-point solution is imposed as the ultraviolet boundary condition. This removes UV logarithmic contributions and ensures independence from the renormalization scale $μ$. The resulting renormalized asymptotically safe form factors at $k=0$ display a power-law decay $\sim1/q^2$ in the ultraviolet and reproduce the expected logarithmic structure in the infrared, with the Planck scale replacing the renormalization scale.

High Energy Theory.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
High Energy Theory.summary: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).
High Energy Theory.comment: 16 pages, LaTeX, uses BibTeX. Minor typos and acknowledgements para corrected

High Energy Theory.title: The Quantum Channels of the Compton Scattering of an Entangled Pair of Photons
High Energy Theory.summary: The Compton scattering of an entangled pair of photons is studied. Using the resulting reduced density matrix, we demonstrate how to derive the Kraus operators for the interaction from the underlying fundamental theory, quantum electrodynamics. The normalization of the final density matrix of the entangled photons after the interaction is crucial to obtaining the correct probabilities and correlations. The reduced density matrix of the photon, which does not participate in the interaction directly, remains unchanged. It indicates that quantum effects in quantum sensing using an entangled photon pair can be observed only through the correlations or superposition of the entire pair. We relate our results to the Stokes parameters for determining polarizations and investigating the entangled states of photons from electron-positron annihilation in astrophysical systems.

High Energy Theory.title: 8-type electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We consider electric flux tube solutions in SU(3) gauge theory with scalar fields in the fundamental representation, for an electric field in the $λ_8$ direction (8-type). In temporal gauge, the 3-type electric field rotates within a single SU(2) subgroup at one frequency, whereas the 8-type electric field necessarily rotates within three SU(2) subgroups with at least two different frequencies. We construct the homogeneous 8-type electric field with three scalar fields and show that two scalar fields are sufficient only on a one-parameter family of gauge field backgrounds. Like the 3-type field, the homogeneous 8-type field is immune to decay through Schwinger pair production of gauge bosons. We then construct an 8-type electric string solution in temporal gauge. Its electric field is of 8-type on the string axis and, unlike the 3-type string, the string is only net color neutral, which results in a weak radial electric field.
High Energy Theory.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Ancillary files contain the string profile functions and scripts that check the solutions

High Energy Theory.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordström black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.

High Energy Theory.title: Extended Local Infrared Cutoff for the Holographic Density
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose an extended local infrared cutoff for the holographic density that leads to linear cosmological equations and gives exact analytical solutions. The model allows to remove the residual matter and radiation-like terms of the local construction based on $H$ and $\dot{H}$, resulting in a clear separation between the standard cosmological fluids and the holographic sector. The homogeneous solution generates characteristic modes that give rise to different cosmological behaviors. The extension includes derivatives up to third order, where two of the characteristic modes can modify the pre-recombination expansion and reduce the sound horizon while remaining subdominant at BBN. A slightly phantom mode provides an additional late-time geometrical freedom that can further increase the CMB-compatible value of $H_0$. Optimizations using BAO constraints yield values of $H_0$ in the approximate range $70.5-72.4\ {\rm km\;s^{-1}\;Mpc^{-1}}$.

High Energy Theory.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
High Energy Theory.summary: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model in which gauge and Higgs fields are regulated on a finite lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This preserves the familiar continuum description of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes, without requiring a finite-dimensional discretization of chiral fermions. The Standard Model's anomaly cancellation permits a gauge-invariant definition of the chiral fermion determinant. Yukawa interactions are included in the full fermion determinant using a gauge-covariant cutoff that acts on the interaction vertices rather than the fermion propagator. We show that removing this cutoff requires only the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, and construct a consistent complex fermion weight, including in topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At fixed bosonic lattice spacing and finite spacetime volume, the resulting bosonic functional integral is finite and exactly gauge invariant under the stated smoothness conditions. The construction provides a finite-regulator Standard Model formulation retaining the physical structure of continuum chiral fermions. Appendix F.5 establishes reflection positivity for a variant reconstruction at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

High Energy Theory.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
High Energy Theory.summary: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.

High Energy Theory.title: Number Theory of Decaying Turbulence 2: The Energy Spectrum and the Riemann Zeta Zeros
High Energy Theory.summary: The odd Euler ensemble, the locally stable attractor of the momentum-loop dynamics of freely decaying incompressible turbulence, has a self-similar energy spectrum \(E(k,t)=L^{-3/2}H(kL)\), \(L\sim\sqrt{\tildeνt}\), which does not depend on the dimension of space. We compute its scaling function as a Mellin--Barnes integral whose amplitude contains the ratio \(ζ(p+15/2)/ζ(p+17/2)\) of Riemann zeta functions; the odd ensemble differs from the even one by a prime-\(2\) Euler factor. The integral is evaluated by deforming the contour to Lefschetz thimbles. The non-trivial zeros of \(ζ(s)\) generate a vertical wall of complex poles. As \(ξ=\log(k\sqrt{\tildeνt})\) increases, the thimble traps them in a Stokes staircase, first collectively and then a few at a time, and Berry smoothing turns each trapping into an analytic activation of an exponentially small oscillatory term. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis and simplicity of the zeros, all these poles lie on one wall and their activations accumulate only at infinite time: the spectrum is analytic at every finite time and has an essential singularity at \(t=\infty\). The same analysis gives the second-order structure function, whose index falls continuously from \(2\) to \(0\) without an inertial plateau, and the decay laws, energy \(\propto t^{-5/4}\) and enstrophy \(\propto t^{-9/4}\). The operator representation and the stability of the Euler ensemble are derived in the first paper of this series, and the comparison with simulations and experiments is given in the third.
High Energy Theory.comment: The energy spectrum analyzed in this paper arises from a subdominant saddle point of the Euler ensemble path integral. This saddle-point approximation is superseded by the exact asymptotic spectrum derived in the revised version of arXiv:2607.05745. The exact spectrum does not involve the zeros of the Riemann zeta function

High Energy Theory.title: Localized Neutrinos in Two Dark Dimensions
High Energy Theory.summary: We study neutrino masses in a six-dimensional framework with two compact dark dimensions. In the conventional flat-bulk realization, the sterile-neutrino zero mode is strongly volume suppressed, so a fundamental scale near $10~\mathrm{TeV}$ requires a large higher-dimensional Yukawa coupling to reproduce the observed neutrino masses, while the accompanying two-dimensional Kaluza--Klein tower is strongly constrained by oscillation data. We show that localizing the sterile-neutrino wave function near the Standard-Model brane substantially alleviates both effects. Using a Gaussian localizer, realistic Dirac neutrino masses are obtained with perturbative, order-one Yukawa couplings, while the brane-visible sterile excitations form a shell spectrum with $M_s^2=8μ^2 s$, and squared active--sterile mixings that decrease as $1/s$. The localization scale therefore separates the experimentally relevant sterile-neutrino spectrum from the gravitational compactification scale. We derive the resulting three-flavour structure and study its phenomenological consequences for reactor oscillations and tritium beta decay, including comparisons with current flat-LED and KATRIN constraints.

High Energy Theory.title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
High Energy Theory.summary: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610, we classified the Narain conformal field theories obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group. For two hyperbolic pairs, this gives twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes, which fall into seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar c=6$. In this paper, we develop the physical interpretation of this family and its connections to three-dimensional topological field theory. We show that all twenty-two codes are topological boundary conditions of a single abelian Chern-Simons theory. Its invertible symmetries, which include fractional $B$-field shifts, organize the boundaries into three orbits: free, mixed and torsion. Boundaries in different orbits are related only by gauging. We determine all gaugings of order at most four between the seven theories, by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$, with explicit twisted partition functions, and follow their effect on the spectrum and the current algebra. We then sum the Chern-Simons partition function over handlebodies at genus one and prove a finite Siegel-Weil identity, valid for any number of pairs. For two pairs, the handlebody sum is the uniform average over the free theories. Recovering the average over all twenty-two theories requires one additional contribution, a solid torus with the torsion lines along its core. For three or more pairs, we find that the handlebody sum is not a positive combination of code boundary states.

High Energy Theory.title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
High Energy Theory.summary: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.
High Energy Theory.comment: 9 pages with 3 figures, comments very welcome

High Energy Theory.title: Higher-Loop Vacuum Integrals on $S^D$
High Energy Theory.summary: We develop a new framework for evaluating higher-loop integrals for scalar fields on $S^D$. Starting from a Schwinger-parametric form for general higher-loop integrals on the sphere, it combines total-derivative identities with edge-contraction relations into a coupled linear system. To illustrate our method, we solve for all vacuum graphs through two loops. This includes, in particular, the two-loop three-melon, for which we construct the analytic solution for general $D$ and obtain explicit dimensionally regularized results at all integer dimensions.

High Energy Theory.title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
High Energy Theory.summary: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.

High Energy Theory.title: Worldline Images for Yang-Mills Theory within Boundaries
High Energy Theory.summary: In this article we develop a worldline technique based on the method of images to study the effective action associated to Yang-Mills theories on manifolds with boundaries. We consider the possibility of having either relative or absolute boundary conditions, which are particular types of mixed boundary conditions. Both vector fields and ghost fields are taken into account in this analysis. As a check of our construction, we compute the first three Seeley-DeWitt coefficients of the heat kernel asymptotics. Finally, we employ our technique to calculate the rate of gluon production due to a chromoelectric field background in the presence of a boundary.
High Energy Theory.comment: 43 pages, 2 figures. Matches the published version

High Energy Theory.title: The Stringy Photon Sphere
High Energy Theory.summary: The S matrix on an asymptotically-flat Schwarzschild black hole is studied as a function of position on $\mathcal{I}$. We derive the lightcone singularities that arise in the S matrix whenever the two points on $\mathcal{I}$ are connected by a bulk null geodesic. This includes geodesics orbiting near the photon sphere for a long time, whose kinematics determine the associated lightcone singularities. By turning on a finite string length $\ell_s$, worldsheet corrections are shown to shift the lightcone singularities into the complex time plane, resolving the singularities at real times. In particular, we derive the leading stringy resolution of the photon sphere singularities. We also compute stringy corrections to the eikonal quasinormal mode spectrum of Schwarzschild, and discuss the kinematics of strings orbiting the photon sphere.

High Energy Theory.title: The Komar charges of type II supergravity and supersymmetric localization
High Energy Theory.summary: We compute the on-shell closed, generalized Komar charges associated to an arbitrary Killing vector of the two 10-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity theories which are the low-energy effective field theories of the type~IIA and IIB superstrings. We study different rewritings of this charge in terms of Page charges and forms with special properties that are used in the derivation of thermodynamical relations in black $p$-brane spacetimes. High Energy Theory.title: Thermomagnetic enhancement of conserved-charge correlations in a lattice-constrained PNJL model
High Energy Theory.summary: Conserved-charge correlations offer a promising probe of magnetic fields in strongly interacting matter. We investigate their magnetic response and the finite-density equation of state within a lattice-constrained three-flavor Polyakov--Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model. A thermomagnetic scalar coupling, inferred by Gaussian process regression from lattice QCD results for the average light-quark condensate, incorporates inverse magnetic catalysis into the effective interaction. Without fitting conserved-charge observables, the resulting framework substantially improves their magnetic-field dependence and crossover behavior compared with the fixed-coupling model. In particular, it captures the pronounced magnetic enhancement of the baryon--electric-charge correlation and related susceptibility ratios, supporting their use as QCD magnetometers. The comparison demonstrates that the medium dependence of the effective interaction is essential to describe this response within the model. We further calculate pressure Taylor coefficients through sixth order and reconstruct the pressure and baryon density at nonzero baryon chemical potential. Our results show that lattice information from a single chiral observable constrains a broad thermodynamic response, connecting inverse magnetic catalysis, conserved-charge correlations, and the equation of state in a common framework. This provides a lattice-constrained basis for investigating magnetic-field signatures and finite-density thermodynamics in QCD matter.

High Energy Theory.title: Amplified EFT corrections near exceptional QNMs
High Energy Theory.summary: We show that the ordinary expansion of EFT corrections to individual QNM frequencies breaks down at an exceptional QNM, and that these corrections become enhanced for near-exceptional QNMs. We give a brief argument for why this should generally happen, before numerically demonstrating this behaviour by calculating the $α'^3$ corrections to QNMs of equal-spin Myers--Perry-AdS$_5$ black holes. This calculation corresponds to $λ^{-3/2}$ corrections to the poles of the retarded Green's function in the boundary CFT, where $λ$ is the 't Hooft coupling. Treating the coalescing pair together, we calculate the leading $λ^{-3/4}$ splitting at the uncorrected exceptional point and the $λ^{-3/2}$ displacement of the exceptional point in temperature and angular velocity. The background derivative expansion can remain valid while the nondegenerate expansion of individual frequencies fails. We discuss the implications for the full response and for other areas of black hole physics.

High Energy Theory.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics of dipole-charged fields in the Proca theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We discuss the dynamics of field configurations encoded in the certain class of electric (magnetic) dipole-charged states in the Proca theory of the real massive vector field. We construct such states so as to ensure that the long distance structure of the mean electromagnetic field in them is initially set by the formula describing the electromagnetic field of the electric (magnetic) dipole. We analyze then how such a mean electromagnetic field evolves in time. We find that far away from the center of the initial field configuration, the long range component of the mean electromagnetic field harmonically oscillates, which leads to the phenomenon of the periodic oscillations of the electric (magnetic) dipole moment. We also find that near the center of the initial field configuration, the mean electromagnetic field escapes from its initial arrangement and a spherical shock wave propagating with the speed of light appears in the studied system. A curious configuration of the axisymmetric mean electric field is found to accompany the mean magnetic field in magnetic dipole-charged states.

High Energy Theory.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
High Energy Theory.summary: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

High Energy Theory.title: Data analysis of millions of Type IIB flux vacua
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the vacuum structure of flux compactifications of type IIB string theory on the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{CP}^4_{1,1,1,6,9}$ with two effective complex structure moduli. We scan $30{,}770{,}178$ flux choices compatible with the tadpole bound, and use a gradient-based constrained minimization based on the SLSQP algorithm to identify candidates for local minima of the scalar potential, yielding a dataset of millions of candidate flux vacua. Using the $1{,}296{,}633$ reliable solutions selected from this dataset, we analyze distributions and correlations of various physical quantities such as vacuum expectation values of moduli and vacuum energy. Using quadratic flux invariants as input features, we train a classifier to identify solutions satisfying the numerical SUSY criterion $|V|<10^{-4.5}$. On a randomly selected test set, selecting the top-ranked $5\%$ recovers $47.2\%$ of the SUSY test solutions. We also use supervised regression to predict the potential and moduli field values. In the regression comparison, quadratic flux invariant inputs improve prediction of potential value and the complex-structure coordinates, while the vanilla six flux parameters give better predictions for the axio-dilaton coordinates under the tested settings.

High Energy Theory.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
High Energy Theory.summary: We derive the primordial $\langleζζh\rangle$, $\langleζhh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

High Energy Theory.title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS$_3$
High Energy Theory.summary: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $α$ and $κ$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

High Energy Theory.title: The deepest X-ray view of a kiloparsec scale jet at z=6.1
High Energy Theory.summary:
The mechanism responsible for the high-energy emission observed in kiloparsec-scale jets across cosmic time remains poorly understood. The relativistic jet associated with the z=6.1 AGN PSO J030947.49+271757.31 is the highest-redshift large-scale jet currently resolved in X-rays, providing a unique opportunity to study these structures.
  We present new Chandra observations, combined with archival data, for a total exposure of 360 ks. The increased exposure allowed us to resolve the extended X-ray emission into two distinct, slightly resolved components and perform spatially resolved spectral analyses.
  The extended emission has a photon index of Gamma = 2.25 (+0.45, -0.44), steeper than that of the core (Gamma = 1.86 +/- 0.09), and an extended-to-core luminosity ratio of 18%. Simulations using the Chandra image as input show that an AXIS-like mission could increase the detected photon statistics by a factor of approximately 17.
  We resolve the kiloparsec-scale jet into two main components and constrain its spectral properties. This is the most distant and one of the most X-ray-luminous large-scale jets currently known. Future X-ray missions with arcsecond-scale angular resolution could enable more detailed studies of such systems and reveal a population of fainter high-redshift jets beyond Chandra's reach.
High Energy Theory.comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A) on 13 October 2026

High Energy Theory.title: Fluids on null hypersurfaces and Carrollian hydrodynamics
High Energy Theory.summary: We study intrinsic ideal fluids on null hypersurfaces and their realisations by causal fluids living in the ambient spacetime. An embedded null hypersurface is equipped with an induced Carrollian structure with a temporal Weyl symmetry inherited from rescalings of the null generator, and we develop the corresponding null submanifold and variational calculus. The intrinsic fluid phases are classified according to their realisation of Carroll boosts and temporal Weyl symmetry. If we demand that an ambient fluid be confined to a null hypersurface, the ambient fluid velocity must be null, which realises an intrinsic zero-temperature Carrollian phase with unbroken Carroll boosts. In general, timelike or null ambient fluids will cross a null hypersurface and lead to an open Carrollian system. On a null foliation, the sources correspond to transport between null leaves. We then show that there exists a decoupling limit of a timelike ambient fluid which gives rise to an autonomous Carrollian fluid with spontaneously broken Carroll boosts and no source terms. This decoupling limit corresponds to an infinite boost while keeping the enthalpy finite and nonzero, which leads to a divergent ambient energy-momentum tensor. Nevertheless, the induced Carrollian responses do not see the divergent term and remain finite, and an independent Carroll boost Goldstone emerges from a subleading component of the ambient fluid velocity in this limit.

High Energy Theory.title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
High Energy Theory.summary: Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections. Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.

High Energy Theory.title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
High Energy Theory.summary: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.

High Energy Theory.title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
High Energy Theory.summary: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $φ$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_φ$, the decay $N\toνφ$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $φ\toγγ$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.

High Energy Theory.title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
High Energy Theory.summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

High Energy Theory.title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
High Energy Theory.summary: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.

High Energy Theory.title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
High Energy Theory.summary: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.

High Energy Theory.title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.

High Energy Theory.title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
High Energy Theory.summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.
High Energy Theory.comment: 81 pages, 34 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook in the ancillary files

High Energy Theory.title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
High Energy Theory.summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

High Energy Theory.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
High Energy Theory.summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

High Energy Theory.title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
High Energy Theory.summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

High Energy Theory.title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
High Energy Theory.summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

High Energy Theory.title: Quantum Charge as a Particle/Antiparticle Label
High Energy Theory.summary: We show that the concept of particles and antiparticles is related to the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$. Its generators are the position operators $\hat x^a$, the momentum operators $\hat p_a$, and the central element $Q_{\sf{v}}$, which defines a subgroup U(1)$_{\sf v}$ of $W\!H_3$. We show that the wave functions have a charge relative to the group U(1)$_{\sf{v}}$ equal to either $q_+=1/\hbar$ (particle $ψ_+$) or $q_-=-1/\hbar$ (antiparticle $ψ_-$). We call these eigenvalues of the operator $Q_{\sf{v}}$ quantum charges: $Q_{\sf{v}}ψ_\pm^{}=q_\pm^{}ψ_\pm^{}$. The wave functions $ψ_+$ and $ψ_-$ belong to the Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_+$ and $\mathcal{H}_-$, on which unitarily inequivalent representations $π_\hbar$ and $π_{-\hbar}$ of the Weyl-Heisenberg group $W\!H_3$ are defined. These representations are related to each other by the antilinear charge conjugation operator $\hat C$, which maps $\mathcal{H}_+, q_+$ to $\mathcal{H}_-, q_-$. Charges $q_\pm^{}$ are intrinsic characteristics of the wave functions $ψ_\pm^{}$, similar to spin and electric charge. The wave function possesses one of these charges, $q_+$ or $q_-$, prior to the specification of any equations. We show that negative probabilities/energies and the Klein paradox in Klein-Gordon and Dirac theories are consequences of the violation of U(1)$_{\sf v}$-invariance in these theories. Restoring this invariance separates particle and antiparticles and eliminates all paradoxes at the level of first-quantized relativistic theories.

High Energy Theory.title: Lipshitz-Sarkar refines mirrors more than Khovanov
High Energy Theory.summary: Lipshitz and Sarkar asked in an ICM 2018 question whether their homotopy-theoretic refinement of Khovanov homology can detect mirror reflection when ordinary integral Khovanov homology cannot. We give an affirmative answer by presenting a prime knot whose integral Khovanov homology agrees with that of its mirror in every bidegree, including torsion, and yet over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the second Steenrod square has rank one for the knot and rank zero for its mirror in a specified bidegree. We also give a composite example. The construction, search and computations are done with the help of {\it chat-GTP 5.6 sol Pro} combing over the {\it Regina Census} of knots.
High Energy Theory.comment: 6 pages. We are extremely grateful to Krishnendu Kar for his detailed and helpful comments on the first version

High Energy Theory.title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
High Energy Theory.summary: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

Materials Science.title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
Materials Science.summary: Resolving steep damage gradients across diffuse cracks in the phase-field modeling of fracture favors the use of high-order finite elements, for which matrix-free methods can provide superior performance and scalability. Here, we implement the Peric & Dettmer constitutive framework for visco-elastoplastic materials in an open source solid mechanics library supporting matrix-free operators for high-order finite elements with p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs. We introduce a rheological fracture element assembled in series with the Peric & Dettmer block, keeping fracture and inelastic material properties mutually independent. We conduct numerical simulations of tensile and compressive quasistatic tests on synthetic particle-matrix microstructures using an El Capitan high-performance computing prototype. The results reproduce representative inelastic responses and fracture patterns, including X-shaped cracking observed in polymer-bonded explosives and cup-and-cone fracture in ductile metals.

Materials Science.title: Methane and ethane adsorption on calcite surfaces: effects of surface morphology from molecular dynamics and 3D-RISM
Materials Science.summary: Understanding the adsorption of alkanes on mineral surfaces is important for industrial processes such as oil and gas recovery from shale reservoirs. Previous studies have examined the adsorption of functionalized and non-functionalized alkanes on calcite, as well as adsorption under confinement. However, real surfaces commonly exhibit defects that can influence adsorption behavior. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and the three-dimensional reference interaction site model (3D-RISM) are used to investigate the adsorption of methane and ethane on calcite surfaces with step defects. MD simulations were carried out with and without positional restraints to investigate the effects of carbonate reorientation. 3D-RISM calculations were performed on these structures and on energy-minimized configurations of the relaxed crystal. Both methods show adsorption enhanced at step defects relative to flat regions, with methane exhibiting higher excess adsorption than ethane. Carbonate reorientation at the relaxed step edges reduces the local density peaks at specific step sites in both methods, while the integrated excess adsorption from MD remains comparable to that of the restrained surface. 3D-RISM predicts lower maxima for the highest density peaks and larger excess adsorption than MD, but reproduces the spatial organization and overall adsorption trends at a fraction of the computational cost. These results highlight the importance of surface heterogeneity in fluid-mineral interactions and demonstrate that 3D-RISM is an efficient tool for semi-quantitative screening of adsorption across complex surface geometries

Materials Science.title: PINN-Phase: Physics-informed neural integration for accurate, generalizable and scalable multiphase-field evolution
Materials Science.summary: Polycrystal phase-field simulations are repeated for many related initial conditions, calling for integrators trained once and reused without retraining. We introduce PINN-Phase, a physics-informed neural time integrator that advances the multiphase field autonomously from its initial condition, enforcing phase bounds and unit sum at every step. Its hybrid realization learns from the governing residual on its own predicted states, without post-initial-condition reference states in the loss or checkpoint selection. A fixed 25-grain model meets all predefined criteria on seven of eight prospectively fixed unseen microstructures and both atypical stress cases, with 0.94-3.71% terminal label disagreement. At native 128^3, a model trained on four microstructures keeps 98.79% label agreement and exact survivor identities on a training case over 24,000 steps, 5.86 times its represented training horizon; five of six unseen microstructures keep the exact terminal survivor set. A complementary phase-local realization, with 2,160 learned parameters independent of the phase count, trained once at 48^3 with eight grains using one-step physical-map targets on its own states, meets all acceptance criteria with unchanged weights on unseen 64^3, 96^3 and 128^3 microstructures with up to 38 grains at fixed grid spacing. At 128^3 with 150 grains and comparable mean initial grain volume, it reproduces all 368 grain extinctions over 13,500 steps with at most 0.88% label disagreement and meets the per-grain volume criterion up to t = 80. These results demonstrate structurally admissible long-horizon neural integration transferring zero-shot across initial conditions within fixed benchmark families and, in phase-local form, across domain sizes and grain counts.

Materials Science.title: Electronic, structural and magnetic properties of goldene nanoribbons
Materials Science.summary: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold. Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Our findings demonstrate that the electronic structure of these nanoribbons depends strongly on both edge chirality and ribbon width. Depending on the boundary configuration, the systems can exhibit semiconducting behavior with electronic band gaps of approximately 0.77 eV and 0.04 eV, or retain metallic characteristics. Additionally, the edge regions act as electronically active sites that may significantly enhance chemical reactivity relative to the central regions. As the ribbon width increases, the metallic characteristics of the infinite goldene sheet are progressively recovered, while the influence of quantum confinement and edge effects on the central region diminishes. These results provide important insights into tailoring the physical properties of goldene through lateral confinement, highlighting its potential for applications in nanoscale field-effect transistors, spintronic devices, and catalysis.

Materials Science.title: Compact representation of strongly correlated Green's functions: the MOR+EC way to explore phase space
Materials Science.summary: Repeated evaluation of the single-particle Green's function (GF) across parameter space is a recurring bottleneck in many-body methods, limiting the resolution at which phase boundaries may be probed and the frequency resolution of computed spectra. We introduce MOR+EC, a framework that constructs reusable reduced-order models for computing single-particle Green's functions by combining eigenvector continuation (EC) for parameter space exploration and model order reduction (MOR) for extrapolation in frequency space. Contrary to conventional parameterized MOR, we construct these reduced-order models with a parameter-independent resolvent, further reducing the number of required full-space evaluations. Benchmarking against exact diagonalization as the impurity solver for our example case of DMFT calculations for single- and two-band models, MOR+EC reproduces the DMFT-converged impurity GF to an average relative error below $10^{-3}$, with a median wall-time speedup of $9.5$-$92\times$. This accuracy and efficiency together resolve a fine-grained scan of the impurity occupation as doping is tuned and produce a high-resolution phase diagram of an orbital-selective Mott transition. The reduced-order model also reproduces real- and imaginary-frequency spectra at no additional cost in full-space evaluations. This framework applies broadly to GF-based methods requiring repeated parametric evaluation and high resolution of the frequency axis.
